The renderer half registers through two optional chains on the sole unsaved-work perimeter for the window. If that channel is ever absent, through preload drift or a stubbed window, the renderer registers nothing, the main process timeout fires and closes anyway, taking every unsaved document. The counter-example is in this same repo: the aeon removal loop handles an absent delete channel explicitly and names it.

title: A file the editor could not stat was reported to the author as deleted from under them, because any stat failure entered the conflict table as absence.
detail: THE SWEEP POINTED ONE LAYER TOO LOW. It attributed a fourth conflict cause to save-guard.ts, which distinguishes three and says so in its own comment table. The fourth entered above it: currentMtime was `catch { return null }` under a comment reading "missing (ENOENT) or otherwise unstattable -> treated as absent". Verified at master 3c198edb before ratifying. So a permissions failure, a symlink loop or an IO error on stat became absence, and absence in that table means deleted externally, which is what the author was told. Fixed with a three-state sentinel on the input. Recorded as its own row because the fix belongs to a different file from the row that found it, and because a consumer of a conflation is not its source.

title: The same unsatisfiable Save existed for sprites: the dirty count included documents the saver would not write.
detail: A third instance of the class, found by the agent building the mechanism for the composer case and then asking where else the shape held, rather than by anything in the packet. The dirty count counted every dirty sprite document while the saver wrote only the saveable ones, so a dirty aeon or new sprite offered a Save that could not succeed. An existing test already constructed exactly that state and answered discard, which is why no row was red. Fixed with the same three-way state.

title: Two more domains are assumed savable while their savers only work with a resident project, and nobody has reproduced the gap.
detail: A FOURTH instance of the unsatisfiable-Save class, deliberately NOT fixed, and the reasoning is worth keeping. The agent found no reproduction of a dirty level or editor store with no resident project, and declined to tighten the guard on an unreproduced case because that would drop Save in states the guard is right about today. The assumption, the missing reproduction and the exact line to change are written at the site rather than only here. Closing this row needs a reproduction first, not a fix first.

title: A third door tells the caller to save first, which is exactly the advice that cannot be followed in the case it fires on.
detail: Found while fixing the other two doors. Its refusal says to save first, and the whole point of the fixed rows is that saving is impossible for some documents, so this is the misleading sentence surviving in the one surface the parcel did not cover. The agent judged it a one-line change and left it deliberately, because it sat outside its two rows and it would have shipped a behaviour change with no test. Correct call, and the row exists so it is not lost.

title: An unreadable sprite art file renders as an object that is simply missing, with no notice of any kind.
detail: Surfaced by the parcel that made the underlying read report its real cause. The sprite cache wraps the build in a catch returning null, so the improved error is thrown into a void: the author sees an absent object and is told nothing. The agent fixed the thrown error and explicitly did NOT claim it became visible, which is the honest half. Booked so the invisible half is somebody row rather than a sentence in a report.

title: 170 test harnesses exist and none is run by the test suite, the landing script, or CI; there is no CI.
detail: Verified against the literal test and land script bodies. No .github tracked or on disk; gh run list returns zero runs while authenticated. An intermediate controller count of 5 reachable was a substring artifact and is withdrawn; the figure is zero. PARKED 2026-09-08 BY THE OWNER, decision d-35: he chose to build the map's coverage and leave these two. They are not fixed, not refuted and not forgotten; they are set aside with a named reason, which the console counts separately from both done and left. Unpark on his word. The reasoning he ruled on: neither ships wrong output to an author, which is the test his cut-the-ceremony ruling sets for instrument work.

title: 24 CDP harnesses attach to whatever page holds their port instead of refusing, so a failed launch reads a stranger's screen back as a measurement.
detail: 155 files carry a PORT default across 75 distinct ports; 134 of 156 carry a portFree preflight. The 24 without one attach via list.find(t => t.type === 'page' && t.webSocketDebuggerUrl) with no check that the page belongs to the child they spawned. Controller re-derived the count independently after a false zero from zsh word-splitting. PARKED 2026-09-08 BY THE OWNER, decision d-35: he chose to build the map's coverage and leave these two. They are not fixed, not refuted and not forgotten; they are set aside with a named reason, which the console counts separately from both done and left. Unpark on his word. The reasoning he ruled on: neither ships wrong output to an author, which is the test his cut-the-ceremony ruling sets for instrument work.

title: A save staleness guard only runs when the caller passes an optional argument; omitting it silently restores the bug the guard was written against.
detail: classic-save.ts:101 declares gen?: DomainGen and the guard reads if (atGen && ...). One producer passes it today. Controller-verified.

title: A second save staleness guard is skipped when its optional argument is omitted, and it also suppresses the warning toast.
detail: atGen?: number at canvasStore.ts:175 with `atGen !== undefined && ...` at :330: absent means stale=false, the doc clears AND returns true, so canvas-save.ts:125 suppresses the warning too. One producer today (canvas-save.ts:64). Sibling of the booked SAVE-GEN-OPTIONAL; the classic one is the more arming of the two because its `collect` is an injectable parameter, so a second producer needs no new call site.

title: Appending a block through the art path leaves an interior range of the collision index zero-filled.
detail: out.set(src) covers only src.length (410 for GHZ) and the append loop writes from doc.blocks.length (439) up, so 410-438 stay zero. collision-write.ts:694 says so in its own words. The shrink direction and the collision door are both closed; this is the open half of the prior packet's U6.

title: Only half of the collision-index overhang defect was closed; the art path still zero-fills.
detail: Shrink direction closed in s1-io.ts (replacing a gate that was literally bytesEqual(x.slice().slice(), x), true for every input); collision door closed at 4de2e617. Tracked open as COLIND-ART-PATH-ZEROFILL.

title: A background stroke on the act default committed after an act switch lands on the new act's plane, indexed by the old act's tiles.
detail: endBgStroke passes bgRef and a freshly read level. history.ts:71-74 resolves a library bgRef by id, which is safe across a switch, but the bgRef===null branch falls back to level.act.bgLayout. The project reasoned this through for UNDO timing (its docblock says so) and never applied it to COMMIT timing. MapViewport.tsx:2631 also mixes stale entries with a freshly read activeSectionIndex in one command. RAISED from medium to high at the fix, on measurement rather than on the fixer's word: an earlier parcel had narrowed this row to a misfiled undo entry, and that narrowing counted COMMAND TYPES when the discriminator is a field inside one of them. The act default carries a null reference, which resolveBgLayout resolves to the ACTIVE act's plane at commit time (verified by the controller at 611412b9), and the paint re-resolves per pixel, so every mousemove after an act switch wrote into the new act's plane with no command at all. That is live document corruption outside undo, which is the same tier as the critical this row was mistaken for a lesser cousin of.

title: The map's wheel handler calls preventDefault in a passive React listener, so it never suppresses the browser's own zoom, and the repo already ruled on this elsewhere.
detail: React 19 registers root wheel listeners as passive. use-anchored-zoom.ts:11-12 states the rule and does it correctly with a native non-passive listener; MapViewport uses neither that helper nor a native listener, and handleWheel never gates on ctrlKey.

title: The classic map has the same wheel defect and worse: it never tries to suppress the window zoom at all, so nothing looks wrong in the code.
detail: Found by the parcel that fixed the aeon map surface, and left there deliberately because that parcel owned only its own file. The classic map wheel handler is a passive React prop that zooms the classic map and never calls preventDefault, so a modifier wheel over it zooms the map AND the application window. Worse than the row just fixed in one specific way: the fixed one had a dead call that a reader could notice, and this one has no call at all, so there is nothing in the source to catch the eye. The convention to apply is now established next door, cited in the packet: a native non-passive listener attached through the helper whose docblock names the empty-dependency null-ref trap. One hook.

title: Landing verification and agent work compete for one machine, and several census rows time out under that load and look exactly like real failures.
detail: Measured tonight, three separate incidents inside an hour. Two different exhaustive-census rows timed out at the 5s default while a subagent was building concurrently: one runs in 1.8s idle and hit 6.0s loaded, the other runs in 1.0s idle and exceeded 5.0s loaded, roughly a threefold and fivefold inflation. BOTH PRESENTED AS GENUINE REDS -- a named row, a failing file, a merge sitting on the tree -- and the second one was a test written the same evening, so "it was always flaky" was not available as an explanation either. I separated the causes rather than re-running until green: the merge in flight touched only files the failing test does not import, and each row passed immediately when given room. THE REAL DEFECT IS SEQUENCING, NOT THE LIMITS. Timeouts here are calibrated for an idle box while the box is routinely running a full suite and a building agent at once, so the honest fix is not to raise limits one row at a time as they bite -- that is adjusting the instrument to suit a busy machine, and it would eventually license raising every census row. I raised exactly ONE, the row whose own work left under threefold headroom, with the derivation and a refusal-to-raise-again written at the site, and declined the second. Candidate fixes for whoever takes this: run the landing suite when no agent is building, or give census rows a limit derived from a measured baseline rather than the global default, or have the suite refuse to grade a timeout while a build is detected. Booked rather than fixed because choosing between those is a real design call and it is not a defect that ships wrong output to an author.

title: The 3,915-line map surface the user draws on is imported by no test, and three standing fixes live inside it.
detail: NARROWED, and HALF THE ORIGINAL CLAIM IS REFUTED. This row said no test loads the component, on two enumerations that agreed. Measured by planting a top-level throw in MapViewport.tsx and running the suite: FOUR test files already load it, transitively, because src/renderer/workspace/facet-registry.ts:18 imports it and they import that registry. They are workspace/__tests__/facet-modules, workspace/__tests__/facet-visibility, providers/__tests__/map-status-classic and workspace/__tests__/classic-art-dock. Both enumerations looked for a DIRECT import from a test file and neither followed the transitive edge, so the row's stated method could not have found this. A fifth file went red in the full poison run and is NOT one of them: test/formats/bg-override-section-ceiling.test.ts passes under the same poison in a narrow run, so that was a load-sensitive flake and taking the full run at face value would have published a false census. WHAT WAS TRUE, and it is the half that mattered: the module was evaluated and the COMPONENT WAS NEVER CALLED, so an import-time error was caught and nothing inside the function body was. NOW: the component RUNS in the node suite, with no jsdom and no new dependency. src/test/render-hooked.ts (which already existed for NumberField) gained useSyncExternalStore, which is what zustand reaches through, and unmount(), which runs the effect cleanups; src/test/window-stub.ts supplies the four browser globals its effects use; src/test/element-stub.ts performs the ref commit React never does here, so the component's own screenToWorld maps a client coordinate to a world one. 25 rows in src/renderer/components/__tests__/map-viewport-mounted.test.ts drive the real handlers over the real stores and read the real undo stack. WHAT REMAINS, so this is not read as closed: the file is 4,357 lines and is NOT thin; these rows cover the four fixes landed on 2026-09-08 and the pointer, key, unmount and wheel paths they sit on, not the surface evenly. Nothing paints, nothing lays out, no event propagates, and the rect a row declares is not one a browser measured, so every claim that depends on a pixel or on layout is still foreground only. The BG stroke half of BG-STROKE-WRONG-ACT is still held by the source scan in src/renderer/components/__tests__/map-surface-listeners.test.ts and not behaviourally: reaching paintBgTile needs a loaded BG plane that this fixture does not build. And the empty dep list on the unmount effect is caught ONLY by that scan, measured: changing it to [finishGesture] leaves all 25 behavioural rows green. Scan and behaviour are covering different things here and both are load bearing.

title: A collision audit indexes past the end of its input and folds the resulting nothing into no-crossover, so it under-reports, which is the direction that hides.
detail: The scan never consults either plane's length and indexes bare; the decoder maps undefined to none, so out-of-range is indistinguishable from a genuine absence. Its sibling in the same file does guard and does report the count it examined. The same module argues that an illegal value must not fold into none because its presence is a defect somebody must see, then folds undefined into none fifteen lines later. Bounded honestly: no production caller — all six call sites are tests passing equal-length planes, so no existing sample could have failed. Sits inside the never-audited collision row. LOCATION CORRECTED AT THE FIX, measured not argued: auditCrossovers, which the row and my brief both named, reads past NO end (proved with a recording proxy over lengths 1-40 by strides 1-12 by three fills plus every unequal-length pair). The past-end read is in the EXPORTED scanCancellingRuns, whose length was a caller's claim nothing checked; verified by the controller at 611412b9. Two further defects on the same surface were worse than the row: a self-mark past plane B's end returned severity ok WITH A NULL MESSAGE, a clean bill for a document aeon's bake hard-errors on, and the did-we-scan flag was set from the stride alone so a scan walking zero rows claimed to have run.

title: The collision grid an agent reads labels column 100 identically to column 0, on the surface whose stated purpose is that agents read data rather than screenshots.
detail: Controller-reproduced with the source expressions: the tens row is floor((x+c)/10) % 10 and prints a space for 0, so x=100 and x=0 emit byte-identical rulers while x=120 reads as 20. Sections are 128 cells wide and validation.ts accepts any x with x+w <= 128. Row labels are correct; only the column axis caps. The single ruler test uses x=9,w=3 — the one case a two-digit ruler gets right, so it could not have failed. Second defect fixed on the same surface: the tool promised a legend and the legend constant was exported and read by NOTHING, so every reply carried the picture and no key. Ruler width is now derived from the digit count of the largest label, the rule the row axis already used, so two-digit windows render byte-identically as before.

title: Two collision paint functions have no live callers while their docblocks name them as the agent tool's core in the present tense, and neither can express a crossover span.
detail: Every non-test hit is a comment. The live agent path is agent-handler.ts:491/497 via the both-planes functions; the human path goes through buildBothPlanesEntries directly. The consequence is not cosmetic: collisionRectCells is called with no span argument so it always defaults to 'cell', a width that layer-transition.ts:226-234 proves always nets to nothing for a two-way pair, so a reader modelling the tool from the function its own docblock names gets the span semantics backwards.

title: A composer document with unsaved strokes is closed with an info toast and no confirmation.
detail: Three sites call useArtStore.getState().closeDocument() directly, bypassing closeDocumentGuarded. The strokes live only in artStore.open.doc and no registered saver can write them. Mitigating: the target tile genuinely no longer exists, so there is nowhere to save to — which is an argument for confirming, not for closing silently.

title: The only guard between a user and the destruction of a composer drawing has ten call sites, no test at all, and uses the one dialog mechanism the repo forbids.
detail: Ten production call sites, zero test references. These are the only two window.confirm calls in src; every other destructive door goes through the app's own confirm dialog under the rule that a destructive button is never the one focused on open, and another guard's source says explicitly that a second dialog mechanism must not exist. window.confirm focuses its destroy arm by default. Given the unsatisfiable-save finding above, this is the guard standing between a user and the only way that document class can leave the app: destruction. PROVEN VACUOUS BEFORE THE FIX: both guard bodies reduced to their unconditional halves and the whole suite came back byte-identical to baseline, green. A SECOND plant then came back green too and not for a matcher reason: nothing asserted the facet CALLS the door, so a guard can be fully tested and still bypassed by its caller, which forced a caller gate. Also measured: three of the ten call sites cannot reach the destroying path at all, because their handlers are wired only to launcher buttons the app renders only when nothing is open.

title: The helper that exists to stop an unusable Save being offered was itself offering one, for a drawing whose chunk had left the library.
detail: Found by the parcel closing the discard guard. composerSaveState answered savable for a chunk document whose chunk had been removed, while the saver answers that same state by writing nothing and saying so. That is the inert-primary-button defect the helper was written to prevent, occurring inside the helper, and it reached two other doors that consume it. It is the fourth early return that was missed when the helper was derived from the saver, which is the shape to expect whenever a predicate is derived from a procedure by reading it: the reader stops at the returns they noticed.

title: Landing verification and agent work share one machine, and a TIMEOUT under that load is indistinguishable from a real failure; an assertion never is.
detail: Measured tonight, three separate incidents inside an hour. Two different exhaustive-census rows timed out at the 5s default while a subagent was building concurrently: one runs in 1.8s idle and hit 6.0s loaded, the other runs in 1.0s idle and exceeded 5.0s loaded, roughly a threefold and fivefold inflation. BOTH PRESENTED AS GENUINE REDS -- a named row, a failing file, a merge sitting on the tree -- and the second one was a test written the same evening, so "it was always flaky" was not available as an explanation either. I separated the causes rather than re-running until green: the merge in flight touched only files the failing test does not import, and each row passed immediately when given room. THE REAL DEFECT IS SEQUENCING, NOT THE LIMITS. Timeouts here are calibrated for an idle box while the box is routinely running a full suite and a building agent at once, so the honest fix is not to raise limits one row at a time as they bite -- that is adjusting the instrument to suit a busy machine, and it would eventually license raising every census row. I raised exactly ONE, the row whose own work left under threefold headroom, with the derivation and a refusal-to-raise-again written at the site, and declined the second. Candidate fixes for whoever takes this: run the landing suite when no agent is building, or give census rows a limit derived from a measured baseline rather than the global default, or have the suite refuse to grade a timeout while a build is detected. Booked rather than fixed because choosing between those is a real design call and it is not a defect that ships wrong output to an author. ⚠ SHARPENED 2026-09-09 by oracle, and my original wording was too broad in the dangerous direction. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE FAILURE MODE, NOT THE LOAD. A timeout or a would-block is load-manufactured until proven otherwise. A FAILED ASSERTION IS NOT LOAD-SENSITIVE AND STAYS A FINDING whatever the box was doing. Oracle has the converse booked twice, on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04: a row that failed only under load was written off as a flake and was a genuine defect with a narrow timing window, both times. So my rule as first written -- treat a red on a loaded box with suspicion -- would have licensed exactly the mistake they made twice, because load is the condition that OPENS a narrow window rather than the condition that fakes one. The correct pair of rules: check the load before believing a TIMEOUT, and never let load excuse an ASSERTION. Both of tonight's false reds here were timeouts, which is why the original reasoning happened to reach the right answer for the wrong reason.

title: A toast tells the author their background files are not in the checkout, for a file that is present and truncated.
detail: The unresolved flag has two producers: a read failure, and a layout file that IS present but shorter than one row. The comment three lines above the second push says so in its own words, calling it a body that is present and says nothing. Three sibling messages have the same shape, including one that says nothing references those tiles in precisely the case where a silent catch means the opposite.

title: An unreadable sprite drew the same hex-id box an unlinked object draws, so a real failure was camouflaged as the ordinary resting state.
detail: Surfaced by the parcel that made the underlying read report its real cause. The sprite cache wraps the build in a catch returning null, so the improved error is thrown into a void: the author sees an absent object and is told nothing. The agent fixed the thrown error and explicitly did NOT claim it became visible, which is the honest half. Booked so the invisible half is somebody row rather than a sentence in a report. SYMPTOM CORRECTED AT THE FIX and the correction is better than the row: the object is NOT invisible. The overlay falls back to a hex-id box on a null sprite, verified by the controller at c0b899c2 where the suite's own row is titled 'fallback hex-box objects (no sprite) are editor chrome'. Most of the S1 object table draws that box normally, so a genuine read failure was indistinguishable from the resting state rather than from nothing. That is worse than invisible, because an author has no reason to look, and it is why the fix distinguishes a thrown failure from an ordinary miss and names which objects failed rather than merely surfacing an error.

title: A third door tells the caller to save first, which is exactly the advice that cannot be followed in the case it fires on.
detail: Found while fixing the other two doors. Its refusal says to save first, and the whole point of the fixed rows is that saving is impossible for some documents, so this is the misleading sentence surviving in the one surface the parcel did not cover. The agent judged it a one-line change and left it deliberately, because it sat outside its two rows and it would have shipped a behaviour change with no test. Correct call, and the row exists so it is not lost.

title: The classic map has the same wheel defect and worse: it never tries to suppress the window zoom at all, so nothing looks wrong in the code.
detail: Found by the parcel that fixed the aeon map surface, and left there deliberately because that parcel owned only its own file. The classic map wheel handler is a passive React prop that zooms the classic map and never calls preventDefault, so a modifier wheel over it zooms the map AND the application window. Worse than the row just fixed in one specific way: the fixed one had a dead call that a reader could notice, and this one has no call at all, so there is nothing in the source to catch the eye. The convention to apply is now established next door, cited in the packet: a native non-passive listener attached through the helper whose docblock names the empty-dependency null-ref trap. One hook.

title: The shared browser-driving helper fails from a worktree every time, because the page collects the long-running open promise while the call waits on it.
detail: Found by the parcel that measured the classic wheel fix. The shared open helper failed three runs of three with the page reporting that the promise was collected, before printing anything, because Chromium collects the long-running open promise while the evaluation awaits it. The agent worked around it inline by attaching a continuation before awaiting, held three of three, and deliberately did NOT fix the shared helper: seventeen importers, outside its rows. Recorded in its own harness header as well as here. This matters more than a flaky helper usually would, because a harness is how anything visual gets proven in this repo and the failure happens before any output, so a session that hits it sees a harness that produced nothing rather than a helper that broke.

title: The main-process binary read applies no path guard at all, so the only thing stopping an escaping path is a check on one of its callers.
detail: Surfaced by the parcel that closed the WRITE twin, and verified by the controller at master 4cf66084: readBinaryFile is `resolve(basePath, relativePath)` then `readFile`, with no isRelPathSafe. Five of the seven exports in that file guard; this one and listProjectFiles (which takes no project-relative argument) do not. Today the only barrier is a renderer-side check at classic-file-access.ts:27, which guards one caller rather than the channel. Left OPEN and deliberately not raised higher because the reachability question is UNENUMERATED: nobody has yet listed which callers can be fed an author-controlled or file-controlled relative path, and that enumeration is what decides the severity. The parcel added a notice row asserting the current unguarded state, so adding a guard becomes a deliberate act rather than a surprise, and so this row cannot be closed by accident. SEVERITY RAISED medium to HIGH at the fix, by the enumeration the row itself said was missing. It is not a hypothetical caller: projectDataRoot derives a path PREFIX from dataPath in the project's own project.json, and dataRootOfPath returns everything up to and including a /data/ segment verbatim (verified by the controller at 1a611de8: it is a slice), so a config saying ../../data/foo yields that prefix, under roughly ten call sites. Two further sites take a whole path segment out of project files. The write channel already refused every one of those strings, which is this repo's own precedent that the value is untrusted. The legacy absolute-path exception that had kept the guard out turned out to have exactly one holder, three lines in one importer, moved to the idiom every other outside-the-project read already used.

title: The directory listing primitives answer the same value for an empty directory and one they could not read, so two more probe sites cannot be fixed yet.
detail: TAGGED by the agent and left open deliberately, with the reasoning verified: two effects sites (scene and preset) carry the identical blind-probe line as the three fixed today, but they probe a DIRECTORY, and flipping them buys nothing while listDir, fileMtime and readManyFiles all swallow a failure into the same value an empty or absent directory gives. So the fix is the listing gaining a third answer first, exactly as pathExists became probePath. Booked as one row rather than three because the two call sites cannot move until the primitive does. FIXED, and a THIRD consumer was found that the row did not name and that matters more than the two it did: the canvas name lister feeds the collision check stopping a new canvas overwriting an existing one, so while the listing swallowed, an unreadable directory answered 'there are no canvases' and every name passed. That file already wrapped the call in a catch that refuses with a message, A BRANCH NOTHING COULD REACH because nothing could throw. A guard written for a failure its dependency cannot express is the quietest kind of dead code, because it reads as protection.

title: When the editor refuses a typed value, the explanation is more than twice as tall as the box it is painted in.
detail: 280px of content in a 129px scroller, over the app's own EW-LAYER-CARD-SCROLLER bar, on every refusal on that surface. Composed at refusal time by NumberField, so no static census could see it. Still 280-in-129 at 1680x2200, so not a small-window artifact. Found by the row-remap harness parcel and left red on purpose as harness row [5b2]. FIXED and measured both ways: 280px in a 129px box before, 119px after, and the on-screen check left red on purpose goes 26/27 to 27/27. A LOOK CHOICE IS LEFT WITH THE OWNER and is recorded here so it is not lost: the already-moved finding stays on screen, which is what makes the result 119 against a 129 FLOOR, under the bar with less than one wrapped line of slack, so a longer number pair could push it back over. Folding it buys about 50px and would hide from an author that their value has already changed, which is the exact defect that clause was added for. The conservative option shipped and the lever is his. Note 129 is the section at its MINIMUM, which is the harness configuration; a normally sized panel has more room.

title: The shared browser-driving helper fails from a worktree every time, because the page collects the long-running open promise while the call waits on it.
detail: Found by the parcel that measured the classic wheel fix. The shared open helper failed three runs of three with the page reporting that the promise was collected, before printing anything, because Chromium collects the long-running open promise while the evaluation awaits it. The agent worked around it inline by attaching a continuation before awaiting, held three of three, and deliberately did NOT fix the shared helper: seventeen importers, outside its rows. Recorded in its own harness header as well as here. This matters more than a flaky helper usually would, because a harness is how anything visual gets proven in this repo and the failure happens before any output, so a session that hits it sees a harness that produced nothing rather than a helper that broke. FIXED in the shared module, three runs of three red before and green after, with the importer question answered by RUNNING rather than asserting: 19 files import it, 16 take the repaired function, the 3 that do not cannot be affected because the diff touches nothing else, and a harness importing the module but not that function was run as a control. THE CONTROLLER'S SEQUENCING CLAIM WAS WRONG: I put this first because I believed it blocked the overflow row; verified afterwards that the row-remap harness does not import this module at all and opens its own way. Also: my 'around seventeen importers' and the helper's own docblock figures of 17 and 12 were all wrong (19/16/15), and both typed censuses were REMOVED rather than corrected, with a one-line derivation in their place, because a hand-maintained count will be wrong again.

title: A header states path-escape safety as an app-wide invariant while the guard is applied at seven of eight handlers, and only one of thirty callers re-checks.
detail: readBinaryFile takes an absolute path deliberately, a designed capability for sheet import reachable only through the loopback-guarded MCP route, and the module says so at file-io.ts:12-14, making this says-unread rather than silent. NOT a vulnerability claim. The finding is the gap between the header sentence and the population: of 30 readBinaryFile call sites exactly one re-checks, and four pass an absolute path with an empty rel operand, one of which passes empty as the BASE path so it resolves against the main process cwd. RE-DERIVED AT THE FIX, and one half of the claim HAS BECOME TRUE. 'Seven of eight handlers' is now eight of eight, partly because the binary read gained its guard in the previous parcel and partly because the old count included an export with NO PATH ARGUMENT that was never in the population. 'One of thirty callers' is one file of eight and five call sites of thirty-six, and is no longer a gap: main refuses whatever arrives, so the renderer check is defence in depth. The header now states where the claim is held, what checks it, and the greps to re-derive it. The agent also closed a SEAM nothing covered: every existing row proves a primitive guards, so a handler doing its own filesystem work would ship green past all of them; the new row derives the channel population from the handler file's own text and classifies every channel, proven by rewriting one handler to read the file itself.

title: A collision harness fails its first row from an agent workspace, and it is a failed assertion rather than a timeout, so it is a real finding.
detail: Surfaced by the parcel that repaired the shared browser-driving helper. It is red on its swatch-arming clause. Recorded with its MODE stated because that is what decides how to read it: a timeout on a busy box is load-manufactured until proven otherwise, but an ASSERTION is not load-sensitive and stays a finding whatever the machine was doing. The same output line reports the open half green (project opened, act ready, panel mounted), so it is not the helper change. NO BEFORE-FIGURE IS OBTAINABLE from a worktree, because before the helper fix the harness never reached row one, which is why this could not have been found earlier.

title: Two more refusals on the same panel take the same long tail into the same small box and neither has been measured.
detail: Named by the parcel that fixed the third one, deliberately unmeasured and unchanged rather than assumed to be broken or assumed to be fine. Both are still single-paragraph hints and both receive the same drift tail in the same box that overflowed. Booked at low because it is the same defect with a known repair already applied next door, so the cost is measuring rather than designing.

title: The ship-silent control tells an author the whole act will boot with its background animation off, and with more than one animation that is false.
detail: Found by aeon correcting THEMSELVES on 2026-09-09: the key is per band, and only when EVERY band carries it does the act boot silent; one marked plus one live band boots ON. Two author-facing strings state the act-level effect: the option label 'ships silent (the act boots with BG animation off)' and the lead sentence 'so the act boots with BG animation OFF in every ROM, RELEASE INCLUDED'. So on the one control whose entire purpose is what SHIPS, the editor tells an author their act will be silent when it will not. HIGH rather than medium because it is a false statement about shipped behaviour rather than a confusing one, and because the author cannot discover it from the editor: nothing looks different either way, which the copy itself says. WHERE THE ERROR ENTERED IS VISIBLE: our own codec comment says 'a SINGLE-BAND act boots with BG animation off', correctly quantified. The UI string dropped the qualifier and nothing compared the two, which is why a rule that only checks strings against a gate would not have caught it. Aeon's wording to use: 'this band does not ship'.

title: Our vendored contract describes a build refusal that our own amendment two fields away says stopped raising three days ago.
detail: Surfaced while checking aeon's correction. BGANIM_VIEW_DERIVED_PERIOD_PX's authorities still read 'the refusal in views_emitted: raise AssertionError', while the same file's amendment dated 2026-09-06 against aeon 364b7bce is headed 'THE TWO default_off OBLIGATIONS STOPPED BEING OBLIGATIONS. Both were AssertionErrors and NEITHER RAISES ANY MORE'. Both sentences are in one document and they contradict each other. This is the stale-document defect aeon just reported on their side, on ours, inside the file whose entire job is to be current: an amendment records that a thing changed and the entry it changed is left describing the old world, because appending is cheap and re-reading the entry you are amending is not enforced. Worth a general rule if it recurs: an amendment should be required to name the fields it invalidates.

title: Every test of the window-close guard begins after the platform event that has to arrive, so none of them can witness that it does.
detail: Oracle's rule, applied to our tree on 2026-09-09 and confirmed here: WHEN A FEATURE DEPENDS ON A PLATFORM EVENT, A TEST THAT STARTS FROM THE EVENT'S PAYLOAD CANNOT WITNESS THE EVENT. Their drag-and-drop was correct code that was never called, and every test passed because each one began one step after the step that never happened. Ours is the same shape on the perimeter that matters most: the window close guard is the only thing between a stray click and every unsaved document, and the seam test landed tonight drives the real state machine, the real registration, the real confirmation and the real channel constants over a fake bus, all of which begins AFTER Electron's close event. The agent that wrote it named the gap in its own report rather than hiding it (its words: the Electron inch, that preventDefault suspends a real close and the later close re-raises the event the let-through path exists for, needs a real window). Booked because a tag in a report is not a row and does not survive the session. NOT a claim that the guard is broken: the payload-shaped test is the natural one to write, it looks complete, and it is exactly the shape that survives the capability being absent, which is why the row exists rather than a fix. Closing it needs a real window, so it is foreground work. Note our harnesses pin the browser engine to X11, so they share the blind spot by construction; oracle measured the same thing on their side, where their only headless harness strips the session variables and forces Xvfb.

title: The crossover audit truncates to the shorter plane and reports ok for an absent one, with no mismatch signal.
detail: Math.min over the two plane lengths, an early return of zero cells for a null plane, and a severity function that never consults the cell count. Its sibling resolvePlaneWords reports a length fault loudly; this one is silent. Not reachable from today's loader, and reported because this audit is the only place a self-mark is noticed anywhere. CLOSED ALREADY TRUE, BY MEASUREMENT AND WITH NO DIFF. fixedAt names the collision merge that actually closed it the night before, not the parcel that discovered it was closed, because a fix is anchored by the commit carrying the code. Proven with 31 green rows naming each of this row's three claims, and the agent then checked the layer the row does not mention: all three consumers carry the new signal, one of them gated on the note being non-null rather than on severity. The row's third clause is still literally true and is a written ruling rather than a residue. Recorded as its own outcome class because a parcel that closes a row with evidence and no change is a better result than one that makes true a thing already true, and no coverage number distinguishes them.

title: A dirty composer document shows no tab dot and does not enable Save, and one open path can become unexitable except by discarding.
detail: currentDirtySnapshot has no artDirty field though currentOpenDirtySnapshot does. No data is lost — the close and open guards both use the other snapshot. Second-order: with only artDirty set, Save-and-open runs the savers, re-snapshots still dirty and aborts forever, and openBlockedMessage names only the canvas case. PARTLY MOVED before it was worked: the dangerous clause closed the night before and its stated symptom is now false, and 'does not enable Save' had become three different answers depending on which Save, one of which is a deliberate documented ruling rather than a defect. What held was the tab dot, and that is what was fixed. ⚠ THE ONE-LINE FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN A REGRESSION: both level savers registered their dirty predicate as the same function that decides the dot, and a save runs exactly when it answers true, so teaching the dot about the composer without splitting the rule would have enabled the save chord over composer-only dirt, run a saver that does not write the composer, and left the dot standing. Split into one rule for save routing and one for display, measured both ways.

title: An adapter interface declares an optional member with no producer and no consumer anywhere.
detail: heightmapsRot appears on exactly one line in the whole tree, its own declaration; the sole caller omits it. Harmless today because nothing reads it; the trap is that a future consumer gets undefined from the only producer with no type error and no test. DELETED on a whole-tree census by producer, consumer and copier rather than by the name in its own module, which is the enumeration this repo has got wrong before. The red-first is the row's own trap reproduced rather than a planted one: consumers written against the declarations typecheck CLEAN while they exist and fail once they are gone, which is what dead means here and is not something a grep for the name shows.

title: An IPC channel constant is declared and never registered, exposed or used.
detail: OPEN_PROJECT appears only in its own declaration; the control constant returns four references. DELETED on a whole-tree census by producer, consumer and copier rather than by the name in its own module, which is the enumeration this repo has got wrong before. The red-first is the row's own trap reproduced rather than a planted one: consumers written against the declarations typecheck CLEAN while they exist and fail once they are gone, which is what dead means here and is not something a grep for the name shows.

title: Two more domains are assumed savable while their savers only work with a resident project, and nobody has reproduced the gap.
detail: A FOURTH instance of the unsatisfiable-Save class, deliberately NOT fixed, and the reasoning is worth keeping. The agent found no reproduction of a dirty level or editor store with no resident project, and declined to tighten the guard on an unreproduced case because that would drop Save in states the guard is right about today. The assumption, the missing reproduction and the exact line to change are written at the site rather than only here. Closing this row needs a reproduction first, not a fix first. ⚠ LEFT OPEN A SECOND TIME, BY A DIFFERENT AGENT ON A DIFFERENT ROUTE, AND THE THREE SENTENCES HOLDING IT OPEN DID NOT SURVIVE CHECKING. One was true on a STRONGER basis than stated (the classic dirty flag implies the classic engine is open by construction, which also covers a race the cited reset does not). One named two of the nine production sites, though the conclusion survives on the wider basis that all nine mount on one branch. And the third, that tightening would drop the Save button in states the guard is right about today, HAS NO EXAMPLE: the classic saver's own predicate never consults the flag at all. That third sentence is precisely what a future reader would have quoted as the reason not to act, so it is worse than no justification: a wrong reason for a correct decision is durable and persuasive. The code is unchanged on the honest narrower reason, that there is nothing to verify a change against, and the site now says that instead. The state IS constructible through the debug surface, just not by a user, which is named at the site.

title: The ship-silent control tells an author the whole act will boot with its background animation off, and with more than one animation that is false.
detail: Found by aeon correcting THEMSELVES on 2026-09-09: the key is per band, and only when EVERY band carries it does the act boot silent; one marked plus one live band boots ON. Two author-facing strings state the act-level effect: the option label 'ships silent (the act boots with BG animation off)' and the lead sentence 'so the act boots with BG animation OFF in every ROM, RELEASE INCLUDED'. So on the one control whose entire purpose is what SHIPS, the editor tells an author their act will be silent when it will not. HIGH rather than medium because it is a false statement about shipped behaviour rather than a confusing one, and because the author cannot discover it from the editor: nothing looks different either way, which the copy itself says. WHERE THE ERROR ENTERED IS VISIBLE: our own codec comment says 'a SINGLE-BAND act boots with BG animation off', correctly quantified. The UI string dropped the qualifier and nothing compared the two, which is why a rule that only checks strings against a gate would not have caught it. Aeon's wording to use: 'this band does not ship'. FIXED, and THREE strings were wrong rather than the two the row named. The third promised the debug view twins unconditionally and is rendered beside the lead without the obligations, so on a mixed act an author read that they get three view twins while the emitter returns zero for that document. AEON'S CORRECTION WAS VERIFIED AGAINST THEIR SOURCE rather than taken from their message, because they had already been wrong about this once: at aeon 22cf8b37 the emitter counts the bands NOT carrying the key and reaches the boots-off case only when none remain, so the act is silent iff EVERY band carries it. Their own comment names the class: the old sentence was true while the key implied a single-band act and became an over-claim once a multi-band act could carry it.

title: Our vendored contract describes a build refusal that our own amendment two fields away says stopped raising three days ago.
detail: Surfaced while checking aeon's correction. BGANIM_VIEW_DERIVED_PERIOD_PX's authorities still read 'the refusal in views_emitted: raise AssertionError', while the same file's amendment dated 2026-09-06 against aeon 364b7bce is headed 'THE TWO default_off OBLIGATIONS STOPPED BEING OBLIGATIONS. Both were AssertionErrors and NEITHER RAISES ANY MORE'. Both sentences are in one document and they contradict each other. This is the stale-document defect aeon just reported on their side, on ours, inside the file whose entire job is to be current: an amendment records that a thing changed and the entry it changed is left describing the old world, because appending is cheap and re-reading the entry you are amending is not enforced. Worth a general rule if it recurs: an amendment should be required to name the fields it invalidates. FIXED, and it was FOUR sentences in THREE places rather than the one entry the row named, with the one I found the least dangerous of them: an invariants entry said aeon RAISES on either failure rather than emitting zero twins, and that a consistent two-band act is refused just as a mixed one is, which is the opposite of current behaviour stated twice in the entry a size model is written against. The new gate derives its expectation from the file's OWN amendment rather than from an agent's reading of aeon, so it survives the next aeon change.

title: The same over-claim existed as CODE, not only as copy: the act-boots-silent predicate asked whether ANY animation carried the setting instead of every one.
detail: Found by the agent fixing the copy, filed by nobody. The predicate used `some` where the behaviour is `every`, which is the identical dropped quantifier in machine-readable form and wrong on exactly the mixed act the strings were wrong about. IT HAD NO CONSUMER TODAY, so nothing shipped wrong from it, and that is why it matters: fixing only the strings would have left the falsehood one accessor away from being true again. Its own docblock JUSTIFIED the choice as temporary and pointed at a decoupling fix as the thing that would separate the two quantifiers. That fix landed 2026-09-06 and the predicate was never revisited. A comment that defers to a future change is a promise nothing keeps once the change lands, and it reads as considered rather than as outstanding. Booked HIGH to match its sibling because it is the same defect in the more durable medium.

title: Author-facing strings asserting behaviour of the engine are policed by nothing unless they contain a number, and one such claim is typed twice by two authors with no arbiter.
detail: The constants gate covers integers with an in-scope arbiter and says so; the guide-text gate is markdown only. So a non-numeric behavioural claim about another repo in a TSX string has no instrument. One claim about the engine flat-pathing a live shift appears twice, independently typed. Another asserts the ABSENCE of a guard in another repo. A third says the engine cannot emit this yet, with no date, owner or retiring event. 40-plus such strings exist in that one file; which are derived from a pinned contract versus hand-typed was not censused, and that split is the actual question. The instrument already exists in-repo: one module parses its claim out of the vendored document and throws at load when it moves. GATE BUILT AND ASSERTED TO CATCH TONIGHT'S HIGH: three permanent control rows read the three PRE-FIX sentences out of git at b6660f23 and require the finished predicate to flag all three, a fourth requires it to pass the repaired ones, and the real sentence was also planted on disk and the census row failed naming the file and the clause. THE ROW'S FRAMING WAS WRONG AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE: it asked for the derived-versus-hand-typed split as the real question, and that split does not exist. 32 strings assert engine behaviour, 26 interpolate a derived number, and in ALL 32 the behavioural assertion is hand-typed. A number arriving from a real source is exactly what made these look checked.

title: Two more refusals on the same panel take the same long tail into the same small box and neither has been measured.
detail: Named by the parcel that fixed the third one, deliberately unmeasured and unchanged rather than assumed to be broken or assumed to be fine. Both are still single-paragraph hints and both receive the same drift tail in the same box that overflowed. Booked at low because it is the same defect with a known repair already applied next door, so the cost is measuring rather than designing. MEASURED, AND THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG IN THE INVERTING DIRECTION. They are not in 'the same small box': one sits in a list section floored at a minimum height, where a taller block is a paragraph no scroll position shows whole, and the other is in a content section with natural height. So the BIGGER block at 264px is fine and the SMALLER at 215px against a 129px floor was genuinely broken, now 120px. The disclosure alone was not enough: a second measurement read 136 against 129 because the bound was stated twice, once in wire units nothing on screen uses.

title: The map canvas ignores device pixel ratio, so its backing store is truncated to whole pixels and stretched, and hit-testing drifts toward the far edge.
detail: A grep for devicePixelRatio over the file exits 1, a genuine zero with stderr unsuppressed. canvas.width = rect.width truncates because canvas.width is an unsigned long, while the element is styled 100%/100%. screenToWorld divides by zoom with no compensation. On HiDPI the pixel-art surface renders at half resolution. FIXED with the scale derived per draw and never cached, across five ratios each recomputing its own expectation, one of them 1 because even at 1 the old code truncated a fractional rect, and seven hostile readings falling back safely. TAGGED and not closed by this: there is NO PAINT verification, because the node canvas context is a no-op; one row states that bound and fails if the stub ever gains a real transform. Nobody has looked at the map on a high-density display.

title: Warping before the mouse has ever entered the map treats never-hovered as hovered at the top-left corner.
detail: lastMouse is initialised to {x:0,y:0} and F7 warps to screenToWorld of it, so a cold F7 warps to the world point under screen 0,0 instead of refusing. Absent and at-the-corner are the same value. THE ROW UNDERSTATED ITS OWN MECHANISM AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FIX. The value was never a hover position: every write is in the mouse-down path, so a plain move never touched it and the warp went to the last BUTTON PRESS while the feature's own comment said 'wherever the mouse is on the map'. Conflating a subtraction base with a position is what made the origin default undetectable in the first place. The cursor now has its own name and the pan anchor keeps the three-state fix.

title: Four places told an author a piece of engine work had not landed yet, when aeon had ruled it out and cancelled it outright.
detail: In NO ROW: found by the census built for the strings gate, and verified by the controller at aeon d3339973 before ratifying. Four author-facing sites said the left-column strip emission 'has not landed' or 'cannot emit this yet'. Aeon's own source says the opposite in terms: 'SpriteMask is declared, and it is RULED OUT ... The strip emission is cancelled, not pending.' So an author was told to wait for something that is never coming, on a key where the alternative arms are the actual answer. Two of the four also said the declaration 'would be accepted' while the build asserts on it. A COMMENT ELEVEN LINES AWAY HAD IT RIGHT THE WHOLE TIME, which is this repo's recurring shape: the correct version present in the same file and never compared. Booked high to match the class it belongs to. The agent's first matcher for this came back GREEN over half the defect because it filtered on strings mentioning the value's name, and the two most author-facing offenders never spell it.

title: Aeon accepts a fourth answer on the left-column key that our scene schema has no word for, so our advice is complete for what we can write and not for what they accept.
detail: Verified by the controller in the same aeon sentence that closed the row above, at d3339973: the engine tells an author to 'Declare Factor0Lock, Accept or DeclineBorrow', and our enum is undeclared, sprite_mask, factor0_lock, accept. NOT urgent and not a falsehood: no string of ours promises that arm, so nothing we say is wrong, and the gap is that an author who wants it cannot express it here. Aeon's own deferred work books the schema addition on their side, so the sequencing is theirs first. Booked low so it is not lost, because a missing option is the kind of gap that never gets reported by anyone: an author who cannot express a thing usually concludes it is not possible.

title: Two more domains are assumed savable while their savers only work with a resident project, and nobody has reproduced the gap.
detail: A FOURTH instance of the unsatisfiable-Save class, deliberately NOT fixed, and the reasoning is worth keeping. The agent found no reproduction of a dirty level or editor store with no resident project, and declined to tighten the guard on an unreproduced case because that would drop Save in states the guard is right about today. The assumption, the missing reproduction and the exact line to change are written at the site rather than only here. Closing this row needs a reproduction first, not a fix first. ⚠ LEFT OPEN A SECOND TIME, BY A DIFFERENT AGENT ON A DIFFERENT ROUTE, AND THE THREE SENTENCES HOLDING IT OPEN DID NOT SURVIVE CHECKING. One was true on a STRONGER basis than stated (the classic dirty flag implies the classic engine is open by construction, which also covers a race the cited reset does not). One named two of the nine production sites, though the conclusion survives on the wider basis that all nine mount on one branch. And the third, that tightening would drop the Save button in states the guard is right about today, HAS NO EXAMPLE: the classic saver's own predicate never consults the flag at all. That third sentence is precisely what a future reader would have quoted as the reason not to act, so it is worse than no justification: a wrong reason for a correct decision is durable and persuasive. The code is unchanged on the honest narrower reason, that there is nothing to verify a change against, and the site now says that instead. The state IS constructible through the debug surface, just not by a user, which is named at the site. REPRODUCED AND FIXED at the third attempt, and the reason two passes missed it is the finding: everyone hunted for a dirty store with a MISSING project, and the state needs the WRONG one. Classic takes precedence in the engine question, so a classic project opened over a resident dirty aeon project leaves the aeon work dirty with the aeon saver skipping. Measured on the unfixed guard: the primary button ran the CLASSIC saver over a project the author never edited, left the aeon work dirty, and advised them to save or discard first. ⚠ AND THE ASSUMPTION WAS IN TWO TEST SUITES AS A GREEN EXPECTATION: both mixed-state rows set the store dirty with no project open and commented it savable, passing only because an injected save seam marked the store clean by hand, which is a save no coordinator performs upholding an offer the guard should never have made. Repaired by making the premise TRUE rather than deleting the assertion. That is why two careful readers found nothing: the row was refuted by its own suite in the passing direction.

title: A loader derives a plane's bound from the very array being bounded, which the consumer module explicitly forbids.
detail: collision-cell-resolve.ts:41-44 says call sites must never pass an array's own length, because deriving the bound from the data being bounded is how a short plane stays short. load.ts:380 passes baseline.length. Not live today because the arrays are allocated at exactly SECTION_PLANE_WORDS, so the number is right for a reason the call site does not state. NOT LIVE, and it cost three things anyway; the third is the one the row missed. Deriving the bound from its own subject meant the mismatch report COULD NEVER FIRE on that road, so the loader was holding its own instrument's mouth shut. Measured: with the old derivation planted, the existing twenty-seven-row block covering absent, unreadable, truncated, odd-length and over-long planes stays FULLY GREEN, so that suite is structurally blind to it. The nested reader was exported precisely because independence cannot be measured unless a short array can be handed in.

title: The collision write path trusts its schema alone for which plane to paint, while the read twin argues at length for a handler-side check and has one.
detail: Suspected rather than verified: the off-schema road was not traced. The read path calls a validator and its source states the reason verbatim, for any road that reaches the handler without passing the schema. The write path has no such backstop, so an off-schema plane value falls through a ternary and silently paints plane A, a destructive edit aimed at a plane the caller did not name. Same threat model, opposite treatment, and the more destructive direction is the unguarded one. FIXED, and the row's suspicion was exactly right. Measured on the unguarded handler: off-schema plane values PAINTED PLANE A and reported success for a destructive edit aimed at a plane nobody named, while the read twin was already correct on all six values. What looked like a guard is the command's own description throwing on a non-string by accident, one refactor from silently painting A too. Not a live bug today because both roads validate against the same registry, which is the same status the read's own backstop has, and that is the argument its docblock makes for having one.

title: A harness clause has never once measured the app: it looks for a space where the app writes a comma, and it was invented rather than derived.
detail: Surfaced by the parcel that repaired the shared browser-driving helper. It is red on its swatch-arming clause. Recorded with its MODE stated because that is what decides how to read it: a timeout on a busy box is load-manufactured until proven otherwise, but an ASSERTION is not load-sensitive and stays a finding whatever the machine was doing. The same output line reports the open half green (project opened, act ready, panel mounted), so it is not the helper change. NO BEFORE-FIGURE IS OBTAINABLE from a worktree, because before the helper fix the harness never reached row one, which is why this could not have been found earlier. ANSWERED AS AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, because harness repair is what the owner's cut parks and making a row green by editing its own test is how a check becomes decoration. The app writes the swatch title with a COMMA after the digits; the clause filters on a SPACE. Verified by the controller against all three real title forms: the filter matches none, while the two other patterns on the same line match all three, so the fault is isolated. Wrong since the harness's first commit in two successive forms, and the app's title predates the harness by two days, so THE FORMAT WAS INVENTED RATHER THAN DERIVED. The failure is pure control flow: no swatches found, the attempt loop never runs, the row reports zero attempts, and its own docblock describes three scrolling and hit-testing hazards whose diagnostics cannot fire because the loop is never entered. Minimal correction recorded at the site with a warning not to delete the clause, since a later predicate would then throw on every other titled button. PARKED rather than fixed; unpark with the other instrument rows on the owner's word.

title: Collision swatch arming is untested rather than proven correct, because the check that was supposed to cover it never reached the control.

The harness clause never matched a swatch, so it has never exercised arming, which means a real defect there is UNTESTED AND NOT DISPROVEN. One run after the one-character correction answers it. Recorded because 'the instrument was broken' is the kind of verdict that closes a question in a reader's mind while leaving the subject unexamined, which is the same shape as a green log over an absent run.

Red-first with the mutation shown on disk and restored from a baseline COMMITTED BEFORE THE PLANT so the restore could not delete my own work: exactly the intended row red, the control green, and the failure shows the actual damage rather than a missing throw, resolving with a success report of one cell written for a plane nobody named. One honest limit: the throw assertion fires before the bytes assertion, so the untouched-foreground half is a belt this plant does not independently redden; the resolve value carrying a cell count is what evidences the write.

title: A fourth answer aeon accepts has no spelling in the shared contract, so no Aurora scene can express it; the missing piece is the HUB's, not aeon's.
detail: Verified by the controller in the same aeon sentence that closed the row above, at d3339973: the engine tells an author to 'Declare Factor0Lock, Accept or DeclineBorrow', and our enum is undeclared, sprite_mask, factor0_lock, accept. So we can neither write nor advise on one arm the build takes. NOT urgent and not a falsehood: no string of ours promises that arm, so nothing we say is wrong, and the gap is that an author who wants it cannot express it here. Aeon's own deferred work books the schema addition on their side, so the sequencing is theirs first. Booked low so it is not lost, because a missing option is the kind of gap that never gets reported by anyone: an author who cannot express a thing usually concludes it is not possible. ⚠ ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED BY THE OVERSEER: this row said the schema addition was booked on AEON's side and that is WRONG. The schema is the HUB's contract, vendored here byte-for-byte from empyrean contract/schema/aurora-effects-scene.schema.json, per our own provenance sidecar. I propagated the misattribution from an agent report into a row and then into a status field reading 'waits on aeon's schema', which is this session's own cross-repo-claim lesson firing on me. MEASURED NOW: the hub's contract at origin/main still carries the four-value enum with no decline_borrow. Aeon's DEFERRED_WORK:7202 names exactly what is needed and states that THEIR side is already done: the enum gains the lowercase string decline_borrow, their generator already maps it to the engine arm with a test, and until the schema lands no Aurora scene can spell it while the two adopters are hand-authored engine files. So handing this to aeon would be handing them work that does not exist. Aeon's own count calls it the FIFTH arm where ours said fourth, and they note six existing spellings keep their meaning, so no shipped record moves: that makes it a backward-compatible addition rather than a redefinition. Aeon's DEFERRED_WORK:26160 also suggests the owner already ruled the arm itself, which I have read one line of and am not asserting. WHAT WE DO ONCE IT LANDS: re-vendor byte-for-byte (our drift gate recomputes the blob id, so a hand-edit would fail), widen the TypeScript union beside it, and the row closes.
