title: The new left-column answer is the only one that changes ROM bytes and it is a trade, so a fifth word in a dropdown would misrepresent it.
detail: Aeon's constraint, relayed by the hub with the contract landing, and booked here rather than left in a message because a design note that lives only in correspondence does not survive a session boundary. Four of the five values declare a policy about a borrow that stays; decline_borrow declines it and is the ONLY value of the key that moves ROM bytes. The author is choosing which plane's sixteen-pixel edge is the correct one, which is a trade rather than a preference, and a fifth entry in a list would present it as one more option of the same kind. So the row is not 'add the option': it is that the surface has to show the trade. NO CONTROL EXISTS TODAY and nothing is wrong on screen, because the value round-trips and the advisories reason about it; this is a constraint on whoever builds the control. Written at the type as well, so a reader who never opens the ledger meets it.

title: Three dated notes claim aeon's bake does not read the crossover bits; whether that is still true at aeon's current head was not checked.
detail: FIXED at aurora 270b1df1. Re-checked against aeon origin/master bdbf9f5d, read from tools/collision_pipeline.py SOURCE rather than aeon's docs about it. TWO OF THE THREE DATED CLAIMS HAD INVERTED, so the file was telling readers the opposite of the truth: bake_plane_cell DOES read bits 15:14 (xover = (cell_word >> XOVER_SHIFT) & XOVER_MASK, interned), and R1 IS implemented (raises ValueError on XOVER == 3), so an act painted entirely with 3 now fails the build rather than emitting a byte-identical ROM. Both landed at aeon 8a4313b5 on 2026-09-02, four days after our notes were written. THE THIRD SURVIVES WITH A BETTER REASON: R2 is still unimplemented, so selfMarks remains the only place a self-mark is noticed, but the live reason is structural rather than unfinished -- bake_plane_cell(cell_word, profiles, angles, attrset) takes no plane parameter, so it cannot ask whether a mark points at the plane being baked. THE TAGGED SECOND HALF IS ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT and the answer is yes: over all 18 shipped section_*.collattr{,b}.bin at that revision, 1,179,648 big-endian u16 cell words, the XOVER histogram is {0: 1179632, 1: 8, 2: 8}; the 16 marks are eight TWO-WAY PAIRS in section 0 at coincident indices, A holding 2 and B holding 1. So the preservation tests are exercised by content. Histogram asserted to sum to the word count, and ENDIANNESS CONTROLLED rather than assumed (little-endian gives 2036/2056 marks at non-coincident indices; only big-endian yields pairs). Zero self-marks and zero reserved 3s ship, written into the comment so R2's absence is not read as a live leak. ONE DEFECT FOUND IN AEON AND RELAYED, not fixed by us: their XOVER_NONE = 0 constant is annotated 'the value every shipped cell holds' and sixteen shipped cells do not hold it.

title: The repo's strictest gate prints a coverage count of files it enumerated rather than files it actually parsed, and skips unreadable ones silently.
detail: FIXED at aurora 11f6edc8 (+ 65dbf28f fallout). parse() no longer swallows: a read failure or a file carrying parseDiagnostics is recorded with file and reason, and the parse pass runs over every enumerated file BEFORE anything is read out of any of them, because an unparsed file shrinks two populations at once (the repo-wide constant table and the scan). Exit 2, matching the existing empty-contract refusal's idiom. Pass line now prints BOTH numbers: '523 of 523 enumerated source files parsed'. CONTROLLER VERIFIED BOTH SIDES on the merged tree with the same plant (a tracked file deleted, ABSENT on disk, git diff --stat showing 1112 deletions): the PRE-FIX gate taken from committed 53ce4dfd printed '523 source files, 134 named numeric constants, 0 re-typed' at rc=0 -- a full-coverage claim over 522 actually parsed -- and the fixed gate refuses at rc=2 naming the file, the reason (ENOENT), '523 enumerated, 522 parsed' and 'A partial run is NOT a pass'. Runner: node scripts/check-prose-constants.mjs, inside the npm test chain. NARROWER THAN THE ROW IN ONE DIRECTION, WORSE IN ANOTHER, both from the agent and both accepted: the agent planted genuine syntax breaks (a bare '(((', an unclosed object literal raising 66 diagnostics, a missing comma inside the arbiter import) and the PRE-FIX gate still found a planted re-typing all three times, because TypeScript's error recovery is that good -- so the 'recovered tree with silently fewer nodes' arm is a STATED BOUND, not a demonstrated loss, and the agent rewrote its own commit message and source comment to say so after asserting it. The DEMONSTRATED half is the read failure. And for a file whose constants arbitrate an EXEMPT row, the pre-fix gate went red for the WRONG reason ('4 stale exemption(s)'), telling the author to delete four correct verdicts and never naming the missing file: silence for most files, misdirection for those.

title: The loopback test drives a hand-transcribed list of routes while its docblock claims it is planted against the real routing table, so a new unguarded route is invisible to it.
detail: FIXED at aurora f01be0bf. Rows now come from app.router.stack on the SAME app object the server serves, so the census grows with the router. Two guards under it, because a census fails by coming back SHORT and a short census is a shorter green run: (i) non-empty and every path requestable; (ii) the express table cross-checked against a second independent derivation (registrations grepped out of mcp-server.ts), refusing on exp.use('...') -- a mounted sub-router, the census's real blind spot -- and on exp.all(. The docblock's explanation of why fetch and why both layers is preserved verbatim, which was the row's own condition. CONTROLLER VERIFIED BOTH SIDES on the merged tree with one plant (a plausible new route that simply forgot the guard: exp.get('/aether/state', ...) with no loopbackOnly, quoted from disk, git diff --stat 1 insertion): the OLD hand-written array, restored verbatim from committed 73b9a4d2 and run against the SAME planted server, passed 6 of 6 and was TOTALLY BLIND; the derived census GENERATED A ROW FOR THE PLANTED ROUTE BY ITSELF ('403s a rebound /aether/state GET') and went red, 'expected 200 to be 403', 1 failed | 8 passed. Runner: vitest run, inside npm test. TAKEN ON THE AGENT'S REPORT AND LABELLED AS SUCH: the sub-router blind-spot guard was proven red on a separate exp.use plant by the agent and not re-verified by me; it is defence-in-depth rather than the row's closing claim, which I did verify.

title: The field telling four currency gates which branch to ask is read unguarded, and losing it degrades them to integrity-only while every other row still passes.
detail: FIXED at aurora ee8545e4. New currencyBranch(block, sidecar, repo) in test/support/peer-repo.ts returns {tip, present, defect}; tip is never undefined, so nothing steers by a hole. defect is asserted in each gate's PEER-INDEPENDENT INTEGRITY ROW -- the only row that still runs on a machine with no peer checkout -- and again at the head of each currency row, so a broken sidecar FAILS instead of skipping behind a peer-shaped excuse. The JSON.parse casts also lost their branch_that_answers_currency: string declaration, so tsc now refuses a return to bare access. A SECOND DEFECT THE AGENT FOUND INSIDE THE ROW: the one guarded reader's typeof check COLLAPSED ABSENT WITH MALFORMED -- a sidecar naming an unusable branch fell back to the repo default exactly like one naming none, so a mistyped field was silently measured against a branch nobody wrote down; present separates them and malformed is asserted before the unmeasurable skip. CONTROLLER VERIFIED BOTH SIDES on the merged tree with the field deleted from aurora-effects-scene.schema.provenance.json (field ABSENT confirmed by grep, git diff --stat naming the one file). PRE-FIX, from committed 05f89f7d: 14 passed | 2 skipped, GREEN, and the skip note read 'undefined does not resolve in <empyrean>; CANNOT MEASURE currency of pin c58dd0ce' -- it printed the literal word undefined as the branch name and BLAMED THE PEER for a defect in our own sidecar. The skip was honest that it was a skip and dishonest about why, which is the worse half: a reader goes and checks empyrean. FIXED: 3 failed | 13 passed, and the currency row's own title reads 'at empyrean (NO BRANCH: the provenance sidecar names none)'. Runner: vitest run, inside npm test. RESIDUAL, JUDGED AND NOT CLOSED, and I agree with the judgement: a WELL-FORMED BUT WRONG branch name (origin/mian) still degrades to a loud skip, because a named branch that does not resolve is genuinely indistinguishable from an unfetched or shallow clone. That is a real unmeasurable, not a defect to force red.

title: The sweep that stops a vendored-document list going stale covers only the fixtures tree, so a fourth contract document under src would get no currency check and nothing would say so.
detail: FIXED at aurora ee8545e4. The publishedness sweep's root became SIDECAR_ROOTS = ['test/fixtures', 'src'] -- 'src' and not 'src/core/formats/effects', because the narrower root would itself be a list, which is the hazard the row is about -- so the three revisions pinned in src sidecars are swept for the first time and all three are published today. PLUS a new COVERAGE describe asserting every vendored document under src/ is opened by a collected test, and so is its sidecar. THE PER-FILE GATES WERE KEPT, deliberately and correctly: they assert content the sweep cannot derive from a directory listing (byte identity against the pinned blob, the $id, that the imported module IS the file on disk, that every schema keyword is implemented). Gates say the copy is right; the sweep says a gate EXISTS. The coverage signal is a QUOTED PATH LITERAL in a collected test file rather than a grep for the filename, because a comment outbids code in a grep and every drift gate's prose header names the paths it discusses; the sweep file is excluded from the corpus it searches and derives every path it looks for, so it cannot certify itself. CONTROLLER VERIFIED BOTH SIDES with a fourth vendored document + sidecar planted under src/core/formats/effects/. PRE-FIX, from committed 05f89f7d over the whole test/formats tree: 56 files passed, 1026 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- COMPLETELY SILENT, which is the finding. FIXED: the COVERAGE row fails naming BOTH files, 'is vendored into this repo and NO collected test opens it by path'. MY FIRST TWO PLANTS WERE WRONG AND A NEIGHBOURING ARM CAUGHT THEM, recorded because stopping at either would have confirmed the gate for a reason that is not the row: plant 1 left the sidecar pointing at the preset schema and fired the describes-the-file-beside-it arm; plant 2 fixed that but used the wrong sidecar filename convention and fired the same arm again. Only the third plant, internally consistent and correctly named with its blob re-hashed on its own bytes, reached the no-gate arm.

title: A plain build reads as FRESH to every instrument in the repo, then the harness dies because the debug hooks are absent.
detail: FIXED at aurora 41da76b1 + 762d51dc. The build now STAMPS its own flavour: scripts/build-flavour-stamp.mjs writes dist/build-flavour.json {stamp, flavour, VITE_AURORA_DEBUG raw, at, by}, mounted as a vite plugin on ALL THREE electron-vite builds so it lands after whichever bundle finishes last. buildFlavour(run) returns debug/plain/UNKNOWN and assertDebugBuild refuses on plain AND on unknown, both naming the rebuild command in the tree the run is against. Six ways of failing to read the stamp are 'unknown' IN THOSE WORDS (absent, unparseable, not an object, unknown version, unknown flavour, older than dist/main/index.mjs), and each unknown row asserts the refusal does NOT contain 'PLAIN BUILD'. CONTROLLER VERIFIED IN THE FOREGROUND on the merged tree, which is the half an agent cannot do: rm -rf dist then npm run build -> flavour 'plain', VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1 npm run build -> flavour 'debug' with the raw '1', both exit 0. Then the four cases exercised directly through the real API: a real plain build refuses and its message SAYS 'PLAIN BUILD'; unparseable, unknown-stamp-version and absent all return 'unknown', all refuse, and NONE says 'PLAIN BUILD'. So 'I could not look' and 'I looked and it is plain' are distinguishable at the consumer, which is the inverse of this repo's boundSocketPaths empty-Set defect. THE AGENT DECLINED TO GREP THE BUNDLE and was right on measurement, which I reproduced: a PLAIN renderer bundle contains the string __dbg FOUR times (unminified, inside preserved docblocks), so a grep-the-bundle reader returns DEBUG for a plain build. TWO FINDINGS THE AGENT COULD ONLY GET BY RUNNING THE REAL BUILD, and its 12 green rows could not see either: the stamp module's shebang BROKE EVERY BUILD (electron-vite bundles the config with esbuild and inlines the import below the import statements, where #! is a syntax error) while node strips shebangs on import so every test passed -- fixed, plus a 13th row refusing a leading #! in any relative import of the build config. LEFT OPEN AND NAMED: ~174 other __dbg instruments do not call assertDebugBuild; a derived check-harness-guards rule is the fix and is out of scope. Anyone holding a dist/ built before this gets a loud UNKNOWN refusal naming the rebuild -- intended, but a real first-contact behaviour change.

title: Eight harnesses select on UI wording the app retired, so they fail the moment anyone runs them.
detail: FIXED at aurora ac0b8118 + 9da3d5fd + 93ecaa26. New scratchpad/lib/effects-sections.mjs; 8 harnesses repaired onto LOAD-BEARING IDS rather than onto the new words, which is the stronger fix: CollapsibleSection's own docblock says data-section/data-section-collapsed exist so a harness need not select on prose. Every replacement derived from src/ with its location named. A SECOND SHAPE HAD MOVED THAT REPAIRING THE STRINGS WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED: the sections now live behind the 'Tile anim' sub-tab and the facet arrives on 'parallax', so they are not in the DOM at all -- SIX OF THE EIGHT never clicked the tab, and a correct new title would still have returned no-section. THE LEDGER'S OWN LIST WAS WRONG AND THE AGENT REFUSED TO CARRY IT: band-trunk-watch DOES NOT EXIST (not now, not at the sweep's pin e17cdb02, not anywhere in history) and effects-foreground-2 is not a harness but a note file carrying none of the retired labels, so 6 of the booked 8 are confirmed; it found one the sweep missed (effects-column), giving 7 files with a live retired selector. Re-derived counts with the predicate STATED (live comment-stripped lines, 297 scratchpad code files): 10 old / 17 new / 3 both / 7 only-old, against the ledger's 15/16/7 which it could not reconstruct under three attempts and declined to explain away. Two files declared exemptions because the retired label IS the fixture: poisons-effects-usability.sh and o55-new-band-door-probe.mjs. THREE FINDINGS INSIDE THE REPAIR: effects-column's 'nobands' POISON found its target by the retired title, so it had stopped removing anything and its row was asserting against an unplanted column; bganim-band clicked a third retired selector by aria-label that the first census missed; fromtile-typing-probe's recorded dead end was measured with a wrong selector on an unactivated tab and is now marked UNVERIFIED rather than rewritten. NOT RUNTIME-VERIFIED, AND SAID SO: no harness was run, the proof is entirely static, and the tag at the top of effects-sections.mjs names the eight commands and what a pass is -- explicitly NOT 'exit 0' but the panel's own headings on screen, openEffectsSection returning clicked/already-open and never no-section, and effects-column's plant reporting what it removed. That is the controller's foreground follow-up and it is OPEN.

title: A census reported 'I could not look' correctly and the row asserting on it threw the reason away, rendering the sentinel as a TypeError that named nothing.
detail: FOUND WHILE JUDGING PARCEL C, not by looking for it, and fixed at aurora 546fb583. clearCallSiteCensus returns {sites: null, why} when the walk cannot complete -- the loud-on-unmeasurable contract, correctly implemented at the PRODUCER. typeof null === 'object', so a row asserting toBeGreaterThan against it first renders as 'TypeError: actual value must be number or bigint, received "object"', naming neither the census nor the directory nor the reason. THE CONSUMER DESTROYED THE PRODUCER'S REPORT. Fixed by asserting why is null FIRST, carrying why in the assertion message. WHAT IT COST is the argument for the row: FIVE full suite runs to establish that the failure was nondeterministic and resource-shaped rather than an assertion about the subject; one run would have said so. Red-first with the mutation quoted from disk against a baseline committed BEFORE the plant; red message now reads 'the call-site census could not look, so nothing below it means anything: /definitely/not/here could not be read (ENOENT)'. Runner: vitest run inside npm test. NOT A RAISED TIMEOUT, deliberately -- the file's own header already rules that out. CONTROLLER ERROR RECORDED: I ran ONE green pre-merge full suite as a control and attributed the failures to the merge, then a second post-merge run came back fully green. A single control run against a nondeterministic failure is not a control, and I stated the attribution before I had earned it.

title: The shared collision module set has never been read by a reviewer, and has taken 3,010 new lines and six new files since the last sweep.
detail: AUDITED at aurora b5c49588; notes committed at docs/reviews/2026-09-09-collision-audit-notes.md. RE-DERIVED FIGURES: 20 files / 3,852 lines in src/core/collision/; only ONE test file lives inside the module, the other 22 files / 2,822 lines sit out of tree in test/collision/; test:code 0.87:1. METHOD, which is the point: a green author's suite is evidence about internal consistency, so it was converted into evidence about correctness by planting 25 PLAUSIBLE defects one at a time, each quoted from disk with git diff --stat, one vitest run each, restored from a clean committed baseline. 22 killed, 3 survived. TWO CONFIRMED AND FIXED TEST-SIDE. (1) findFullBlockShapeId's h >= 16 threshold could be loosened to h >= 15 with the whole suite green -- and that id is stamped into AUTHORED DATA by blockRefToCollisionWord (every solid cell of every chunk in a donor import) and by migrateLegacyChunkCollision (a one-shot, load-time, NON-IDEMPOTENT rewrite); cause was that the near-miss decoy was EIGHT pixels short, so no plausible loosening could reach it. (2) crossoverAuditSeverity's cancelling arm could be DELETED ENTIRELY with the suite green -- the module's headline defect, since a two-way pair at the default mark width is exactly pairs>0/oneWay==0/cancelling>0, which layer-transition.ts says is EVERY cell-width pair, so the mutated predicate grades the defect this whole parcel exists to close as 'ok'; severity is what CollisionPalette colours on and what paint_collision returns to an agent. Cause: the count was asserted in crossover-span.test.ts, the predicate in crossover-audit.test.ts, and NO ROW IN EITHER FILE JOINED THEM -- a seam with no author. CONTROLLER VERIFIED THE HEADLINE ONE BOTH WAYS on the merged tree with the cancelling arm deleted (mutation quoted from disk): PRE-FIX 226 passed / 0 failed, completely silent; FIXED exactly 1 red, 'expected ok to be warn', on the row named 'a pair at CELL width nets to nothing'. I read the failure MESSAGE to confirm it named the planted mechanism rather than a neighbouring arm. NO FILE UNDER src/core/collision/ IS MODIFIED -- both changes are test-side, so nothing here can change authored output. MY BRIEF WAS WRONG AND THE AGENT CORRECTED IT: I relayed this ledger row's own sentence that classic renderer code imports collision-adapter.ts directly. It does not -- the adapter is imported by s4-collision-adapter.ts (aeon-only) and one test, while classic imports exactly two modules of this tree, collision-render.ts and collision-angle-mark.ts, from classic-overlays.ts and ClassicCollisionPanel.tsx. The row's CONCLUSION holds (the tree is shared, a defect reaches both paths) but its example does not, and acting on the sentence sends a reviewer to the adapter interface to find nothing. I passed a ledger sentence into a dispatch as fact.

title: findFullBlockShapeId returns 0 for both 'no profiles loaded' and 'loaded, no full block', and the chunk importer checks neither before writing the project and toasting success.
detail: RAISED BY THE AUDIT (finding 3), left for the controller because refuse-vs-warn is a design call, and NARROWED BY ME rather than closed. THE TWO ANSWERS: full-block-shape.ts returns 0 at `if (!profiles) return 0` (could not look) and again at the end of the search (looked, found none). migrateLegacyChunkCollision and blockRefToCollisionWord both check the result; chunk-library-import.ts:64 does NOT -- it passes the 0 straight into importChunks, then addChunks, markDirty() and a SUCCESS toast reading 'Imported N chunks -- Save to keep'. So not-looking would render as clean at a gesture that writes the author's project, which is this repo's dominant defect class at a data-writing site. MY NARROWING, and it moves this from live to LATENT: collisionProfiles defaults to null in projectStore, setCollisionProfiles has NO CALLERS anywhere in src/, so the field is populated only by openLoaded from aeon-open.ts, and the import gesture is reached only from AeonChunkActions.tsx -- an aeon component. The defect therefore requires an AEON PROJECT THAT OPENED WITHOUT COLLISION PROFILES. WHETHER THAT IS POSSIBLE IS THE OPEN QUESTION AND I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED IT; it is the one remaining step and it is named rather than guessed. Not claimed reachable, not claimed unreachable.

title: Four latent or plausible collision findings the audit reported and deliberately did not fix, plus one docblock that describes behaviour the code does not have.
detail: Recorded so they are not refound from scratch; full reasoning in the committed audit notes. (4) surfaceAnchor takes a median over an EVEN run, which has no unique median -- the audit declined to assert one, correctly, because a row pinning a choice there would be a test pinning an assumption rather than a behaviour. (5) flipProfile recomputes hasAngle from s4's odd-byte rule INSIDE an engine-agnostic module. (6) resolveCell and organizePalette alias the base bank's heights array; no mutating consumer exists today. (7) readCollisionCell folds a past-end index to air where its sibling crossoverInPlane exists precisely to REFUSE that -- currently unreachable because the loader rejects a mis-sized .collattr.bin. Also findMatchingBlockCells's docblock claims 'Returns the painted cell first' and it does not; no caller reads out[0]. RECORDED AS NOT-A-GAP so nobody refiles it: dropping the index >= plane.length guard from crossoverInPlane is unobservable, because the next line already answers undefined for every realistic ArrayLike.

title: Collision swatch arming is untested rather than proven correct, because the check that was supposed to cover it never reached the control.
detail: ANSWERED BY A REAL RUN, and the answer is that arming WORKS -- now tested rather than merely undisproven, which is the distinction the row was booked to protect. Foreground run by the controller on an idle box after a VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1 build (flavour stamp read back 'debug', so tonight's BUILD-FLAVOUR-INVISIBLE fix carried this run). npm run harness:collision-gesture: 9/9, exit 0, twice. THE EVIDENCE, not the pass count: row 1 reports `shape armed=1 via "shape 1, not used in this zone yet"` -- the comma proves the corrected filter matched -- and, decisively, `the probed block read shape 0 before the pick and 1 after, which is what says the swatch click reached the handler`. That is a state change read back out of the panel rather than a UI assertion about the click, so it discriminates. Also `0 earlier swatch attempt(s)`, so it matched first try with no fallback masking. Teardown clean: collision table back to the opening state, port free, 0 SIGKILLed.

title: findFullBlockShapeId returns 0 for both 'no profiles loaded' and 'loaded, no full block', and the chunk importer checks neither before writing the project and toasting success.
detail: CONFIRMED REAL, upgraded from 'narrowed, not claimed either way'. The one open step was whether an aeon project can open with collisionProfiles empty. It can, BY DESIGN, and I read it from source: core/project/aeon/load.ts loadCollisionProfilesFa 'Returns null on any missing/unreadable table so the overlay degrades gracefully (the view falls back to flat cell fills) rather than crashing' -- its catch swallows and tries the next location, and all misses return null. The call site loops the candidate dirs and its own comment says 'All misses -> null -> the overlay falls back to flat fills (no crash) and migration is skipped'. So the open SUCCEEDS with the field null. AEON SUPPLIED THE OTHER HALF, measured on their master: project.json declares no collision profiles at all (a regex for coll|profil|shape|bank over every manifest key returns nothing, and the string 'collision' does not appear), so the bank is an UNDECLARED WELL-KNOWN PATH with a second copy one directory up, and nothing validates a convention. A project whose bank is missing, renamed, or in the other of those two locations opens silently profile-less. THE CRUX, which is why this is not simply a missing guard: THE DEGRADATION IS CORRECT FOR THE OVERLAY AND WRONG FOR THE IMPORTER. The producer's null contract is deliberate and right for the consumer it was written for; chunk-library-import.ts:64 is a SECOND consumer that never asked whether null meant 'none' or 'could not look', passes findFullBlockShapeId's 0 into importChunks, then addChunks, markDirty() and a success toast reading 'Imported N chunks -- Save to keep'. migrateLegacyChunkCollision and blockRefToCollisionWord both DO check, so the importer is the outlier. Same shape as tonight's census finding one level up: the producer reported its blindness and this consumer read it as a value. NOT FIXED HERE: refuse-vs-warn changes what happens when the owner clicks Import, so it is his call and is filed as decision d-36.

title: Four latent or plausible collision findings the audit reported and deliberately did not fix, plus one docblock that describes behaviour the code does not have.
detail: DISPOSED ONE BY ONE rather than left standing as PLAUSIBLE, because a plausible finding nobody resolves becomes noise that makes the next reader trust the list less. (5) REFUTED AS STATED. The claim was that flipProfile recomputes hasAngle from s4's odd-byte rule INSIDE AN ENGINE-AGNOSTIC MODULE. The rule is s4's, but the module is not engine-agnostic and does not claim to be: collision-flip.ts's opening docblock is 'Mirror of the engine bake's flip math (tools/collision_pipeline.py flip_profile_x/y + flip_angle_x/y) so the editor preview is byte-faithful to what the ROM bake produces.' It declares its engine in its first sentence. WHAT SURVIVES, weaker and worth keeping: its POSITION in src/core/collision/ advertises a neutrality its docblock denies, and no consumer-side guard exists if a non-s4 profile ever reaches it. I also checked the transitive edge rather than the direct one, because this repo has been caught by exactly that before on MapViewport: flipProfile is reached through collision-cell-resolve, whose importers are OverlayRenderer, debug-hooks, agent-handler, CollisionPalette and map-flip -- all aeon-side -- while classic renders collision through its own providers/collision-overlay-classic.ts, which imports neither. So the s4 rule is applied only to s4 data, where it is correct. (6) CONFIRMED AND MEASURED, then deliberately not fixed. A throwaway probe against the real resolveCell reported 'UNFLIPPED aliases base: true / X-FLIPPED aliases base: false' -- flipProfile early-returns its argument when neither flip is set and the spread copies the Int8Array REFERENCE, so an unflipped cell's profile.heights IS the shared base bank's. A defensive copy is 16 bytes per cell per frame inside the overlay render loop, paid forever against a consumer that does not exist; enumerated today, none mutates it. Disclosed at the return site instead (aurora 78d1da76) so the day a consumer needs a private copy it makes one at ITS site. (7) and the findMatchingBlockCells docblock claim: left as the audit recorded them, verified by it, neither re-derived here and this row says so rather than implying I checked.

title: The connection badge displays serverName, which the producing lane documents as a deployment label and not an identity, so two different machines render the same string.
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER 2026-09-09 on oracle's ask, BEFORE aurora's UX pair runs rather than after. Oracle's pilot found that two of their windows can be two independent machines with nothing on screen saying which, and asked each lane to check its own surface for the same shape, since an editor with a live preview and a served surface has it available. AURORA HAS IT, IN A SHARPER FORM: not 'nothing says which' but 'something says which and it is a constant'. aetherStore.ts:136 sets the badge peer to (s.serverName ?? 'oracle') and AetherStatus.tsx renders it as 'connected · <peer>'. CONFIRMED AT THE PRODUCER'S SOURCE, oracle origin/main aca9e9a: engine.rs:3021 emits "serverName": self.config.server_name, config-supplied, with its own comment three lines above reading 'serverName beside them stays a deployment label, and stops being an identity'; build_info.rs:25 says '**Not serverName.** serverName remains a deployment label a config may set'; engine.rs:3023 emits "implementation": build_info::IMPLEMENTATION as the field that names which server. THIS LANE ALREADY BANKED THE RULE -- docs/OVERSEER.md says 'Read implementation, never serverName' -- and the store ALREADY HOLDS implementation, serverBuild, identityWarning, methodCount and servedMethods, so it displays the one field that cannot identify while holding the ones that can. A DISPLAYED IDENTITY THAT IS A CONSTANT IS WORSE THAN NONE, because it invites the trust that absence would not. SECOND LAYER, and it is what actually closes oracle's axis: implementation alone does not distinguish two INSTANCES, both of which report oracle-rs. The socket path is the only arbiter per this lane's own boot doc, and NOTHING UNDER src/renderer MENTIONS IT -- verified by grep. Dispatched as parcel/bus-identity-displayed.

title: No harness records which revision of a sibling repo it ran against, so a stale fixture is indistinguishable from a current one.
detail: FIXED at aurora 02529fd0. THE ENUMERATION MOVED THE ROW ONE LAYER AND MY BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS WRONG: I guessed three acquisition mechanisms including fresh clones, and there are NO fresh clones anywhere in this repo. The ACQUISITION side is already sound -- peers are read through git plumbing at a named revision, sibling-root.mjs is the one path derivation, several harnesses git-archive a SHA into a mkdtemp and never open the working tree. What was missing is the REPORTING side, which is what the row actually says. CENSUS (new scratchpad/peer-fixture-acquisition-census.mjs, groups asserted to partition or exit 1): 293 files name a peer -- 47 read bytes from the object database at a revision, 10 resolve a revision without reading by it, 56 name a peer and read nothing, and 180 READ A PEER'S BYTES WITHOUT GOING THROUGH GIT AT ALL. That 180 is the row's real population. THE SHAPE OF THE FIX honours this suite's own hard-won rule that a provenance record is SEVERAL CLAIMS THAT DO NOT SHARE A CLOCK: a record is an ordered list of claims, each with a label, a value, its own timestamp, and a `tracks` sentence saying what the value follows AND what it may not be read as. Nothing renders a fused string. The caller must declare `committed` (the revision names the bytes) or `worktree` (the revision names the BASE ONLY), and a ref in worktree mode is REFUSED, because a ref beside working-tree bytes reads as a claim they came from it. Unknown throws unless a named allowance accepts it, then renders 'UNKNOWN: <why>'; an unresolvable ref throws even with every allowance set. WHAT THE STAMPS MEASURED, live during the parcel: aeon's checkout was DIRTY with 33 uncommitted paths and its HEAD moved three times during the session. The 180 were reading a moving target and saying nothing. THE AGENT'S PLANTS FOUND TWO DEFECTS IN ITS OWN ROWS, both fixed then re-planted red, and both are house defect classes: a timestamp inside a compared string made a not.toBe unfailable (two renderings always differ by milliseconds), and a row asserted over a whole block so a SECOND claim still carried the words after the first claim's reason was deleted -- two operands, one assertion, which is this repo's consumer-side-guard rule. It also lost a conversion to `git checkout --` on a dirty tree, the exact hazard bar (b) names, and reported it. ONLY 3 OF 293 CONVERTED and the other 290 are named as a gap rather than a finish; the derived rule is DELIBERATELY not written, because a rule firing on 180 files at once is a rule the next lane disables.

title: Landing verification and agent work share one machine, and a TIMEOUT under that load is indistinguishable from a real failure; an assertion never is.
detail: FIXED at aurora 5ff4e398, and I RULED on the row's open design call rather than leaving it parked. REJECTED its candidate (3), 'refuse to grade a timeout while a build is detected': a suite that declines to grade a failure under load swallows the regression it exists to catch, and makes the verdict depend on an ambient condition nobody records -- blindness-as-cleanliness one level up. Candidate (1) is operational and stays open. Candidate (2) is per-row work the row itself warns would license raising every census row. BUILT THE FOURTH THING: the output SEPARATES the classes so one run says what cost five tonight. A vitest reporter (scripts/failure-class-reporter.mjs, third in vitest.config.ts) classifies every failure record as ASSERTION, TIMEOUT/would-block, or UNCLASSIFIED, prints 'why this bucket' per row, and refuses to sum wrong. Placed as a reporter rather than in land.mjs so it covers npm test, bare vitest and watch alike WITHOUT touching the landing script's control flow. THE SIGNATURE WAS DERIVED FROM THE PRODUCER, not from memory: a throwaway probe reporter dumped the real error shapes, then the wording was confirmed at @vitest/runner's own makeTimeoutError template, giving /^(?:Test|Hook) timed out in \d+ms\./. A structural-looking alternative (the STACK_TRACE_ERROR placeholder) was REJECTED after checking, because it is constructed in ~10 unrelated places; errno is an allowlist rather than 'has a code', since ENOENT arrives in the identical shape and would launder a missing binary into 're-run it later'. THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE IMPLEMENTATION: a HOOK timeout attaches its error to the SUITE and leaves the tests beneath reported as SKIPPED, not failed -- so the obvious reporter, walking allTests() for state === 'failed', sees NOTHING for that class, and it is the class load bites hardest because beforeAll is where the expensive fixture is built. The walk therefore covers module errors, suite errors, test errors and unhandledErrors. CONTROLLER VERIFIED THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRSTHAND on the merged tree: the canary's five deliberate failures classify 1 ASSERTION / 3 TIMEOUT / 1 UNCLASSIFIED, summing to the 5 records it reports against 4 failed tests -- the header states 'a hook or collection failure has no failed test of its own', which is the discovery made legible. Exit code 1 with the reporter. The TIMEOUT prose carries oracle's converse correctly and is not a licence to dismiss: 'load OPENS narrow windows as well as inventing delays, so a timeout that repeats on a quiet box is a finding, and one that does not is not proof of nothing.' NINE MUTATIONS, each read for the mechanism it named, including unwiring the reporter from the config (9 rows red -- the control proving the greps match nothing vitest prints by itself) and a fourth bucket firing the do-not-sum guard. ONE MUTATION CAME BACK APPLIED-AND-STILL-GREEN and the agent relayed it: its land.mjs coupling rows searched the whole file, so deleting the string left them passing because the COMMENT above the refusal mentions it -- a comment outbidding code in a grep, this repo's own bar, found independently. DISCLOSED AT THE SITE: this is a reader aid, not a gate; a silent regression in it reddens nothing on its own, which is what its two guard files exist for. LEFT OPEN BY THE AGENT AND WORTH KEEPING: unhandledErrors has no positive control, and a hook timeout skips the tests beneath it with no reason, so skip-report-reporter will call that unexplained and add a second complaint reading as a false accusation against the test author -- that is the other reporter's territory.

title: BEFORE dispatching the UX pair: each seat writes its OWN look-and-taste test SEALED, before being given the suite's, and only then walks under the suite's.
detail: AN ARRANGEMENT THAT MUST BE MADE BEFORE DISPATCH AND CANNOT BE MADE AFTER, banked here because it arrived only in hub traffic and a rotation would lose it. THE REASON: the suite is deciding on ONE shared look-and-taste test, and every lane asked about it so far was asked INSIDE the message that told them the answer -- so every opinion on record, including my own amendment, is a response to the incumbent rather than an independent invention. Sigil has already relayed the test to both of its walking seats, so it has no uncontaminated seat left. AURORA'S PAIR IS THE ONLY ONE NOT YET DISPATCHED, so this lane is the only place a clean data point is still obtainable, and only until dispatch. WHAT TO DO, two extra sentences in each brief, costing the run nothing: each seat writes its own test cold, from the brief's description of the job and nothing else, and SEALS it; then it receives the suite's test and walks under the suite's. The sealed answers are the data and are worth having even if both agree with us -- an independent arrival at the same test is the strongest evidence the rule is right, and that evidence exists nowhere else in the suite. THE ADOPTED TEST, to hand over AFTER the seal: 'does the person lose information they need to act, OR to know they are being misled?' -- the amendment is this lane's, adopted because without it a surface that confidently states something false bins as taste (it withholds nothing you need in order to act). STATE THE POPULATION AND COST UNIT BESIDE EVERY VERDICT: for aurora that is an authoring surface where a missing affordance costs AN HOUR OF WORK rather than a retry; sigil's is someone porting a disassembly, cost unit a build cycle. Without that, two lanes agree on the test and still produce incomparable bins -- a count has a unit. CARRIED BUT NOT ACTED ON, sigil's caution: the amendment covers the badge case and oracle's tick-box case for DIFFERENT reasons -- the badge states something meaningless, the control states something false about what it will do, and an inert wrong label costs trust while a wrong label on a destructive control costs data. Run under the text as written; if a seat produces the finding that breaks it, that is the next revision arriving the right way.

title: A consumer sweep asking 'does anyone branch on this?' is structurally blind to 'does anyone SHOW this?' -- and for an identity field, showing IS the failure mode.
detail: MINE, AND IT IS THE OLDER HALF OF BUS-BADGE-NAMES-NO-MACHINE. Oracle booked F-SERVERNAME-PREDATES-THE-RENAME on 2026-08-29 and THIS LANE CLEARED IT AT THE TIME: 40 references swept, zero comparisons, branches, includes, startsWith or match, verdict 'every use is display or pass-through'. DISPLAY WAS IN THE CLEAR LIST. The sweep sorted uses into branch versus pass-through and binned display as harmless -- correct for almost every field and PRECISELY WRONG FOR AN IDENTITY ONE. A rename would have left our suite green, the sweep correct, and a wrong name on screen: three artifacts agreeing and the user misled. My own caveat that day, 'our green is not evidence your rename is safe; it is evidence we do not look', was aimed one category short of the real exposure. IT IS ALSO THE AMENDED LOOK-AND-TASTE TEST FIRING ON THE SWEEP THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO PROTECT IT: the person loses nothing they need to ACT and everything they need to KNOW THEY ARE BEING MISLED. ORACLE PROPOSES IT AS A BAR-14 REFINEMENT AND SAYS IT IS MINE TO OWN, since both halves are. What the amended bar must say: when sweeping a consumer set for a field, DISPLAY IS A THIRD CATEGORY, not a subset of pass-through, and for any field whose job is to identify something, display is the category that matters most. NOT WRITTEN YET -- the owner's 09-02 cut forbids new process bars while its moratorium stands, and the hub has not said that clause lapsed with the rest; ask before writing it into OVERSEER-REVIEW-BARS.md.

The cut was aimed at process that COSTS. The standing split: refinements of existing shared bars land; NEW standalone process bars stay parked and batch through empyrean's protocol fold. Roughly twenty bar candidates came out of tonight and the hub is not letting them become twenty checklist steps in six repos. title: The connection badge displays serverName, which the producing lane documents as a deployment label and not an identity, so two different machines render the same string.
detail: FIXED at aurora c4212bdc. busStore lost `peer` entirely (one writer, one reader, and the field carried the label that cannot identify); the badge now reads implementation, serverBuild, socketPath, identityWarning and methodCount off aetherStore directly, and shows 'connected . oracle-rs . tmp/oracle.sock'. A SECOND DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY, and it would have made the fix look like it worked once: the socket path was ALREADY in AetherStatusPayload and already produced by the connect handler's RETURN, but publish() -- the push every status change travels on -- called statusPayload() with NO ARGUMENT, so every push in between carried undefined. A badge showing the path would have shown it at connect and lost it at the first stop or resume. NOTHING WAS ASKED OF THE PROTOCOL: the path is not on the wire and does not need to be, because THIS side chose it. identityWarning reached the store months ago and was DISPLAYED NOWHERE; it now reaches the tooltip, the aria-label, the agent reply and a visible '!' rather than hover-only, because a warning only as loud as a hover is half-surfaced. shortSocketLabel keeps TWO path segments, derived not guessed: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/oracle.sock and /tmp/oracle.sock SHARE A BASENAME, so a basename label would render two machines identically. Seven plants, each restored from a committed baseline and each failure message read to confirm it named the planted mechanism; row 6 exists because the obvious test (assert the placeholder is displayed) PASSES ON 'oracle', the exact string deleted, so its bar is derived from the producer -- a registry value is one token and a socket path has a separator. The agent also closed the same defect on two further surfaces rather than leaving one, since leaving one is how a class survives. CONTROLLER'S FOREGROUND ANSWER TO THE TAGGED LAYOUT RISK, derived from source and NOT from a running app: the fear was that CSS ellipsizes the socket tail off the right edge and silently destroys the property. IT CANNOT. There is no overflow, text-overflow, white-space or min-width rule anywhere in the chain -- ui/primitives.tsx StatusBar is a flex footer with space-between and height 24, MapStatusBar's two spans set none, and AetherStatus sets none -- and flex items default to min-width auto, so they cannot shrink below their content. WHAT DOES HAPPEN AT A NARROW WINDOW is that the bar's content overflows its own box rather than truncating, and the label growing from ~30 to ~48 chars makes that happen at a wider window than before. That is a LOUD failure rather than a silent one, which is the right direction, but it is real. STILL TAGGED AND NOT DONE BY ME: the on-screen look at the owner's own window width, which is partly his taste call, and the actual two-window test with two ORACLE_SOCKET values. I proved the string differs and that nothing clips it; I did not photograph two screens.

detail: SEAL EXECUTED 2026-09-09, branches parcel/uxa-sealed-test and parcel/uxb-sealed-test, each in its own worktree so neither seat can see the other's answer. Each produces one file under docs/reviews/2026-09-07-lens-ux/sealed/ carrying its question, its reasoning, what it admits and bins with two concrete examples each way, where it is weakest, how a verdict should be reported, and the alternatives it rejected. WHY IT HAD TO BE NOW: the final revision of the shared text arrived from the hub minutes after the seats were dispatched, and sigil's own two seats had already read the base text before the amendment reached them mid-walk. Aurora's pair was the last uncontaminated point in the suite and would have stopped being one on the next message. THE TEXT TO HAND THEM AFTER THE SEAL, third revision, VERIFIED FIRSTHAND at empyrean origin/main -- and note the location, because the hub's message said 'banked at 8b22db0' without naming the file and a reader who followed that SHA to OVERSEER.md would find nothing: it is docs/OVERSEER-PENDING-BARS.md line 13, commit 8b22db0644526a2263bec5c4e0659b045f803f99, confirmed an ancestor of origin/main by git merge-base --is-ancestor. Verbatim: 'Does the person lose information they need to act, or to know they are being misled -- including by an output that cannot be told apart from a materially different outcome?' STATE THE POPULATION AND COST UNIT BESIDE EVERY VERDICT; for aurora the population is an authoring surface and the cost unit is AN HOUR OF WORK rather than a retry, because two lanes can agree on a test and still produce incomparable bins -- a count has a unit. WHAT FORCED THE THIRD REVISION, and it is the class our surface produces in quantity: sigil's UXa found that `sigil emp <file>` with no -o prints 'built: 4 bytes', exits 0, and writes nothing, in a line BYTE-IDENTICAL to the writing run's. Nothing false is stated because nothing is stated at all, and nothing needed for the next action is missing -- what is lost is the ability to tell two materially different outcomes apart, lost to an ABSENCE rather than an assertion. UXa proposed a third clause 'or to know what the run actually did'; the hub adopted the substance and refused the separate bin, because that wording would admit almost any output gap, and closed the reasoning step inside clause two instead. OUR OWN INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, named by the hub: the badge parcel's publish() defect was exactly this -- a value that existed, was computed correctly, and silently stopped reaching the screen, every push after the first carrying undefined, with nothing on screen distinguishable from the working case.

title: The conflation is now impossible: findFullBlockShapeId is gone, lookupFullBlockShape returns a three-state result, and the 0 sentinel left the whole chain. The importer no longer claims success over an all-air library. Refuse-vs-warn is still d-36's and is untouched.
detail: FIXED, and the fix is the VALUE rather than a guard. findFullBlockShapeId returned 0 for both 'no profile set was loaded, so I could not look' and 'a real bank was searched and holds no full block'. It is DELETED. lookupFullBlockShape(profiles) returns FullBlockShapeLookup = {status:'found',shapeId} | {status:'no-full-block'} | {status:'no-profiles'}; only 'found' carries an id, so a blind answer cannot be spent. AND THE SENTINEL LEFT THE WHOLE CHAIN, which is the part that makes it impossible rather than discouraged: importChunks (core/formats/chunk-mappings.ts) and migrateLegacyChunkCollision (core/model/chunk-migrate.ts) both took fullBlockShape:number and both checked ===0 CORRECTLY, but a signature that accepts a bare number accepts a collapsed one. They take the result type now, so the only route to a shape id is a status==='found' narrowing the compiler enforces. The producer upstream (loadCollisionProfilesFa's deliberate null, correct for the overlay) was NOT changed. THE IMPORTER: chunk-library-import.ts opens the lookup instead of spending it, and a new pure exported chunkImportOutcomeToast(count, lookup) gives a different sentence per state -- success on found, and TWO DIFFERENT warnings naming which blindness happened and that every cell came in as air. The import still proceeds. WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT MINE: d-36-air-collision-import (refuse vs warn) is UNANSWERED and untouched; its own recommendation is 'refuse'. The truthful toast is the floor of all three of its options -- under 'refuse' the same sentence becomes the refusal's text, and the refusal arm has a named home in importChunkFiles before addChunks -- so nothing here has to be undone whichever way it goes. HONEST CAVEAT: today's behaviour is what d-36 words as 'warn'; the claim is that it does not CLOSE the card, not that it is distinguishable from that option in behaviour. A SHARPENING FOR THE CARD, offered not taken: there are TWO situations, not one. 'no-profiles' (the tables did not load; refusing costs nothing) and 'no-full-block' (a bank loaded and has no full block; refusing refuses an author who HAS collision data). They may deserve different answers. docs/decisions.jsonl was not edited. load.ts:833 keeps its behaviour exactly (a library it cannot migrate is left alone) and gains a console line naming which blindness skipped it, guarded on there actually being legacy collision to migrate. CALLER CENSUS, two instruments of different kinds: grep for the identifier, and tsc --noEmit after the rename (a census a grep pattern cannot miss). Same population both ways: two src callers plus three test files. The wider collisionProfiles:null readers (agent-handler readCollisionRegion, MapViewport ghost/overlay/status-bar, CollisionPalette, OverlayRenderer) are READERS, not writers of authored data, and MapViewport's status bar already prints '(tables not loaded)' distinctly. VERIFIED: npm test 562 files passed | 3 skipped (565), 8208 tests passed | 9 skipped (8217), rc=0, against a master db894e96 baseline of 560|3 (563) and 8198|9 (8207) -- +2 files and +10 tests, reconciling exactly. NINE red-first mutations, each applied on disk with the diff quoted and restored from a committed baseline; each two-armed guard broken in BOTH directions separately, with the other status's row staying green each time. Mutation 4b restores the original defect (plain success toast on every answer) and reddens both blind rows. DECLARED GAPS: no DOM, so the button-to-function wiring, the toast being painted and its legibility are unproved (TAGGED for foreground); and the no-full-block arm of load.ts's console line has no load-level row (it needs a decodable bank with no full block on disk) and rests on the shared status narrowing proved elsewhere. Packet: docs/reviews/2026-09-09-fullblock-two-answers.md. Branch parcel/fullblock-two-answers.

title: The 3,915-line map surface the user draws on is imported by no test, and three standing fixes live inside it.
detail: NARROWED AGAIN, AND THE SCAN/BEHAVIOUR SPLIT IS NOW MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The previous row left three residuals: the coverage was not even over a 4,357-line file, the BG-stroke half of BG-STROKE-WRONG-ACT was held by a SOURCE SCAN rather than behaviourally, and the empty dep list on the unmount effect was caught only by that scan. All three are addressed; parcel parcel/map-coverage-2, packet docs/reviews/2026-09-09-map-coverage-2.md, tips 80fd0d17 -> 7bcd4d08 -> 12c90f67. THE BG HALF IS NOW BEHAVIOURAL, and it found a live defect on its first run. Reaching paintBgTile needs a loaded BG plane; the fixture now gives both acts bgLayout/bgTiles and the COMPONENT'S OWN reloadBg loads them (a test calling sectionRenderer.loadBg would assert against a plane the component never resolved). Eight rows drive the real handlers. The sixth went red against source in which every line the scan asserts was present and correct: abandonStaleGestures's BG arm reverted the stroke's live writes and dropped bgStroke.current but left isPaintDragging.current TRUE, where both sibling arms end their gesture. The held button survived the cancellation, the next mousemove re-entered paintBgTile and opened a BRAND-NEW stroke in the act that had just been switched to -- an edit to a plane the author never pressed on, immediately after a toast saying 'Nothing was written'. Fixed in 80fd0d17, one line, inside the bgStrokeMustRevert arm (background-switched must keep the drag alive or the held button is stranded mid-paint). AND THE OTHER DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE FINDING TO CARRY FORWARD: a scan row can NAME a defect and still not catch it. map-surface-listeners.test.ts asserts revertBgStroke does not contain resolveDisplayedBg or getCurrentAct, with the message 'a revert that re-resolves the plane would write into the wrong act'. Planted exactly that -- revertBgStroke writing through bgFrameFresh() instead of stroke.layout -- and the scan stayed GREEN, because bgFrameFresh calls both banned functions one level of indirection away and a text scan reads only the block it was pointed at. Three behavioural rows caught it. A negative enumeration of known-bad callees was deliberately NOT added to the scan: that is a partial instrument that then earns trust it has not got. BOTH INSTRUMENTS STAY, AND BOTH WERE RE-MEASURED. (1) The empty dep list: changing [] to [finishGesture] reddens two rows in map-teardown.test.ts and NONE of the behavioural rows -- re-measured under the enlarged set, not quoted from the previous report. (2) The act check inside endBgStroke is STRUCTURALLY scan-only: abandonStaleGestures runs first on all three teardown routes and always reverts an act-moved BG stroke, so by construction no behavioural row can reach endBgStroke with a stale actKey. It is a consumer-side arm against a FUTURE call site, and no harness work changes that. COVERAGE ADDED: 24 rows, 25 -> 49 in map-viewport-mounted.test.ts. Three blocks: the BG tile stroke (8, previously scan-only), the map's keyboard (9 -- arrows, zoom keys, Escape, the isTypingTarget guard and the levelKeysEnabled guard, none of which had ANY test running them), and the FG tile stroke (7 -- recordPaint/endPaintStroke/revertPaintStroke, the fourth gesture carrier, also untouched). Every one of the 24 is red-first proven by a mutation shown applied on disk: 19 mutations, 19 reds, none unapplied. TWO ROWS COULD NOT FAIL UNTIL THEY WERE CHANGED, stated rather than folded into a clean 24/24. The Escape CONTROL row parked at zoom 1, so a planted 'Escape resets the view' called setZoom(1) on a view already at 1 and all 42 rows stayed green; it now parks at zoom 2 off the origin and the same plant reddens it. The direction rows had the same shape: viewStore.pan clamps with Math.max(0, ...), so at the default vpX/vpY of 0 the Left and Up arrows are indistinguishable from a dead key. Every direction row now starts at (256,256) and ONE row keeps the bound, labelled as the clamp row. One hazard, met twice. A FIXTURE THAT WOULD HAVE MADE A ROW LIE, fixed: the section nametable was Uint16Array(64) while worldToSectionTile computes row * SECTION_TILES_WIDE + col = 256, and an out-of-range typed-array store is DROPPED not thrown. A row dragging down a column would have painted one cell, asserted three, and the fixture rather than the component would have been what failed. Sized from the engine constants now. Both planes' fills are per-act so a wrong-act write is a wrong VALUE, not only a wrong array identity. WHAT REMAINS, so this is still not read as closed. The file is ~4,500 lines and three blocks do not make it even. Reachable and still uncovered: the marquee drag and its snap, paste mode, the BAND STAMP (the sixth gesture carrier, and the one the isPaintDragging row shape has not been pointed at), collision paint incl. both-planes, the BG OVERRIDE arm of paintBgTile (the out-of-blob refusal and its once-only toast -- this parcel built the 'act' arm), the context menu, the guide drag and the screen-frame drag. FOREGROUND-ONLY and tagged, not attempted: anything depending on a pixel or on real layout (nothing paints, nothing lays out, no event propagates, and every rect in the file is DECLARED by the test rather than measured by a browser); the browser fact the wheel fix rests on (React registers root wheel listeners as passive); 'is this on screen', which needs the rect compared to the SCROLLER's box and there is no scroller here; and resolveEscape's band-lens arm, gated on inEffectsFacet(). Also noted for whoever is next in that file: map-escape.test.ts's header still says the Escape branch 'is inside a React effect the node suite cannot reach', and that sentence is now false. SUITE: before 1 failed | 8197 passed | 9 skipped (8207); after 8222 passed | 9 skipped (8231). The baseline failure was a TIMEOUT in facet-modules.test.ts, classified by the repo's own failure-class reporter and green after -- load, not a defect. 8231 - 8207 = 24, the number of rows added; the counts sum. tsc --noEmit clean.

title: The client that talks to the emulator got its first plant-and-count audit: 52 plants, 32 killed, 62 percent. 16 of 20 survivors closed with zero source lines changed; the overseer's rulings on the other four are here.
detail: Packet docs/reviews/2026-09-09-aether-client-plant-audit.md, merge 791d2578. Kill rate 62% against the collision audit's 88% the same night. HEADLINE, and it is the badge defect one field over: paletteUnservedMethod is guarded once at PRODUCTION and nowhere on its journey to a person -- three independent delivery-path plants all passed green (classic probe arm dropping it, connect handler never storing it, statusPayload never wiring it). Its consumer at agent-handler.ts:1784 turns it into 'this is a server gap, not a ROM problem', so its absence tells an artist their ROM lacks palette symbols and they rebuild a ROM nobody asked for. FOUR SURVIVORS THE AGENT DELIBERATELY LEFT, RULED BY THE OVERSEER 2026-09-09. (P14) requireMethod has NO production caller: VERIFIED FIRSTHAND -- client.ts:402 plus one test, nothing else in src/. RULING: do not harden it. The question it answers is already answered TWO other ways in production, and I checked which: a PRE-FLIGHT gate against the advertised list (push-palette) and a REACTIVE classification of -32601 after the call (unservedMethodOf, bridge.ts:81/91). requireMethod is a third mechanism nobody uses, and an unused guard is exactly what a later session adopts believing it is the house one. It gets a production caller or it goes; booked, not done, because it ships no wrong output today. NOTE FOR THE PACING-REVIEWER QUEUE ROW: its claim that 'our client already asks whether a method is served' STANDS -- but via those two mechanisms, not this one, and the row should say which. (P10) methodCount from methods.length vs a de-duped Set: NOT RULED HERE, and deliberately. The consumer is this repo's own freshness tell -- read the startup banner's method count and treat a mismatch as a stale binary -- so the semantics must MATCH ORACLE'S OWN COUNT, and deciding it from our side would pin a number against a producer that may count differently. Ask oracle what their banner counts before pinning ours; a de-duped count would also hide a server advertising a duplicate, which is itself a signal. (P08) loadSymbols clears its cache after the await rather than before: real under concurrency, but nothing today makes it concurrent. Booked as latent with the trigger named -- the day any caller runs two loadSymbols against one client. Not fixing speculative concurrency. (P19) the onStatusChange publish: near behaviour-preserving; accepted as low, no action, and the agent reporting it low rather than inflating it is the right handling. METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: two runs were discarded as MALFORMED rather than scored, because a collection-time SyntaxError reddens nine files and produces a totals line indistinguishable from a genuine catch; the runner now refuses to score any log containing SyntaxError. And the agent's own first census draft went red on UNMUTATED code by asserting over every 'connected' push including ones taken before the palette probe ran -- an over-strong claim, not a defect, corrected to read the push a bus event triggers after connect. TAGGED FOR FOREGROUND, needs a live bus: that a real oracle-aether sends 'limits' at all; that advertised-and--32601 is a shape a real server produces rather than only a modelled one; and that a path at exactly SOCKET_PATH_MAX is refused by the kernel rather than only by our arithmetic about sun_path.

detail: CLOSED BY AN INSTRUMENT, NOT BY A FIX - no product code changed; src/main/index.ts and src/main/close-handshake.ts are byte-identical to master. `npm run harness:close-guard-witness` (22 rows, 0 failed, 21.7s) launches the real app under Xvfb three times and injects an ADDITIVE observer into the RUNNING main process over Node's --inspect, registering its `close` listener AFTER the app's so the `defaultPrevented` it reads is the app's decision; records are appendFileSync'd to a trace file because main's stdout dies with the process. title: P10 ANSWERED, and the answer kills the approach rather than settling the dedup question: NO method count is a freshness tell, and this repo's boot doc said otherwise in three places.
detail: Supersedes the 09:41:58Z row's P10 ruling, which was 'ask oracle what their banner counts before pinning ours'. Oracle answered via the hub and I VERIFIED IT FIRSTHAND at oracle origin/main 47dc414eb4e8870afb87b8b0d545b8fabfaa662f (tree named, SHA pinned, symbols quoted so the claim survives the lines moving). THE FACT: dedup is moot -- there are no duplicates, and oracle's tests/methods.rs already asserts uniqueness, so a duplicate is caught AT SOURCE rather than inferred from a count, which answers my duplicate-hiding objection better than either option I was choosing between. THE REAL DIVERGENCE IS A FILTER AND IT IS BY CONSTRUCTION: the banner at crates/oracle-aether/src/main.rs:87-88 prints METHODS.len(), the raw static table, unconditionally; initialize.methods at engine.rs:2999 is built from advertised_methods(config.presents_frames), which drops PRESENTING_ONLY (engine.rs:758). main.rs NEVER SETS presents_frames -- I checked, zero occurrences in that file -- so it takes the default, and THE STANDALONE HEADLESS BINARY'S BANNER IS OFF BY ONE ABOUT ITS OWN HANDSHAKE, on every connection, deterministically. A windowed player sets it true and both read the same. So the tell fires 'stale binary' at a CURRENT, CORRECT server, off by exactly one -- the most misleading magnitude available, because one reads as a miscount or a stale build rather than as two honest answers to different questions. THIS IS O26 RECURRING ON THE CONSUMER THAT FILED IT: we pinned methods === '35' and threw 'stale oracle-aether binary' at every correct binary, and that booking's durable line was A TOTAL WAS THE WRONG OBSERVABLE. Pinning a peer's banner instead of a literal is the same defect with a longer wire -- one of their numbers against another of their numbers under different definitions. the budget module's two-sided currency claim
detail: OFF-SCHEMA ROAD, CLOSED. AgentRequest is a type, erased at compile, so each transport's own parse is the only gate. Census taken with the compiler (retype requestAgent's payload and handleAgentRequest's req to a unique symbol, run tsc, read the caller list): production has exactly three call sites forming one chain, mcp-server.ts:26 and :135 into agent-handler.ts:142. Blind spot named: ten TEST sites write `as never`, which is assignable to everything, so they never error and never appear. RATIO: Aether road 57/57 gated (100%); MCP road 45/57 (78.9%), 12 ungated (21.1%). mcp-server registered inputSchema only when a method had params, and the MCP SDK picks the callback SIGNATURE off exactly that, so for the twelve zero-param methods `args` bound to RequestHandlerExtra and was spread into the request: 13 keys no schema has seen, two of them functions. webContents.send serialises with structured clone, which throws on a function, so all twelve could not cross the IPC hop (fails loud, not silent). Fixed by registering inputSchema for every method; tools/list before/after differs only by 12 added $schema lines (45 -> 57). Red-first 24 failed / 150 passed, then 175 passed. BUDGET CURRENCY CLAIM, FALSE. Answered from the producer's committed source, not Aurora's copy, at aeon origin/master 544bd749af6eae9a5f47316cc39076ef71926b43 (games/sonic4/vram.toml blob ebbf4afba83beb8d79bd0ae74090041565684813, tools/vram_map.py blob 1c8e49f8f88cb73d1cb662c7191b9b75a51023d5). FG_TILE_LIMIT was 1024 under the comment 'BG region starts at tile slot 1024'. PREMISE TRUE (Aurora already vendors BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT = 1024, currency-gated); CONCLUSION FALSE: aeon declares fg_art_pool at base 0 with tiles = 768 (POOL_TILE_CEILING), and ELEVEN regions occupy the gap, so Aurora handed authors 256 tiles belonging to other regions, a 33% overstatement on the generous side. Not a stale copy of a past value either: aeon's ceiling moved 960 -> 896 -> 768 and 1024 was never any of them; it was a bare literal with no provenance, no contract entry and no gate, in a repo that has all three for the BG twin. Corrected to 768 and gated by test/formats/fg-pool-ceiling-currency.test.ts, which reads two aeon authorities at a committed revision and skips loudly when absent; planted, restoring 1024 reddens both rows. STILL OPEN AND MEASURED BY NOTHING: the COUNTING half. computeActBudget sums two checkerboard VRAM groups from the retired per-section VRAM-base scheme while aeon holds act FG art in one globally-deduped paged pool, so a shared tile is counted twice here and once there; the old comment claimed fits === !exportThrows and that export path was retired 2026-08-19. The reading is conservative on the tile axis and is now described that way rather than as an equivalence. Whether the two-group split is the right model, and whether page-frame fragmentation can refuse an act whose raw tile count fits, wants aeon's pager. TAGGED for foreground: the twelve broken MCP tools are proven by the structured clone algorithm, not by a running Electron.

title: The FG budget was wrong TWICE in one night about one number: the ceiling's VALUE was a third too generous, and its UNIT was the tile when the engine refuses you in page frames.
detail: SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME QUANTITY. GUARD-SEAT-RESIDUE corrected FG_TILE_LIMIT 1024 -> 768 (master 145de20c). That was the ceiling's VALUE. THE UNIT WAS ALSO WRONG. Read at aeon origin/master 49a8144cc8d286483c131f69bbc4ca9f91b8bc90 (6d92821f, the revision the brief named, is an ancestor; aeon advanced one commit mid-parcel): games/sonic4/vram.toml blob ebbf4afba83beb8d79bd0ae74090041565684813, engine/system/constants.emp blob 3b7f1b5fef0257b572785f858835082bf88b90ce, engine/level/page_cache.emp blob 699f4cf2a35d658c7cf173b0bae724d09d5570ca, games/sonic4/config/constants.emp blob 3ee19baeb11762223d0fdce68bc3306746336dbf. THE MECHANISM: the FG art window is carved into FIXED page frames (vram.toml `quantum`, engine ART_POOL_PAGE_TILES) and an act's baked art is split into pages of that size; A HALF-FULL PAGE STILL CONSUMES A WHOLE FRAME, so an act costs its PACKED page count, which aeon's packer decides at bake time and Aurora cannot run. So the reading is a LOWER BOUND, ceil(tiles/quantum), and says 'at least' everywhere it is shown. `fits` is REMOVED from ActBudget: a boolean answering 'does it fit' is an output that cannot be told apart from a materially different outcome. Two honest verdicts: 'over' (the bound alone exceeds the frames, which is the one thing a bound can prove) and 'undetermined'. FRAGMENTATION IS CLOSED and is NOT why: the frames are fixed-size, so there are no variable-size holes and any free frame takes any page; the waste is INSIDE a partly-filled page. DERIVED, NEVER TYPED, BECAUSE THE VALUE IS ABOUT TO MOVE: the engine lane has an open recommendation to shrink POOL_TILE_CEILING, and aeon does not store the frame count either (pub const PAGE_FRAMES = POOL_TILE_CEILING / ART_POOL_PAGE_TILES, with its own comment recording that a spelled-out count went stale for two relayouts). Aurora mirrors the division and THROWS on an inexact split. NOTHING IN THIS REPO PINS A FRAME COUNT: the new gate test/formats/fg-page-frame-currency.test.ts reads aeon's inputs at the tip and DIVIDES, so a pool resize stays green, and it also gates the SHAPE of aeon's derivation (a reserve added there would silently make our division wrong while every value stayed correct) and that AURORA declares the count by division rather than a literal. Loud skip proven: with an empty AEON_DIR, 2 passed / 4 skipped, every skip saying CANNOT MEASURE. TWO INSTRUMENT FINDINGS, BOTH FROM PLANTING. (1) MY OWN CHECK WAS VACUOUS: the first version compared multi-digit runs in the RETURNED strings against the derived values, and a typed 12 passed it, because a typed 12 and an interpolated FG_PAGE_FRAMES interpolation PRODUCE THE SAME STRING. Only the SOURCE distinguishes them; the row now reads the module text and strips the interpolation spans. (2) THE REPO'S SHARED PROSE GATE CANNOT SEE A DERIVED CONSTANT. scripts/check-prose-constants.mjs polices author-facing `description:` prose and `description` IS in its key population, so the tool description LOOKED covered; its constant table is built by numericInit, which folds a numeric literal or constant('X') and nothing else, so FG_PAGE_FRAMES (declared as a CALL) is absent and a typed twin matches nothing. Measured: with 12 on disk over the interpolation, rc 0 and '0 re-typed in author-facing prose'. THE GENERAL SHAPE IS WORSE THAN THE SITE: the constants it cannot fold are the DERIVED ones, which are exactly the ones whose values move. OPEN, not fixed here (523-file blast radius, wants its own red-first parcel). ALSO CORRECTED: docs/MCP.md still said 'must fit the 1024-tile FG pool' and 'fits: false' hours after the constant was fixed, because a document is a second author with no arbiter; it now restates NO number and points at the gates. And two claims about `fits` inside fg-pool-ceiling-currency.test.ts had become false. STILL UNQUANTIFIED AND DELIBERATELY MADE MORE PROMINENT, NOT LESS: the DOUBLE-COUNT (the reading still sums two checkerboard groups from the retired per-section VRAM-base scheme against an engine that dedupes globally, so it is conservative by an amount nobody has measured; answering fragmentation did NOT make the figure equivalent), the PACKING WASTE, and PINNING (a pinned frame is never an eviction candidate, so the capacity covering a moving view is the UNPINNED count, which aeon has open with no measurement; no number invented). All three ride in the reply's unquantified[] so the figures cannot be read without them. STILL OPEN: whether the two-group split is the right model at all. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED; nothing here wants one. Suite 8439 passed / 9 skipped (8448) in 569 files, exit 0; baseline on master 145de20c was 8426 / 9 (8435) in 568.

title: The half this row filed rather than half-fixed is CLOSED: the shared prose gate can now see a derived constant, and says out loud what it still cannot see.
detail: HALF CLOSED BY docs/reviews/2026-09-09-prose-gate-derived-constants.md (branch parcel/prose-gate-derived-constants, base master d9fbf105). The 523-file blast radius this row named as wanting its own red-first parcel is that parcel. Restored from the committed baseline before any change. THE FOLD now reaches three shapes: arithmetic over names already in the table (+ - * / % ** << >> >>> & | ^ and unary - + ~; `+` folds only when BOTH sides are numbers, so the 32 exported string-concatenation consts fall out with no special case), alias, and ONE call shape -- a function whose body ends in its only return, whose returned expression is arithmetic, and EVERY identifier in which is one of its own parameters. That last clause is what stops it being an interpreter: a body reaching module scope would need the DEFINING module's names, and resolving those against the caller's table INVENTS a value rather than declining to have one. deriveFgPageFrames is exactly that shape. The table is built to a FIXPOINT, so git ls-files order no longer decides whether TILE_RGBA_BYTES = TILE_PIXELS * 4 resolves. MEASURED BEFORE IT SHIPPED, because a gate that cries wolf is retired by its readers and that is worse than the blindness: over the whole tree the arms take the table from 135 named constants to 168 and cost exactly TWO new candidate findings (raw candidates 10 -> 12; the gate reports 0 either side). Both are in editor-methods.ts, both about the value 12: a BIT POSITION ('solidity 13:12') and an ILLUSTRATIVE COORDINATE ('section 3, cell (col 12, row 40)'). Both adjudicated in EXEMPT with written verdicts. A fold that flooded the gate would have been reported with the number and constrained instead. THE SILENCE IS THE HALF THAT MATTERED MORE. What the fold cannot reach now announces itself in two tiers. NEAR MISS (hard, 4 today): the fold attempted the initialiser and abandoned it, so an author is asked to fold it or write an UNFOLDABLE verdict; an unadjudicated one FAILS the run and a stale row fails too, on the rule EXEMPT already lives by. Counted, NOT adjudicated, deliberately: a written verdict per constant would redden the build on ordinary effects-lane work, and a gate that fires on correct landings gets switched off. Both counts ride on the GREEN line, which now opens 'NOT FULL COVERAGE', and --blind names all 37. NEITHER TIER CLAIMS TO BE THE WHOLE BLIND SET and the header says so: a constant built by a shape neither predicate recognises is invisible to this census too. REJECTED, with the measurement: refuse-only (leaves the blindness in place, and its predicate is only meaningful relative to what a fold attempts -- a first cut accepting ANY single-return helper call named 118 constants, most returning objects and strings, which is noise); and fold-only with a silent remainder, which is the defect shape this repo already knows best. FOUND BY BUILDING IT, the same defect one level down: the first working ledger named MARK_BOX_MARGIN = NORMAL_LEN / 16 as a blind spot when the fold had evaluated it perfectly to 0.40625. The table was dropping non-integers, so 'could not evaluate' and 'evaluated, and it has no digit-run twin' arrived as the same null. The integer filter now lives at the prose MATCH, where the stated bound is, and the table keeps 6.5. The fold is split into scripts/prose-constant-fold.mjs (+ .d.mts) because it is the half that fails SILENTLY: a broken scan stops printing findings, a broken fold just shrinks the table and still prints a clean summary. RED-FIRST, every mutation applied ON DISK and restored from the COMMITTED baseline: the post-fix plant of the same typed 12 gives rc 1 'types 12, which this module already has as FG_PAGE_FRAMES'; neutering the helper-call arm reddens 4 of 18 rows; removing the fixpoint reddens the dependency-order row; restoring the integer drop reddens 4; silencing the near-miss tier reddens 4; deleting 'NOT FULL COVERAGE' from the passing line reddens the summary row; unwiring the gate from package.json reddens the wiring row. After: 568 / 3 (571), 8481 / 9 (8490), exit 0.
