title: The shared isolation proof asks "is there nothing on :0?", which reads CLEAN during the exact escape it exists to catch; and the obvious replacement reads clean too, because the CLIENT end of a unix socket has no address.
detail: THE DEFECT. The suite's isolation proof confines a PROCESS while leaving it a path to the owner's screen that nothing in the proof looks at. The oracle lane's 2026-08-29 record has all four facts at once: DISPLAY=:91 set, the window on his real screen, the log saying "Wayland window", python-xlib finding ZERO windows on the Xvfb. "Nothing on :0" was true and meant nothing, because the escape route was not X11. Closed by isolating the SURFACE: the display-server sockets the launched tree actually holds, read from /proc/<pid>/fd, never an environment variable read back as evidence. THE FINDING, and it is a defect in the FIRST DRAFT OF THIS CHECK, caught ONLY because the RED row is required to reproduce and refused to. A connecting client's unix socket carries NO ADDRESS: unix_stream_connect copies the listener's address onto the ACCEPTED socket. Measured — a window-less Electron launched the pre-2026-08-30 way put two fresh /run/user/1000/wayland-0 rows in /proc/net/unix and NOT ONE fd in our own tree pointed at either, stable across 8 samples over 20s; those rows are the COMPOSITOR's ends, and the escaping app's own fds were St 03 rows with no path, indistinguishable from the mojo socketpairs beside them. BOTH HALVES WRONG TOWARDS A PASS: the escape was invisible, AND a "presence" was available anyway because the Xvfb we launched is inside our own tree and holds its own listening socket. Verdict read ISOLATED with the app on his compositor, never having spoken to the Xvfb. THE FIX. unixPeerMap() reads the kernel unix_diag table (ss -x -a -n) for inode -> peer inode; the path still comes from the single /proc/net/unix reader. surfaceCensus resolves an fd DIRECT (listener/accepted end — how the Xvfb appears) or via PEER (connecting end — the only way an escape is visible), and refuses to answer without the peer table. surfaceVerdict requires the positive presence to come from a process that is NOT the Xvfb. MEASURED, one run, 14/14, elapsed 15.6s, box uptime 59.5h, load 23.00 22.74 17.82. [r1] RED: pid 4167374 fd 41,42 -> /run/user/1000/wayland-0 via peer, and the app reported the owner's monitors 2844x1600@1.35 and 1920x1080@1 while we asked Xvfb for 1001x777. [r2] THE THESIS: with DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY BOTH deleted the environ audit reads DISPLAY=:101 WAYLAND_DISPLAY=null — perfectly clean — and pid 4174160 holds both compositor connections anyway (libwayland's literal wayland-0 fallback). [w1] WINDOWED, the case HAZARD 5 could only INFER: python-xlib on our Xvfb :101, screen 1001x777, window id 2097155 1000x776+0+0 viewable WM_NAME "Aurora" class electron/Electron. [w2] that live 11-process tree holds /tmp/.X11-unix/X101 only, no compositor socket. [b1..b7] every blind path driven for real, each landing UNKNOWN never a pass, including [b6] the missing peer table and [b7] our X socket held ONLY by the Xvfb we started (the RED run's own shape). THE RED, THREE WAYS. (a) [r1]/[r2] are permanent rows: if the unpinned launch ever fails to reach the compositor the file reports UNMEASURABLE and fails, saying the green rows prove nothing. (b) MUTATION on disk before its red run — pinOzoneToX11 neutered to `return args` — run --windowless-only, 10/12 exit 1, [g1] flipped ISOLATED -> ESCAPED naming pid 84407 fd 41,43 -> /run/user/1000/wayland-0, [s1] red at position -1; restored from committed baseline e89ee80c and verified gone. (c) THE INTERLOCK WATCHED REFUSING WITHOUT THE MUTATION: [s1] inspects the exact argv about to carry a window and REFUSES the windowed rows when the pin is absent. Proving that by mutating the guard and then running the windowed rows would leave an unpinned windowed Electron one interlock-bug away from his live desktop — the interlock is the thing under test, so it cannot also be the thing relied on. SURFACE_PROOF_FORCE_UNPINNED=1 falsifies only the proof's view of the argv, guard intact, refusal branch spawns nothing: 11/14 with FAIL [s1] and REFUSED [w1]/[w2], no window launched. SAFETY. Every launch through spawnGuarded except the two RED rows, which must not be guarded and are WINDOW-LESS (lib/ozone-probe-app creates no BrowserWindow, so an Electron that attaches to his compositor still presents nothing to it — HAZARD 5's own precedent). No uinput, no xdotool/ydotool/wtype/dotool/xte; this proof dispatches NO input at all. The only display it names comes from the argv of an Xvfb inside its own tree; xvfb_window_census.py takes the display as a required argument with no default and has no code path reaching :0. The compositor path is derived from our own inherited XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/WAYLAND_DISPLAY — his runtime directory is never listed or globbed. STILL INFERRED, stated because HAZARD 5's honesty about its own limits is the standard: (1) the UNPINNED WINDOWED case is not measured and must not be while he is logged in — every red row here is window-less; (2) ISOLATED is a claim about unix-domain display sockets only, a TCP X display would land in the unresolved bucket (not reachable here: xvfb-run starts Xvfb -nolisten tcp, and the unresolved count prints every run); (3) it is a point-in-time reading, not continuous — an app that connected AFTER the census would pass; (4) the unresolved bucket is argued from the mechanism, not verified per fd; (5) ss is a new hard dependency, absent = BLIND not a pass ([b6] drives it) but no box without iproute2 was tested; (6) not wired into npm test on purpose (four Electron launches, ~16s), so the guarantee is about the shared guard module rather than each of ~110 harness runs; (7) only HAZARD 5's comment was updated — the suite's shared "nothing on :0" proof lives in another repo and its readers still get the answer this parcel says is not evidence. TAGGED for foreground. HAZARD 5 in scratchpad/lib/harness-guard.mjs updated where the measurement changed what it can claim: the paragraph saying the windowed case is INFERRED now records the windowed measurement, keeps the unpinned-windowed case explicitly untested, and adds that the environ read is not the instrument. Regressions green with the module changed: check-harness-guards 252/252 clean 0 failures (declared allow-raw-launch), harness-guard-proof 16/16, xvfb-reap-proof 22/22, check-cited-paths / check-doc-citations / check-peer-path-literals / check-prose-constants / check-ledger-timestamps all OK. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED. [state normalised at landing: this row was appended as 'closed', a value no other row in this ledger uses. The vocabulary here is open/fixed/holds/refuted/parked, and an unrecognised value is counted by nothing -- the overseer's own 'N fixed of M' summary groups by state, so a stray value silently drops a row out of BOTH halves of the count. Same defect the lane-status checker catches for the board, one file over, and this ledger has no such checker.]

title: The effects tree's two largest named files are now planted and counted; preset.ts and the five small advisory modules are still unplanted, and a run that never reached vitest scored nine false kills before anything else here was true.
detail: CLOSED BY docs/reviews/2026-09-09-guard-residue-scene-ui.md (branch parcel/guard-residue-scene-ui, base d9fbf105, tip 41fea818): section-wiring.ts and scene-ui.ts, the two files the 10:44 row named for itself. 63 plants applied, 4 shown not to discriminate and removed from the denominator, 59 scored: 39 killed, 20 survived (66%). Every plant scored against the WHOLE npm test. All 20 survivors closed by 19 new rows across two files with ZERO SOURCE LINES CHANGED, each proven red-first with the mutation quoted from disk and restored from a committed baseline. npm test 8463 -> 8482 passed, exit 0 both ends, 570 -> 571 files all collected. READ SECTION 0 FIRST, BECAUSE EVERY FIGURE DEPENDED ON IT: nine scene-ui plants in a row scored KILLED and all nine verdicts were VOID. npm test runs fourteen check scripts and a typecheck before vitest, and check-test-dashes refused a U+2014 in an assertion MESSAGE in a file THIS PARCEL had committed twenty minutes earlier, so the run exited 1 at the twelfth script and vitest never started. The driver's rule was rc != 0 => KILLED, and a run that dies before any assertion executes is indistinguishable from one that judged them all. WHAT EXPOSED IT WAS A PREDICTION FAILING IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION: two of the nine were plants I had reasoned could not discriminate at all, so being told they were caught was not plausible and the logs got read. A GREEN BASELINE IS NOT A CONTROL FOR THIS - the poison arrived in a mid-parcel commit, so the check has to be per-run; the driver now scores UNMEASURABLE, not KILLED, unless the log carries vitest's own Test Files line, and it fired again on a genuine typecheck error. All nine were re-run and became six survivors and three kills. THE CORRECTING GUARD, which is what this parcel was asked to answer. clampRowRemapPlaneY repairs rather than refuses; six plants, one non-discriminating, five scored, two killed. The method is NOT blind to a correcting guard - the mutation applies and scores identically - but its observable set is structurally smaller: when a REFUSAL is widened the bad value survives the control and meets the codec, which holds the same rule out of the same schema, but when a CLAMP is wrong the number it returns is (everywhere except at the range edge) a number the codec ACCEPTS, indistinguishable afterwards from one the author typed, and nothing records that it was corrected. So the validator can catch a clamp that corrects OUT of range and can never catch one that corrects to the wrong value INSIDE it. MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: rowRemapFromToggle's row runs the seeded document through the codec, and that is what killed the ceiling-off-by-one (plane_y 512, refused); it caught nothing in the non-finite fallback, the deleted non-finite arm or round-to-trunc, where the corrected value stays legal. Consequences: a direct unit row is the ONLY instrument a correcting guard has, and 'a comfortable distance from the edge' is strictly worse here than on a refusal (which can still be caught through a caller that renders the sentence) - the clamp's two existing points sat 1000 from their bounds and the new rows probe at min-1, min, max, max+1. FOUR PLANTS PROVED NOT TO DISCRIMINATE, each given a LOUD row that goes red the day its precondition ends rather than being dropped: the clamp reading vsplit's bounds (both nodes are 0..511 today, and it is the exact defect its own docblock is written against), isValidSceneId reusing the module RegExp (the pattern carries no flags, so .test is stateless), and rowRemapHeightShiftRefusal's membership test plus its contiguity arm (the enum is a singleton, so the range IS the set and the length===1 arm short-circuits ahead of it). A docblock can correctly identify a hazard and be guarding against a divergence that has not happened yet. title: The UX seat pair ran on aurora: two independent seats, 15 findings, and the one they AGREED on was the rig rather than the app.
detail: Seats dispatched cold in separate worktrees with separate displays, ports, builds and project copies; each judged by the standard it wrote itself before the shared text existed. Seat A: five newcomer jobs, all five completed, 20m09s, 30 screenshots, README.md the only document read, every result verified against bytes on disk. Six findings ranked by time burned, two predicted and labelled, twelve binned. Seat B: 46 of 88 panels as a CENSUS with every unwalked panel named (S1 7/12, S2 11/17, S3 10/25, S4 3/8, S5 4/11, S6 11/15), 9 findings of 41 observations, 32 binned and listed, plus a separate inspection-hazard list. CONVERGENCES: (C1) the save contract is invisible AND its one advertised remedy is a silent no-op -- A knew the gesture was undiscoverable, B knew it silently failed, neither could have said both; (C2) the art composer writes wider and less reversibly than it looks -- 14 pixels in an UNUSED tile rewrote two .nem files (+329 bytes) for A, and for B a paint stroke moved the canvas hash with Undo already disabled against a matched sprite-canvas control that undid perfectly. (C3) IS THE TRAP: both seats hit the native file dialog, and agreement would have filed a serious app defect that the controller then proved was the rig -- a twelve-line Electron script with none of Aurora's code reproduces it. Convergence is evidence about REPRODUCIBILITY, never about CAUSE; a shared environment is a shared confound. Reconciliation at docs/reviews/2026-09-09-uxpair-reconciliation.md; attribution at docs/reviews/2026-09-09-rig-native-dialog-blindspot.md. Seat B's F1 is deliberately RE-FRAMED before becoming a fix row: ComposerCanvas has several commit paths and bgOverride is demonstrably undoable with a test, so the defect is path-specific and 'the art canvas has no undo' would be fixed against the wrong thing.
convergence: C1 save contract (A-F2 + B-F3/F7); C2 art composer writes (A-F3 + B-F1/F8); C3 native dialog -- AGREED AND WRONG, attributed to the rig
dispositions: PARCEL parcel/uxpair-findings, base be742845, dispositioned four of the pair's remaining findings and left the rest. B-F8 art document destroyed by a project switch: REFUTED as a UI defect, HOLDS as a debug-door observation. The seat switched through __dbg.openDir, whose whole body is classicProjectStore.openDirectory called raw; the user's road has awaited confirmProjectOpen() since f0e15731 (2026-08-16), three weeks BEFORE the walk, and that guard's snapshot has carried artDirty since the same commit. Census of every production caller of the two switch primitives: useProject.openPath GUARDED (and every UI entry funnels into it -- both Open Project buttons, the Home switch, the recents rows, the palette's open-project and recent: commands); debug-hooks UNGUARDED, debug builds only; agent-handler guarded BY REFUSAL; ProjectSetupTab re-opens the already-open dir so the session key never changes and resetProjectRuntime never fires. That census lived only in a comment, so a new caller would reproduce F8 FOR REAL in the UI with no row noticing -- it now runs, plus a row asserting the composer document's PIXELS survive a cancelled open rather than its dirty FLAG. The Untitled Sprite half is not a defect: it had no edits, so endDocumentSession closing it is the documented cross-project-write guard. B-F5 the Explorer filter deletes the panel's only control: FIXED. The panel is the Explorer sidebar, the control is the button labelled 'Open Project...'; the render condition carried a query.trim() === '' term, so three characters removed it. The rule moved to explorerEmptyState in core/shell/explorer.ts (this suite has no jsdom and vitest collects .test.ts only, so a .tsx row would not even be collected) and three rows read Explorer.tsx as text to hold the seam. 'No matches' unchanged in behaviour AND wording -- the seat's second half, that it misdescribes a state with nothing to match, is a wording call and is PARKED. B-F4 the emulator badge produces no visible response: FIXED, with the client STUBBED and no socket opened. The badge renders bus status verbatim when not connected, so a refused connect walks disconnected->connecting->disconnected and ends on the label it started from; the error reached only the button's title. connect() now toasts on a non-connected outcome, relaying the main process's sentence verbatim and saying so when there is none. The raw-errno wording of one of the two refusals is the main process's call and is PARKED; the half that outranks it, that neither message was SHOWN, is closed. A-F3 14 pixels rewrote two .nem files for +329 bytes: CAUSE DETERMINED, fix PARKED. Two files because a Sonic 1 act's tile pool is the CONCATENATION of its .nem files (GHZ is the only multi-file zone, all three acts) and writeS1Level re-encodes and emits every pristine file 'patched or not' to preserve the split. Grew because Aurora's nemesisCompress is not the original encoder: measured live on the vendored fixture, both sides, 8x8 - GHZ2.nem is 5031 on disk and 5193 re-encoded with ZERO edits -- exactly the after-size the seat measured, and tile $30 is in GHZ1's span so GHZ2 was never patched. GHZ1 is 5727 -> 5881 with zero edits against the seat's 5894. So ~316 of the 329 bytes (96%) is encoder overhead on bytes that did not change and ~13 is the drawing. NOT FIXED because the one-line candidate is not mechanical: planted, it kills 23 rows across 2 files, 20 of them PRE-EXISTING s1-io rows that pin 'emit every art file' as a contract, and it collides with the save contract -- with nothing emitted saveClassicWriteResult answers 'nothing' and its caller's nothing-arm does not clear the dirty domains, so a Ctrl+S after paint-and-undo would go silent. Four options and a recommendation (b then c) in the packet. PLANTS: 13, nine predicted kills all killed, four predicted NON-discriminators all survived. P4 is the one worth naming -- rewriting the unsaved-changes dialog's BODY COPY left all 36 rows of the two open-guard files green, so that copy is unpinned BY THEM (a scoped claim, not a suite-wide one). npm test at BOTH ends, rc=0 both: base 581 passed | 3 skipped (584 files) / 8714 passed | 9 skipped; tip 585 | 3 (588) / 8745 | 9. +4 files, +31 tests, all mine, and zero phantom React failures in this worktree at either end. GREP CANARY FIRED: grep here is a function wrapping ugrep --ignore-files, so a token in a gitignored directory returns a clean zero; every absence measured here is under src, test or docs, all tracked, and the census walks with readdirSync rather than grep. NOT REACHED: no live app, no CDP, no ROM (the owner is screen-recording); F5 and F4 are held at the pure-rule/store layer and observe no rendered pixel; seat B's F1/F2/F6/F9 and seat A's F1/F2/F4/F5/F6 are untouched; every look call including d-38 is written up, not picked.

title: Seat B's F1 HOLDS, and it is the DOC-LOCAL path, not "the art canvas": the composer's own live-tile path undoes the identical gesture at the identical pixel, seconds apart, in the same run. The FIX is parked on a design question about where a transient document's history lives.
detail: THE REFRAME WAS NECESSARY AND THE FINDING SURVIVED IT. Seat B filed "a paint stroke in the Art composer cannot be undone"; ComposerCanvas.commitWrites has four commit paths and its own docblock claims bgOverride is undoable with a green test (band-art-undo-stack.test, 6/6 on this branch), so a fix aimed at the headline would have been aimed at the wrong thing. CENSUS, read from ComposerCanvas.tsx:196-395 in full and cross-checked with a search: P1 live-tile -> executeCommand set-tileset-tiles (:335), UNDOABLE on the zone-art stack. P2 bgOverride -> executeCommand on the ACT stack (:238), UNDOABLE. P3a chunk doc, atlas-backed cells -> executeCommand batched (:278), UNDOABLE. P3b chunk doc, empty/local cells -> setPixels + markOpenDirty (:284), NOTHING RECORDED. P4 doc-local -> setPixels + markOpenDirty (:295), NOTHING RECORDED. P5 applyTileCell (tile-stamp / collision / palette-apply, :356/:379/:388) -> NOTHING RECORDED, on EVERY document kind including the ones whose pencil IS undoable, and it never reaches commitWrites at all. Five openers land on P4 and on those documents EVERY write is doc-local: New Tile, New Block, New Chunk (art-facet.tsx:39/:52/:62) and the map's "Edit block..." and marquee->Block captures (MapViewport.tsx:4360/:1982) -- so a 16x16-tile region captured off the map is entirely un-undoable, which the seat could not have known. REPRODUCED, one app session, one canvas, two document kinds, four consecutive runs identical. dpr=1, canvas attr 64x64, rect {x:690,y:445,w:64,h:64} -- the same rect the seat recorded. The aim is the INTEGER client point (702,457) and the doc pixel is derived through PixelViewport's own floor((client-rect.left)/zoom) with zoom=8 recovered from the element, printed as (1,1); both rows aim at the same integer and land on the same doc pixel, well inside the canvas, so nothing rests on a fractional rect or a boundary. ROW B live-tile: 1523021819 -> 3126058246 -> 1523021819, Undo chip disabled true->false->true, focusedHistory().canUndo false->true. ROW A New Tile: 1523021819 -> 524852502 -> 524852502, chip disabled true->true->true, canUndo false->false. ROW B IS A STRONGER CONTROL THAN THE SEAT'S: the seat compared against the sprite canvas, a different store and a fair objection ("two different editors"); row B is the same ComposerCanvas, the same PixelViewport, the same PixelEditController, the same toolbar, the same pixel, seconds apart, differing only in open.liveTileIndex. The seat's sprite control still stands and was not re-run. CAUSE. focusedDocId() (editorStore.ts:613) resolves the art facet to zoneArtDocId(zone) unless open.bgOverride is set; it has no notion of a composer document that is neither, so no stack exists that a doc-local stroke could record on, and commitWrites' tail records none -- markOpenDirty is a SAVE signal, not a history one. commitWrites' docblock says "no command until save" and is accurate; what nobody wrote down is that for a New Tile / New Block / map capture that means no undo for the document's whole life. SECOND CONSEQUENCE, DERIVED NOT MEASURED, and the row I would drive first if this is picked up: Ctrl+Z there is not inert, it is aimed at the ZONE-ART stack, so with any earlier zone-art edit in the session it undoes THAT -- a change on a document the user is not looking at. The seat's stack was empty and so was mine, which is why it read as nothing happening. FIX PARKED, deliberately, as a design question: where a transient unsaved buffer's history lives, and what to do about the chunk document, where giving the doc-local half its own stack would put ONE document's gestures on TWO stacks -- the exact interleave this codebase already ruled against in writing when it created the bgOverride branch (editorStore.ts:637-643, "one document had two undo stacks interleaved by facet"). Three options and a recommendation (option 1: per-document composer stack for PURE doc-local documents only, covering P4 and P5, chunk documents untouched) are in the packet. IT TOUCHES SHARED PLUMBING ANOTHER PARCEL IS IN -- one branch in editorStore.focusedDocId() and a documentHistoryHub factory, while parcel/save-contract works on dirty-state and undo-history -- so it is flagged rather than raced. NOT ESTABLISHED, said plainly: P3 (chunk doc) and P5 (tile-space tools) are SOURCE-DERIVED ONLY, no gesture driven through either; the zone-art-misfire consequence is derived; the sprite control was not re-run. NO TEST ADDED and the reason is the bar, not laziness: a test asserting a doc-local stroke undoes would be permanently red until the design question is answered, and a new test here must be red-first against a FIX. The instrument is scratchpad/art-undo-path-harness.mjs, now registered as npm run harness:art-undo-path (check-harness-guards G6 caught it unregistered; 257/257 clean after), and it EXITS 1 today on purpose -- rows A2/A3 are the finding, row B is its own control, and it goes green by itself the day the fix lands. Method: spawnGuarded under xvfb-run, in-tree build of this worktree (root announced, NOT borrowed), VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1, hardlinked copy of aeon as the project (the live aeon tree is never opened), project opened through the debug door so no native dialog is involved, killTree in a finally. ONE ENVIRONMENT NOTE FOR THE NEXT RUNNER: a worktree has no node_modules, and symlinking the parent's breaks scripts/check-cited-paths.mjs -- its ignore canary asks git check-ignore about a path under node_modules/ and git answers "fatal: pathspec is beyond a symbolic link" (128), so the gate exits 2 COULD NOT MEASURE. Scaffolding, not this branch: with the symlink removed the same command prints OK. A SECOND INSTRUMENT HAZARD, measured in this shell because a peer measured the opposite in theirs the same minute: `grep` here is a shell function from a Claude Code shell snapshot that honours ignore files -- a canary string in dist/_canary.txt (proved ignored by git check-ignore -v) returned 0 from `grep -rl` and 1 from `command grep -rl`. Nothing in this census lives in an ignored path, and the cross-check was run with `command grep` regardless, because a search that silently skips a class of file makes a short census read exactly like a complete one. Gates green: check-doc-citations, check-prose-constants, check-peer-path-literals, check-scripts-dashes, check-harness-guards, check-cited-paths (symlink removed). NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted.

title: The save contract's four mechanical halves, each reproduced on a live window before it was touched; the fifth is a look decision and is parked for the owner.
detail: Branch parcel/save-contract, base c8652263. Closes the mechanical half of UXPAIR-AURORA-RESULT C1 (uxa F2, uxb F2/F3/F7/F9). FOUR PREDICATES, NAMED PER ROW, because dirty/unsaved/on-screen/on-disk are not synonyms: (a) the store believes, (b) the screen shows, (c) an ACCESSIBLE NAME a tool can read, (d) the bytes moved. R3 FIXED: the dirty dot was a bare 6x6 span with a title and nothing else -- no text, no role, no accessible name -- so a screen reader walks past it and a DOM scan finds a decorative element; measured pre-fix WITH THE MARKER ON SCREEN, aria-labels matching /unsaved/i = []. Now role=img + aria-label, title kept, nothing visual changed. A scan for the TITLE would have been green over this defect, which is why the row keys on the accessible name. R5 FIXED: dirtyActs is a monotone counter and UndoStack is argument-free, so an undo could not tell the store which way the document moved; BoundEditHistory's onCommand now carries a direction and dirty is DERIVED. THE NEAR-MISS: walking the counter back is sound only while every edit since the save was an undo step, and markDirty() is also called from mid-gesture paths that record no command, so 'place A, save, write a BG tile directly, undo A' would have reported CLEAN OVER UNSAVED WORK -- markDirty defaults to HARD and only the two command paths opt in, with a row pinning it. R4 FIXED (the loss half): disposeStacksForClosedTab rests on 'a closed document's stack is unreachable', true of a sprite and a canvas and FALSE of a level, whose document outlives its tab; measured pre-fix, close and reopen left the object present, the act dirty, and canUndo=false with Undo AND Redo disabled. Stack now survives while the work is unsaved; a CLEAN close keeps the old behaviour and that is a control row. R2 FIXED: Ctrl+S on a tab no saver owns was silent while the dot's own tooltip advertised it -- dirtyActs [ojz/act1] before and after, no message of any kind; the narrow routing STANDS and only the silence changed, via a pure rule over the same snapshot the dot reads. R1 RE-SCOPED RATHER THAN FIXED: 'Ctrl+S is a silent no-op on a level surface' is false with the level tab ACTIVE (the act file went ino=8781483 size=549 -> ino=8785043 size=708 and the dot cleared); the no-op's real condition is 'the active tab has no saver'. PARKED, NOT DECIDED: no Save control, no success toast, no close confirmation, no README line -- all one look decision, written up with options, costs and a recommendation (B then C, not D, because after R4 the close is non-destructive and an honest dialog there has no Discard button). VERIFIED: npm run harness:save-contract, a new committed instrument, 12/16 -> 16/16 rows 0 unmeasured, proven red-first by reverting the fixes ON DISK and REBUILDING -- exactly the four receipt rows failed and every control held. vitest red-first in two passes (4 failed | 8 passed, then 1 failed | 11 passed). npm test 8509 -> 8521 tests, +12 all mine, EXIT 1 BOTH ENDS: four component files fail at the base commit on this machine, 77 rows, all 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useCallback)', controlled by running those four alone with my changes stashed (identical 77 failed | 6 passed). BLOCKER FOUND ON THE WAY IN, fixed separately in b5f6761c: a build of this tree put a THIRD react copy into the project-runtime chunk, App imports it at mount, and the renderer died before painting -- window up, title Aurora, #root EMPTY, nothing logged unless CDP has Runtime.exceptionThrown enabled. Deterministic over five builds and present at three commits, so not a recent regression; resolve.dedupe took #root from 0 to 8211 characters. NOT EXPLAINED and said so: main aurora's dist/ from 08:07Z has only two copies and paints, from byte-identical sources and the same node_modules. THE VITEST HALF OF THAT DEFECT IS STILL OPEN -- resolve.dedupe does not apply to the node suite, and those 77 rows are the same second React instance.

title: A PURE doc-local art-composer document now owns one undo stack. FIVE openers, THREE writers, and a NAMED remainder: chunk documents' doc-local half is still one-way, so this is NOT 'the art canvas has undo now'.
detail: Branch parcel/art-undo-fix, base 9fd11455, tip 0a8816af. Closes ART-UNDO-PATH (docs/reviews/2026-09-09-art-undo-path.md) by implementing OPTION 1 of its section 4 exactly as ruled by the overseer and approved by the owner; options 2 and 3 were refused there and no part of either is here. THE DEFECT: markOpenDirty is a SAVE signal and was never a history one, and focusedDocId() resolved the art facet to the ZONE-ART document unless open.bgOverride was set, so a document that is neither had no stack a stroke could record on -- Ctrl+Z there was not inert but AIMED AT ANOTHER DOCUMENT'S STACK. THE FIX follows the sprite and canvas documents' precedent exactly, because that precedent already existed: one SnapshotHistory-derived stack per document id, minted on open, dropped on close. tabs.ts mints doc:composer:<serial> (a SERIAL, not a name -- two 'New Tile' documents are different documents and the second must not inherit the first's stack); core/editing/composer-history.ts is eleven lines of substance on the shared engine; artStore owns composerDocId + isPureDocLocal + setOpenDirty and the entire lifetime is two lines in openDocument/closeDocument; state/composer-history.ts is spriteStore's read/write/record trio one document kind over; editorStore gains ONE branch beside the bgOverride one. COVERS (and only): the five openers whose EVERY write is doc-local -- New Tile, New Block, New Chunk, the map's right-click 'Edit 128x128 chunk region' and marquee->Block -- across THREE writers: the doc-local commitWrites tail (P4), applyTileCell (P5, one step per DRAG rather than per cell, since it is driven off the host-pointer hook once per cell entered and has no natural batch), and the map clipboard's collision paste, WHICH IS NEITHER P4 NOR P5 AND IS COVERED ANYWAY. That third site was added beyond the letter of the ruling for a reason worth keeping: an undo of an EARLIER step restores the whole document, so an unrecorded write in between is not merely un-undoable, it is SILENTLY REVERTED by somebody else's Ctrl+Z. The three are now the complete set of writers of open.doc on such a document, enumerated with `command grep` over every ComposerDoc mutator. THE DIRTY FLAG IS IN THE SNAPSHOT, not derived from a counter as the save contract's R5 gave an act, because it is not monotone over document kinds: a New Tile opens CLEAN and a map capture opens DIRTY, so 'undone back to the start' means false for one and true for the other and only the start state knows which. Harness row D2 and one vitest row exist purely to hold the second direction -- a fix that cleared dirty unconditionally passes everything else here. ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THAT IS NOT UNDO: a tile-stamp that changes nothing no longer dirties the document (palette-apply and collision already returned early), because a write that dirties without recording leaves a flag no undo can walk back -- the shape of R5's near-miss. PROOF, both ways, in-tree build of the worktree with AURORA_BUILT_TREE and ELECTRON_BIN both passed, spawnGuarded under xvfb-run, hardlinked aeon copy opened through the debug door, killTree in a finally, dpr=1 every run, every aim an integer client pixel with the doc pixel derived through PixelViewport's own arithmetic and printed. GREEN 23 pass / 0 fail / 4 note (27 rows), was 9/2 at the census. A 1523021819 -> 524852502 -> 1523021819 UNDONE; B (the one-field control, same canvas, same toolbar, same integer point (702,457) -> doc pixel (1,1), differing only in open.liveTileIndex) byte-identical to the census run; C collisionA[0] 0 -> 12399 -> 0 with dirty false->true->false; D map capture 3069092495 -> 959760282 -> 3069092495 with dirty TRUE after the undo. NOT ONE ASSERTION IN A2/A3 CHANGED -- only the header's statement of what to expect and the epilogue that named them expected-red, which now names them as a regression list. RED on revert: the eight modified files checked out at base and the two new modules moved aside (444 deletions, quoted in the packet), rebuilt, 17 pass / 6 fail -- A2, A3, C3, C4, C6, D1 -- with every control (B1/B2/B3, C2 'the stroke lands', C5 'it dirties', every precondition) holding, restored from committed baseline c1826b29. D2 PASSED ON BOTH SIDES and therefore discriminates nothing on its own: with the fix gone the document simply stays dirty. Said so rather than counting it. THE HARNESS'S DISCARD ARM IS NOT DECORATION: with the fix reverted row A leaves its document dirty, so 'New...' raises the unsaved-strokes dialog and rows C and D would have failed for the wrong reason -- the red log shows it firing twice and the green log shows 'no dialog'. An instrument that only works on the green side cannot show the red side. NODE SUITE: 12 new rows, and THREE mutations each restored from the commit -- revert focusedDocId's branch alone 5 failed/7 passed, always-clear-dirty 2/10, no-dispose-on-open 2/10. TWO ROWS WERE VACUOUS UNDER THE FIRST MUTATION and were strengthened because of it (0a8816af): 'leaves a document that OPENED dirty dirty' and 'restores the document in place' both passed while the undo had gone to the zone-art stack and reverted nothing, because an undo that does nothing also leaves the flag set and the object identical; each now asserts the pixel came back FIRST, and that mutation went 3 failed -> 5 failed. npm test EXIT 1 AT BOTH ENDS and none of it is mine: base 77 failed | 8435 passed (8521), tip 77 failed | 8447 passed (8533), the same four files (aether-badge-identity, classic-map-wheel, map-device-scale, map-viewport-mounted), every row 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useCallback)' -- the node-suite half of the second-React-instance defect in docs/reviews/2026-09-09-save-contract.md section 7, still open, resolve.dedupe does not reach vitest. SURPRISES: the default collision brush paints AIR (selectedCollisionProfile 0 -> AIR_CELL), so the first row C measured 0 -> 0 and read like 'the tile-space writer does nothing' when it was the app correctly refusing an unchanged write; the tool survives a document change, so row C left `collision` armed and row D's 'pencil stroke' moved no pixel and looked like a capture-path defect until the pencil was re-armed and ASSERTED; the launcher's button says 'Block 16x16 px (2x2 tiles)' while 'New Block (16x16)' is the DOCUMENT's name; the census's 'Edit block...' is really 'Edit 128x128 chunk region'; and useAeonHistoryVersion() cannot see a composer stack by design, so writeComposerSnapshot must bumpDoc() itself or an undo moves the document and leaves the picture untouched. WHAT IS NOT COVERED is a separate row, ART-UNDO-CHUNK-SPLIT, and section 6 of the packet lists all six items. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted.

title: A CHUNK document's doc-local half is still one-way, deliberately: paste, cut, selection move, all seven transforms, every tile-space tool and the collision paste record nothing, and Ctrl+Z there still reaches the ZONE-ART stack.
detail: QUEUED, NOT FORGOTTEN, and not a gap in parcel/art-undo-fix but its explicit non-goal -- the overseer's ruling excluded chunk documents and said so in advance. THE REASON, which any fix has to answer first: a chunk document ALREADY SPLITS. A pencil stroke on an atlas-backed cell records a set-tileset-tiles command on the ZONE-ART stack (census path P3a), while its empty cells (P3b) and every allowCow gesture are doc-local. Giving the doc-local half its own stack would put ONE document's gestures on TWO stacks, so a single Ctrl+Z would unwind them in an order that is neither the author's nor either stack's. THIS CODEBASE HAS ALREADY RULED AGAINST THAT IN WRITING, in the comment that created the bgOverride branch in editorStore.focusedDocId(): 'Without this, one document had two undo stacks interleaved by facet (live-app finding F1, docs/reviews/2026-08-26-effects-foreground-checks-2.md)'. Re-introducing the interleave would undo a defect a previous LIVE finding closed, which is why the smaller fix was ruled and this was split off rather than bundled. WHAT IS ONE-WAY TODAY on a chunk document, enumerated: P3b (a pencil stroke on an empty cell); every allowCow gesture through commitWrites -- PASTE, CUT, SELECTION MOVE and all seven transforms (flip-h, flip-v, rotate-90 and the four shift-*); applyTileCell in all three modes (tile-stamp, collision paint, palette-apply); and the map clipboard's collision paste. AND THE SHARPER HALF, which is not merely 'no undo': focusedDocId() still resolves a chunk document to the zone-art stack (correctly -- its pencil records there), so Ctrl+Z after a doc-local-only gesture on one takes back some OTHER zone-art edit, on a document the author is not looking at. STILL NOT MEASURED, as it was not in the census: no row drives a prior zone-art edit, then a chunk-document paste, then a Ctrl+Z. That is the row to drive first if this is picked up, and it is the one that would say how bad this is rather than how it works. OPTIONS a future parcel has to choose between, none of them ruled: (1) move the doc-local half of a chunk document onto the ZONE-ART stack so the document has one stack again -- but a doc-local write has no command representation today, so this means inventing one; (2) split the document itself, which is a data-model change; (3) refuse the doc-local gestures on a chunk document and say so, which is honest and removes function. The parcel that lands it needs the same live proof shape parcel/art-undo-fix used -- scratchpad/art-undo-path-harness.mjs already drives a chunk document's neighbours and its C row shows how to read a doc's collision plane through __dbg.aeon.artDocCollisionAt rather than a pixel hash. NO EMULATOR.

title: The design half is now answered and built: case A (collision tables never loaded) REFUSES before any mutation and before the file dialogs; case B (a real bank with no full block) still imports and warns, unchanged.
detail: CLOSED BY THE OWNER'S RULING, not by my judgement. Decision `d-36b-air-collision-import-split-closed` in docs/decisions.jsonl, answered `refuse_a_warn_b`. The value half of this row was fixed on 2026-09-09 (findFullBlockShapeId deleted, lookupFullBlockShape's three-state result, the 0 sentinel gone from the chain); what stayed open was refuse-vs-warn, which changes what the button does and was therefore his call. It is now built. CASE A: `lookupFullBlockShape` answers `no-profiles` -- the editor could not look -- and `importChunkFiles` returns false at the TOP of the function, above the try, before addChunks, before markDirty, and before the three selectFile dialogs. An `error` toast names the three tables and every directory the loader probes. CASE B is NOT a change: `no-full-block` still imports and still carries the wording the earlier parcel corrected; I read it and it is right. WHY BEFORE THE DIALOGS AND NOT MERELY BEFORE THE WRITE: collisionProfiles is written only by openLoaded (setCollisionProfiles has no callers in src/), so nothing the author picks in those three dialogs can turn a null profile set into a bank. THE REFUSAL IS COMPILER-ENFORCED, which is the same move that made the split visible in the first place. chunkImportOutcomeToast now takes ProceedingFullBlockShape = Exclude<FullBlockShapeLookup,{status:'no-profiles'}>, so the blind answer cannot reach the success path; mutation M5 deleted the refusal and tsc went red (TS2345 at chunk-library-import.ts:213). A runtime guard would have gone quietly green. WHERE IT LOOKED IS DERIVED FROM THE LOOKER: core/project/aeon/load.ts gains COLLISION_TABLE_FILES (keyed by ROLE, so a reorder cannot hand the adapter the wrong table), collisionTableProbeDirs and collisionTableSearchPaths, and loadCollisionProfilesFa CONSUMES the first two, so the sentence and the probe cannot drift. A test drives the real loader against a recording FileAccess and asserts the message names exactly the directories it read. RED-FIRST plus FIVE MUTATIONS, each applied on disk and restored from a committed baseline. The one that matters: M1 moved the refusal to AFTER addChunks+markDirty (a rollback wearing the word 'refusal') and the MESSAGE row stayed GREEN while the state rows went red -- which is why the rows assert the project state and both dirty flags, not the sentence. M2 swapped the discriminator for the near-synonym (status !== 'found') and reddened exactly the two CASE B rows, CASE A green. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: the refusal does not say WHICH of the three tables was missing. The loader wraps all three reads in one Promise.all inside one catch, so that fact is discarded before anyone could report it; naming one would be inventing precision. Recovering it means allSettled and a richer return from a function whose deliberate null contract other consumers depend on -- a follow-up, named rather than hidden. FOUND ON THE WAY PAST, stated rather than fixed: mutation M4 renamed COLLISION_TABLE_FILES.solidity to solid.bin and 172 aeon-load rows did not notice. A `command grep` for the literal solidity.bin across src/ returns exactly two files, load.ts and the new test, so NO TEST ROUND-TRIPS A REAL BANK THROUGH loadCollisionProfilesFa and the loader's on-disk table names are pinned by the single assertion added here. NOT DONE AND NOT DRIFTED TOWARD: refuse_and_declare (a declared collision-bank field in project.json) was on the superseded card and was not chosen. It changes a format aeon owns and which their region work is about to touch; it stays a follow-up on their schedule. DECLARED GAPS: no DOM, so the button-to-function wiring, the toast being painted and the long refusal's wrapping are unproved (tagged for foreground); and `false` does not distinguish cancel from refuse, which is harmless today because AeonChunkActions.tsx discards the value. VERIFIED: npm test 77 failed | 8452 passed | 9 skipped (8538), rc=1, against a base 4e66b570 of 77 failed | 8447 passed | 9 skipped (8533), rc=1 -- +1 file, +5 tests, reconciling exactly. The 77 are the four pre-existing React-dispatcher files already recorded at this same count in docs/reviews/2026-09-09-save-contract.md section 6; none is touched by this parcel. Branch parcel/air-collision-import-split.

title: DRIVEN, AND IT REPRODUCES: on a CHUNK document a doc-local-only gesture followed by Ctrl+Z takes back an EARLIER ZONE-ART edit made on a DIFFERENT document, with the Undo control ENABLED and the canvas repainting so it looks like the undo worked. Severity raised from medium; the fix is still a design question and is still NOT applied.
detail: THE SENTENCE THAT WAS DERIVED IS NOW MEASURED, and it was true. ART-UNDO-CHUNK-SPLIT was filed at state open with its sharper half labelled source-derived: that focusedDocId() still resolves a chunk document to the zone-art stack, so Ctrl+Z after a doc-local-only gesture on one takes back some OTHER zone-art edit. Both earlier packets (docs/reviews/2026-09-09-art-undo-path.md section 3 and docs/reviews/2026-09-09-art-undo-fix.md section 6.4) said explicitly that no row drove it. This row drives it. WHY AN EMPTY STACK COULD NOT HAVE SHOWN IT, which is why two packets missed it: with nothing on the zone-art stack Ctrl+Z after a doc-local gesture does nothing at all and reads as undo is merely missing here. The discriminating setup is an ORDERING, not a gesture -- zone-art edit FIRST, then the doc-local gesture on the chunk document, then Ctrl+Z. THE CONTROL VARIES ONE FIELD. Rows C and T are the same chunk document (OJZ_00, 16x16 tiles), opened from the SAME library cell by the same double-click, the SAME two gestures at the SAME derived cell, the SAME integer client point (404,167) -> doc pixel (12,4) -> cell (1,0), in the SAME app session. The only difference is whether the setup row ran in between. THE NUMBERS. zoneArtHash() is FNV over the open zone tileset -- the zone-art witness, read from the tileset BYTES and not from any canvas, so it can be sampled while the composer shows another document. Setup: two strokes on a LIVE-TILE document (tile #0, opened by double-clicking the Tileset panel) took the zone from 628154474 -> 218895101 -> 3069218194, two set-tileset-tiles commands and so two stack entries. CONTROL (stack empty): pencil 628154474 -> 628154474 -> 628154474; collision 628154474 -> 628154474 -> 628154474; Undo chip disabled=true and canUndo()=false throughout. TREATMENT (same document, same gestures, two entries on the stack): the pencil stroke leaves the zone at 3069218194 and its Ctrl+Z puts it at 218895101 -- THE STATE BEFORE THE SECOND ZONE-ART EDIT; then the collision paint leaves it at 218895101 and its Ctrl+Z puts it at 628154474 -- THE STATE BEFORE BOTH. The undo eats them one at a time. AND THE AUTHORS OWN WORK SURVIVES BOTH UNDOS, so nothing they just did is what came back: doc pixel (12,4) 0 -> 1 -> 1 and collisionA[0] 0 -> 12289 -> 12289, identical in the control and the treatment. ENABLED AND WRONG, not disabled and inert -- the two are different defects and an author can tell them apart before pressing, so both were read. Control at the moment of the gesture: chip disabled=true, canUndo()=false. Treatment at the moment of the IDENTICAL gesture: chip disabled=FALSE, canUndo()=TRUE. focusedDocId() answered zoneart:ojz in BOTH rows, read from the app through a debug hook that calls editorStore.focusedDocId() itself rather than reasoned about. WORSE THAN SILENT, and this was NOT predicted by the source reading. OJZ_00 atlas-backed cells reference tile #0, which is the tile the setup edited, so when the treatment Ctrl+Z reverted that tile the composer canvas REPAINTED (hash 2836917162 -> 13661738). The author presses Ctrl+Z, sees the picture change, and has every reason to read it as my undo worked -- while their stroke is still there and a tile they edited earlier in another panel has been reverted underneath it. This is the strongest argument for the standing warning staying up. ANTI-VACUOUS CONTROLS, because without them the run is unfalsifiable. C3/T2b: the pencil stroke moved NO zone art, so it is census path P3b and not P3a -- a stroke on an atlas-backed cell IS a zone-art command and a Ctrl+Z taking it back would look identical to the defect while being correct. The aim is chosen from artDocCellAt (which cell is empty) and asserted. T0b: closing the live-tile document did NOT roll back its commands (zone still 3069218194 after the chunk was re-opened), so every row after it is measuring the undo and not the close. C7/T5a: the collision paint LANDS (0 -> 12289). TWO INSTRUMENT FINDINGS, each of which first read as a defect in the app. (1) A CANVAS HASH CANNOT MEASURE THE DOC-LOCAL HALF OF A CHUNK DOCUMENT: its atlas-backed cells are drawn from the zone tileset, so the undo that reverted tile #0 repainted the canvas while the DOCUMENT was untouched, and the first run read that as the stroke was taken back. The row now reads the documents own pixel through composer-buffer.getPixel. (2) THE TILESET PANEL SAT AT y=2796 IN A 1050px WINDOW, so the double-click meant to open a live-tile document hit nothing and the setup strokes landed on the CHUNK document that was still open -- making real zone-art edits through P3a and quietly staging a WEAKER version of the experiment (the other edit would have come from the same document). It still reproduced there (3709196434 -> 3784752349 on the same pencil row), but Z1 is now FATAL rather than a failed row, because a setup that silently degrades is how a weaker claim gets reported as a stronger one. STILL DERIVED, said plainly: paste, cut, selection move and the seven transforms (all allowCow through the same commitWrites tail the pencil row drove); tile-stamp and palette-apply (the collision row drove applyTileCell, the other two modes of the same function were not driven); the map clipboards collision paste; REDO -- only the Undo chips disabled was read, so whether the destroyed zone-art edit can be recovered with Ctrl+Shift+Z was NOT measured and it matters to how bad this is; and whether more than two edits deep behaves the same. NO FIX APPLIED, deliberately. The obvious wide fix -- a stack for the doc-local half -- is forbidden by this codebases own written ruling in the comment that created the bgOverride branch of focusedDocId (editorStore.ts): Without this, one document had two undo stacks interleaved by facet (live-app finding F1). WHAT THE MEASUREMENT CHANGES ABOUT THE OPTIONS: the root is now visible as an ASYMMETRY rather than an omission -- a chunk document is half live-editing and half buffered. Its atlas-backed cells write THROUGH to the project immediately as set-tileset-tiles commands on the zone-art stack; its empty cells and every allowCow gesture write into a buffer that reaches the project only at Save. focusedDocId is right about the first half and has nothing to say about the second. THREE OPTIONS, none ruled: (1) write the doc-local half through as set-chunk commands -- that type already exists with nametable and both collision planes (core/editing/commands.ts) and is already in ZONE_SCOPED_COMMAND_TYPES (editorStore.ts), so it routes to the SAME zoneart document P3a does and the ruling is respected rather than worked around; its cost is that a chunk document stops being a buffer and Save changes meaning, which touches the save perimeter another parcel has been in. (2) refuse rather than misaim -- answer null from focusedDocId while a chunk document is open so the chip is greyed and Ctrl+Z is inert; cheap and honest, but it removes the P3a halfs undo, which works today. (3) split the document, a data-model change, recommended by nothing here. RECOMMENDATION: option 1, and not as a mechanical change -- it wants the owners ruling first, the way option 1 of the census packet did. INSTRUMENT: scratchpad/chunk-undo-measure-harness.mjs, registered as npm run harness:chunk-undo-measure (check-harness-guards 259/259 clean). 31 pass / 2 fail / 5 note over 38 rows, IDENTICAL ACROSS TWO CONSECUTIVE RUNS. It EXITS 1 BY DESIGN while this holds -- T2 and T5 ARE the finding and go green by themselves the day it is fixed, and both the docblock and the summary line say so. Five READ-ONLY debug hooks were added for it and none is a fix: focusedDocId (canUndo says whether the focused stack has anything on it, which is precisely NOT the question when the suspicion is that a gesture and its undo point at different documents), zoneArtHash/zoneTileHash/zoneTileCount (every canvas on screen is a picture of ONE document and the whole question is what happened to a document that is not open), artDocCellAt (commitWrites branches per CELL, so doc-local is a property of the AIM, and nothing on screen distinguishes an empty cell from one holding an all-transparent tile) and artDocPixelAt. METHOD: spawnGuarded under xvfb-run, in-tree build of this worktree with AURORA_BUILT_TREE and ELECTRON_BIN both passed and the root announced, VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1, a hardlinked copy of aeon as the project (the live aeon tree is never opened), opened through the debug door so no native dialog is involved, killTree in a finally, node_modules a real hardlink copy rather than a symlink. dpr=1 every run; composer rect x=308 y=135 w=1024 h=1024, integral; zoom 8 recovered from the element as width divided by widthTiles times 8; the aimed cell asserted, not assumed. Evidence tracked at docs/captures/2026-09-09-chunk-undo-measure/. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted.

title: REDO IS MEASURED, and it is the good answer with a deadline: pressed straight after the misfire it restores the destroyed zone-art edit exactly, on both bindings and to full stack depth, without touching the author's own work -- and the author's NEXT real zone-art command truncates the redo side and destroys it for good. Tile stamp is now the THIRD gesture measured to misfire. Fix still NOT applied.
detail: THE ONE THING docs/reviews/2026-09-09-chunk-undo-measure.md section 5 left derived IS NOW DRIVEN. That packet read only the Undo chip's disabled and said plainly that whether the destroyed zone-art edit can be recovered with Ctrl+Shift+Z was not measured, and that a recoverable loss and an unrecoverable one are different rows. THE FOUR CELLS, all read from zoneArtHash() -- FNV over the open zone's tileset BYTES, sampled while the composer shows another document, because a canvas hash cannot answer this and section 5 of the packet shows the numbers that prove it. (1) DOES REDO RESTORE THE EATEN EDIT: YES, exactly -- 3069218194 -> 3765034709, bit for bit the value held before the misfire, and Ctrl+Shift+Z does the same as Ctrl+Y (rows R3, R10). (2) IS THE REDO CONTROL ENABLED AT THAT MOMENT: YES -- Redo chip disabled=false and focusedHistory().canRedo true, so the author is offered the control that would in fact rescue them (R2a, R2b). (3) DOES REDO INSTEAD TOUCH THE AUTHOR'S OWN DOC-LOCAL WORK: NO -- doc pixel (12,4) reads 1 after the stroke, 1 after the Ctrl+Z and 1 after the Ctrl+Y (R4). (4) A SECOND PRESS: IT KEEPS WORKING, one rung per press in BOTH directions -- three Ctrl+Z walk the zone art 3765034709 -> 3069218194 -> 218895101 -> 628154474 and three Ctrl+Y walk it back up all three, with the chips honest at both ends (Undo disabled=true / Redo disabled=false at the bottom, Redo disabled=true at the top) (R5-R9). THAT LOWERS THE SEVERITY OF THE MISFIRE AND IS SAID WITHOUT HEDGING: the immediate rescue is real, correct and deep. THE ROW THAT KEEPS THIS ABOVE COSMETIC IS X3, and it was not one of the four cells -- it is what the four cells made worth asking. A redo stack is discarded when a new command is pushed, and on a chunk document that is not hypothetical: the author who pressed Ctrl+Z, SAW THE CANVAS CHANGE and carried on working will make a stroke on an ATLAS-BACKED cell, which is census path P3a, a real set-tileset-tiles command on the very stack holding their rescue. Driven on the same document in the same session: doc-local stroke on cell (3,0), zone unchanged; Ctrl+Z, zone 3765034709 -> 3069218194, the misfire; Redo chip disabled=false, canRedo()=true, the rescue is there; pencil on cell (0,0), atlasTile 0, ATLAS-BACKED, zone 3069218194 -> 165717223, a real command; Redo chip now disabled=TRUE, canRedo()=FALSE; Ctrl+Y does nothing and the zone art never returns to 3765034709. THE EDIT IS DESTROYED FOR GOOD. So the shape of the whole defect in one line: the author is given a working rescue for a loss they were never told about, and it expires on their next brush stroke. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the loss becomes unrecoverable THROUGH REDO. The zone art is still whatever the last Save wrote to disk, and neither the reload nor the file route was measured. TILE STAMP, the one derived gesture driven here, and it was picked rather than drawn: a chunk IS a nametable of atlas tiles, so placing a tile into a cell is the PRIMARY authoring gesture on a chunk document and of the six still-derived gestures it is the one most likely to be performed on one at all. It behaves exactly as the pencil and the collision paint did -- cell (1,0) {atlasTile null, localId 1} -> {atlasTile 0, localId null}, zone unchanged (S2, doc-local), Ctrl+Z takes the zone 3765034709 -> 3069218194 (S3, THE FINDING, third gesture), the stamp itself survives (S3b), and Ctrl+Y restores it (S4). STILL DERIVED and named: paste, cut, selection move and the seven transforms; palette-apply, the third mode of applyTileCell; the map clipboard's collision paste; every route other than Redo for recovering the eaten edit; and everything about non-chunk documents. INSTRUMENT FINDING, and it first read as the finding itself: ARMING A TOOL CAN MOVE THE CANVAS OUT FROM UNDER A CACHED AIM. ArtToolDock renders eleven tools in a fixed column order, Pencil is first and Tile stamp is ninth, and clicking a dock button calls scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) -- scrolling to the ninth moved the composer rect from y=135 to y=172, 37px, while scrolling to the first did nothing. The first run reused a client point derived before that scroll, dispatched its press where the canvas no longer was, and got cell (1,0) atlasTile null -> null AND a Ctrl+Z that ate an edit anyway: a row that reads precisely like 'the tile stamp is doc-local and its Ctrl+Z misfires' while measuring a no-op followed by a misfire belonging to nothing. Every gesture's aim is now RE-DERIVED from the rect after the tool is armed and ASSERTED to be inside the named cell before anything is dispatched (armAndAim, the *aim rows). The doc pixel is invariant under this -- a cell centre is always (cx*8+4, cy*8+4) -- so the witness is the same pixel in every row and only the client integer moves. Same class as the previous packet's y=2796 Tileset panel: a setup that silently degrades is how a weaker claim gets reported as a stronger one. WHAT THIS MOVES ABOUT THE RECOMMENDATION: not which option, but why. Option 1 (write the doc-local half through as set-chunk commands so the document has one stack again) is still the one that leaves both halves undoable, and the Redo result is evidence FOR it -- the zone-art stack's redo side is already correct, deep and symmetric, so it is not a stack that needs fixing and the defect is entirely in what gets ROUTED onto it. Option 2 (answer null from focusedDocId while a chunk document is open, so the chip greys and Ctrl+Z is inert) is MORE attractive than it looked, because what it protects against is not 'an unrecoverable loss' but 'a loss the author will not notice in time to press Ctrl+Y' -- a greyed chip removes the window entirely, at the price of the P3a half's working undo. Nothing here argues for option 3. THE STANDING WARNING IS STILL RIGHT AND SHOULD GAIN A CLAUSE: Ctrl+Z on a chunk document is unsafe whenever the session has any earlier zone-art edit, the canvas will change in a way that looks like it worked, AND IF YOU REALISE, PRESS REDO BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANYTHING ELSE, because the next real edit takes the rescue away. NO FIX APPLIED -- the repair is the owner's ruling and changes what Save means on a chunk document. ONE read-only debug hook added and it is not a fix: canRedo(), focusedHistory()?.canRedo ?? false, the store-side twin of the Redo chip's disabled, read for the same reason canUndo() is read beside the Undo chip -- the chip alone cannot tell 'the app decided there is nothing to redo' from 'the chip is stale', and rows R2a/R2b and X3 rest on the two together. INSTRUMENT: scratchpad/chunk-undo-redo-harness.mjs, registered as npm run harness:chunk-undo-redo. 44 pass / 2 fail / 8 note over 54 rows, the PASS/FAIL block BYTE-IDENTICAL across two consecutive runs (md5 70f7b912b236f19691c920ad2c4145f6). It EXITS 1 BY DESIGN and both the docblock and the summary line say so: S3 and X3 ARE the findings and each goes green by itself the day it is fixed, while every recovery row (R3, R4, R5, R7, R8, R9, R10, S4) is written to PASS when Redo is a clean round trip and all of them do -- a harness that could only ever confirm the alarming direction would not be a measurement. METHOD: spawnGuarded under xvfb-run, in-tree build of this worktree with AURORA_BUILT_TREE and ELECTRON_BIN both passed and the root announced, VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1, a hardlinked copy of aeon as the project (the live aeon tree is never opened), opened through the debug door, killTree in a finally. dpr=1 every run; composer rect x=308 y=135 w=1024 h=1024, integral; zoom 8 recovered from the element; every aim an integer client pixel with the cell asserted, not assumed. Chunk OJZ_00: cell (1,0) empty (the doc-local aim), cell (3,0) the second empty cell row X needs because row S's stamp makes the first one atlas-backed, cell (0,0) atlas-backed for the P3a command. Evidence tracked at docs/captures/2026-09-09-chunk-undo-redo/. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted.
