title: Build & Run reloaded a ROM from an UNRELATED PROJECT under a green toast: the preference for the running ROM was right about its mechanism and unbounded on a second axis. Bounded to the artifacts this plan builds, refused by name otherwise, and the toast now names the path it reloaded. FIXED, both halves, with four planted violations scored.
detail: THE FIELD REPORT, 2026-09-09: Ctrl+Shift+B, 'build successful', the emulator reloads, and the chunk the owner had just changed is not in the game and he is not put back where he was. Measured, it was worse than a failed build: the build SUCCEEDED and wrote a fresh, correct aeon/s4.debug.bin containing his chunk, and Aurora then asked the emulator to reload a completely different ROM from an unrelated experiment directory, 2.5h old. A real reload of a stale file. The position was not restored because that ROM is not the build whose boot override the restore keys on. THE LINE: `const romPath = runningRom ?? join(plan.cwd, plan.romPath)`. THE COMMENT ABOVE IT IS CORRECT AND STAYS -- the plan's default is s4.bin, the emulator is usually on s4.debug.bin, and reloading the configured default there would swap the debug ROM for the release one and silently remove the symbols a feature depends on. THE DEFECT IS ITS EXTENT. The design means 'ask the running machine which FLAVOUR you are on'; the implementation asked 'what file is loaded' and never whether it was even this project's file. NOT INVERTED: preferring the built path is the same silent substitution the other way and would yank a user off a ROM they chose. THE RULE, and it is derived from plan.cwd + plan.romPath rather than from any literal: the running ROM is used iff it IS one of the artifacts this plan's build writes, full path, the pair being <dir>/<stem><ext> and <dir>/<stem>.debug<ext>, with the release stem recovered by stripping a trailing .debug first so a project declaring the debug artifact names the same pair. Classic gets debug:null -- build.lua takes no switch and writes one artifact, and an s1built.debug.bin is a file AS never wrote. THREE CANDIDATE RULES REJECTED, EACH BY ITS OWN ROW: path identity rejects s4.debug.bin against a plan whose romPath is s4.bin, which is the ONLY case the preference exists for; a bare basename passes two projects' s4.debug.bin, and in the incident BOTH ROMs were called exactly that, so the name is the least discriminating thing about the file; directory membership passes demo.bin beside s4.bin, since aeon's build writes both into one tree after the engine/game split. Comparison canonicalises through the DIRECTORY's realpath with the basename put back, so a symlinked checkout is not refused for a difference nobody can see and a never-written debug sibling still compares (realpath on a missing file throws); the resolver is injected, the shape buildPlanFor already uses for `exists`. ORDERING IS PART OF THE FIX: the classification runs BEFORE the flavour decision, because wantsDebug reads the running ROM's suffix and reading it off someone else's ROM is the same unbounded question one step earlier -- it decides which file this build WRITES. A foreign RELEASE ROM used to produce DEBUG=0. The refusal is emitted BEFORE emulator/pause, for the reason the unserved gate already gives in this file: stopping a machine and then declining to reload it leaves it frozen on someone else's ROM and looks like a hang. REFUSING IS THIS FILE'S OWN ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOUR, not a new preference: one gate up it already declines when emulator/status is unserved, with 'the build ran, but Aurora refused to reload rather than guess which ROM is loaded'. This is that ruling one axis over, where we KNOW which ROM is loaded and it is somebody else's. THE SECOND HALF IS SEPARABLE AND IS THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE: the result must NAME THE ROM IT RELOADED on SUCCESS, not only on refusal. Every link in the chain that misled the owner was individually honest -- the build did succeed, the reload did happen, the toast was accurate -- and the composite still told him his edit had vanished. BuildRunResult.romPath has existed in main since the reload path was written and src/main/aether/bridge.ts dropped it: AetherBuildResult in src/shared/ipc-types.ts had no such field, so the renderer could not name what it had just reloaded even in principle. It now crosses, and the toast reads 'Build succeeded (debug, fast): reloaded /home/volence/sonic_hacks/aeon/s4.debug.bin, back at (1234, 560) ...'. THE FULL PATH, NOT THE BASENAME -- both ROMs in the incident were called s4.debug.bin, so a basename toast would have read identically on the good day and the bad one, and the row 'is DIFFERENT for two ROMs that share a name' asserts exactly that. The old wording survives as the fallback when no path comes back, so a main-process bug shows as the sentence that was always there rather than 'reloaded .'. BOTH STRINGS IN THE PACKET WERE PRINTED FROM THE REAL CODE PATHS, not transcribed from source. A FINDING BEFORE THE FIX, committed separately at ff2b27b2: EVERY aeon row in src/main/aether/__tests__/build-run.test.ts paired a mkdtemp() project directory with a running ROM at /engine/s4.bin -- a cross-project pair, the literal shape of this defect, written into the fixtures of the rows that were supposed to be watching for it, and all 41 were green. (The classic rows already used join(dir,'s1built.bin'); only the aeon half drifted.) The fixtures now name the project's own directory and `dir` is a REQUIRED field of both fakes rather than an option with a plausible default, because a default is how this comes back; 41/41 still green against the UNFIXED runner, which is what makes it a fixture change and not a fix. RED FIRST at d899fb89, on the tree it fails against: Test Files 2 failed (2), Tests 10 failed | 45 passed (55), rc=1. The sharpest line is the toast row -- expected '...' not to be '...', two DIFFERENT ROMs and byte-identical toasts. Three of the green rows are green before AND after on purpose: they are the s4.bin/s4.debug.bin pairing the preference exists for, and a fix that breaks them is the wrong fix in the other direction. WHICH PREDICATE EACH ROW READS: every refusal row asserts the CALL LOG (reload_rom, load_symbols and pause all empty, romPath undefined), not the message; there is exactly one row about the wording and it is labelled as such. FOUR PLANTED VIOLATIONS, each applied to the fixed tree and reverted: basename-only rule -> 4 red incl. 'SAME NAME in a different directory'; directory-only rule -> 2 red incl. 'DIFFERENT artifact in the same directory' and 'gives classic no debug sibling'; TOAST reverted to 'emulator reloaded' -> 3 red renderer rows; and the one that matters -- REFUSAL MOVED TO AFTER THE WRITE, message still produced, foreign ROM reloaded anyway -> 4 STATE rows red and the MESSAGE row STAYED GREEN. That is the hazard reproduced on demand, and a suite asserting only the wording would have called the mutation correct. A SECOND DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY IN AND FIXED: with a connected server and nothing loaded, the fallback reloaded join(cwd, plan.romPath) -- the RELEASE name -- while the build had just written DEBUG (the default with no running ROM to read). It is now the artifact the chosen flavour actually produced, which is also the path the refusal names. Empty romPath from status is now 'no answer' (|| null, not ?? null). FOUR RESIDUALS NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT QUIET, and 5.1 is an OWNER CALL: a project declaring buildEnv.DEBUG='0' builds s4.bin while the emulator sits on this project's own s4.debug.bin, a FAMILY MEMBER, so it is accepted and reloaded and it is a file this build did not write -- the same byte-identical-game failure inside ONE project. Not fixed deliberately: the brief's rule explicitly admits the flavour sibling, reloading s4.bin instead is the substitution the preference forbids, and refusing would override a documented ruling that stated config outranks anything inferred. The fixture is one line. Also: the canonicaliser resolves symlinks and not mounts (a bind mount gives a LOUD false refusal, which is the safe direction and still a way to be wrong); no mtime check, so a family-member ROM that predates the build is accepted; and status's romPath is trusted verbatim once it matches. TOTALS BOTH ENDS WITH EXIT CODES, whole npm test chain (fourteen check-* scripts, then typecheck, then vitest): base 5c107282 rc=0, 574 passed | 3 skipped (577 files), 8584 passed | 9 skipped (8593); tip rc=0, 575 passed | 3 skipped (578 files), 8598 passed | 9 skipped (8607). failure-class: no failures at both ends. THIS WORKTREE SHOWS NONE OF THE 77 PHANTOM REACT FAILURES -- it had no node_modules at all and one was installed fresh (259 packages), so nothing here stands on a pre-existing red. LOUD-WHEN-IT-CANNOT-MEASURE was observed rather than assumed: an early filtered run that matched nothing printed 'skip-report: COULD NOT MEASURE' and 'failure-class: COULD NOT MEASURE' rather than a clean zero. GREP: this shell's grep is a ugrep wrapper; a positive control was run, and every population statement rests on that or on a Python str.count over the file's bytes -- the fixture rewrite asserts an exact occurrence count for all 27 of its substitutions and would have thrown on any miss. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted: emulator/status and the whole reload sequence are client calls, and every row drives a served fake, which is the pattern the existing rows already used.

title: Build & Run could still reload a ROM this build did not write, inside ONE project: a declared buildEnv.DEBUG builds one flavour while the emulator sits on the other, and the family rule accepted it. REFUSED now, naming what was built, what is running, which of the two the project's own config chose, and both remedies. Closes §5.1; §5.4's acting half closed with it; §5.2 and §5.3 restated with reasons.
detail: THE RESIDUAL, §5.1 of docs/reviews/2026-09-09-build-run-rom-mismatch.md, which that packet named as an OWNER CALL and did not take. Yesterday's parcel bounded the reload to the artifacts this plan's build writes; the hole it left is that A PLAN WRITES TWO ARTIFACTS AND A BUILD WRITES ONE. With buildEnv: { DEBUG: '0' } declared, the build writes s4.bin while the emulator sits on this project's own s4.debug.bin -- a family member, so accepted, and a file this build did not write. Same byte-identical-game failure as the field bug, inside one project, which reads WORSE because everything in sight belongs to one tree and so it looks like a bug in Aurora rather than a mismatch. THE RULING (owner's, 2026-09-09) AND THE OBJECTION IT ANSWERS. The packet hesitated because refusing looked like overriding the documented ruling that stated config outranks anything inferred. IT DOES NOT, and the distinction is the whole parcel: STATED CONFIG GOVERNS WHAT GETS BUILT -- wantsDebug is untouched, buildEnv still beats both the running ROM and the default, and nothing here changes which file the build writes or which listing is derived -- AND IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHICH ROM THE EMULATOR SHOULD BE HANDED, which has exactly one correct value: a file this build actually wrote. Both substitutions are silent, which is why it refuses rather than picking: reloading the running s4.debug.bin hands back a file the build never touched and the game comes back byte-identical; reloading s4.bin instead swaps the flavour under the owner behind a 'Build succeeded' toast, the substitution the running-ROM preference exists to prevent. Refusing is this file's own established behaviour for the THIRD time (unserved emulator/status; a foreign ROM; now the wrong flavour of ours), and it is emitted BEFORE emulator/pause beside the other two, because stopping a machine and then declining to reload it looks like a hang. THE RULE READS THE BUILD'S OUTCOME, NOT THE FILE NAMES, and that is not a stylistic preference -- it is the ONLY predicate that separates the refused case from the case the whole preference exists for, because THE TWO HAVE THE SAME FILE NAMES. romPath s4.bin + running s4.debug.bin + nothing declared = ACCEPT (the running ROM picks the flavour, the build then writes exactly the file that is running). romPath s4.bin + running s4.debug.bin + DEBUG=0 declared = REFUSE. Identical in every path they mention. So: flavourConflict = running.ours !== null && canonicalPath(running.ours) !== canonicalPath(builtRom). In practice it can only fire on a declaration, which is why the message can name one. THE MESSAGE, PRINTED FROM THE REAL CODE PATH (both the BuildRunResult.reloadError and the toast the renderer composes from it, the second carried through AetherBuildResult into useAetherStore.build) and reproduced in full in the packet. It does four things: names what is running and what was built AND SAYS WHICH IS WHICH (unlike the cross-project refusal these two paths differ by six characters in one filename); says the project's own config chose the flavour that differs, QUOTING THE DECLARED VALUE ('buildEnv.DEBUG is "0"'), without which the whole situation reads as Aurora malfunctioning; spells out both consequences, because a refusal that does not is indistinguishable from a bug; and NAMES BOTH REMEDIES WITHOUT PICKING ONE (change buildEnv.DEBUG, or load the built ROM in the emulator) because which is right depends on what the owner was doing. The build's own result is unchanged and still reported: ok true, exitCode 0, debugBuild false. ONE THING MORE THAN THE RESIDUAL ASKED FOR: declaredDebug is read BEFORE plan.envOverrides.DEBUG is overwritten with this runner's own decision. That field is the project's declaration on the way in and Aurora's answer on the way out, and a message reporting the second as the first would tell the owner his project.json says something it does not. PRE-FIX STATE MEASURED, not argued, by driving runBuild on the base tree: debugBuild false (the build wrote s4.bin) and reloaded true with romPath /tmp/aurora-build-rnXW42/s4.debug.bin, call log emulator/reload_rom:.../s4.debug.bin then load_symbols:.../s4.debug.lst, under a green result. RED FIRST at 14ecc671, committed on the tree it fails against before any source change: Test Files 1 failed (1), Tests 3 failed | 54 passed (57), rc=1. Seven rows; three red, FOUR GREEN BEFORE AND AFTER ON PURPOSE. An eighth row was added after the fix and shown red against the pre-fix source by stashing the source change alone. THE GREEN ROW THAT MUST NOT MOVE: 'still reloads when the running ROM chose the flavour itself' is BYTE FOR BYTE the first red fixture minus the declaration, and asserts reloaded true, reloadError undefined, romPath <dir>/s4.debug.bin and the literal emulator/reload_rom:<dir>/s4.debug.bin in the call log. Two more sit beside it: a declaration that AGREES with the running ROM still reloads, and classic is untouched (build.lua takes no switch, so buildEnv.DEBUG there is inert and the family has one member). WHICH PREDICATE EACH ROW READS: every refusal row asserts the CALL LOG AND THE RESULT STATE (reloaded false, romPath undefined, reload_rom/load_symbols/pause all empty), not the message. There is exactly one wording row and it is labelled as such. FOUR PLANTS, each applied to the fixed tree from a pristine copy by anchored substitution whose driver refuses unless its anchor occurs exactly once, and reverted: (1) rule compares to family.debug instead of builtRom, i.e. reads the PATHS not the outcome -> 7 RED including 'still accepts the release artifact itself' and 'drops to release when the emulator is on the release ROM', the legitimate cases such a rule costs; (2) reload target back to running.ours ?? builtRom -> 1 red (the symlink row); (3) attribution sentence deleted -> 1 red; (4) REFUSAL MOVED TO AFTER THE WRITE, message still produced and attached to the result, reload happens anyway -> 2 STATE ROWS RED AND THE MESSAGE ROW STAYED GREEN. That is the predecessor's hazard reproduced on demand, on the same file, one parcel later. A FINDING AGAINST MY OWN ROW, from plant 3: THE ATTRIBUTION PLANT WAS GREEN AGAINST THE FIRST DRAFT of the message row, which asserted toContain('buildEnv.DEBUG') -- and the REMEDY sentence ('Either set buildEnv.DEBUG in project.json...') contains that substring too, so deleting the entire attribution clause left the row passing. It now asserts 'buildEnv.DEBUG is "0"', quoting the value the fixture declared, which no other sentence produces. Same class as plant 4 one level down: an assertion that names the right SUBJECT can still be satisfied by something other than the thing it is about. Planting is what found it; reading the row did not. THE THREE SMALLER RESIDUALS, one closed and two restated rather than all three fixed by reflex. §5.4 (status's romPath trusted verbatim as the reload target) is CLOSED for the half that ACTS, and it falls out of the ruling rather than being extra work: reaching the reload line now means the running ROM is either nothing of ours or the very file builtRom names (the other flavour is refused above it), so the two spellings denote one file and the choice is free -- builtRom is derived from plan.cwd and absolute by construction, while the other was whatever string the server sent and would have been passed straight through if relative. Held by a symlinked-checkout row that is red pre-fix ('expected .../aurora-link-Atlo28/checkout/... to be .../aurora-build-jFML5Y/s4.debug.bin'). What REMAINS of §5.4 and is not closed: the string is still trusted as EVIDENCE, which is unavoidable -- it is the only report of what is loaded. §5.2 (symlinks resolved, mounts not) RESTATED, and the entry gains something it lacked: IT IS MEASURABLE WITHOUT PRIVILEGES, because a hard link has the same st_dev/st_ino as its target with a different realpath and a bind mount shares the superblock, so a statSync dev/ino comparison would close it and could be red-first tested. NOT TAKEN, and the reason is this parcel's own asymmetry: such a fix adds a new ACCEPT route, a false refusal here is loud and names both paths, and a false accept is the silent class that produced both the field bug and §5.1 -- buying a rarer loud failure with a new silent-failure surface, for a configuration nobody has been observed to run, is the wrong side of that trade, and it would land in the same commit as a refusal written BECAUSE silent substitution is worse than a stop. §5.3 (no mtime check) RESTATED AND NOW NARROWER: its own example splits, and the DISAGREEING half (running is ours but the other flavour, stale) is refused outright by this parcel before mtime enters into it. The agreeing half is unchanged, and the surviving silent residue is narrow -- a build that exits 0, leaves a PREVIOUS artifact in place, and reloads it; a failed build never reaches the reload, and one that writes nothing at all makes reload_rom fail on a missing path, which is loud. A cheap guard exists (existsSync(builtRom), or the artifact's mtime against the build start) and it is A DIFFERENT GUARD -- 'did this build write anything?' rather than 'whose ROM is this?' -- wanting its own red-first fixture and its own name, not a clause bolted onto a rule about ownership. Named so it is not lost. TOTALS BOTH ENDS WITH EXIT CODES, whole npm test chain: base 866a426a rc=0, 575 passed | 3 skipped (578 files), 8598 passed | 9 skipped (8607); tip rc=0, 575 passed | 3 skipped (578 files), 8605 passed | 9 skipped (8614). failure-class: no failures in this run (578 modules) at both ends; skip-report OK at both ends. The +7 is the seven new rows; no new file, so the file count is unchanged. THIS WORKTREE SHOWS NONE OF THE 77 PHANTOM REACT FAILURES: it had no node_modules at all and one was installed fresh (rc=0) before the base run, so neither end stands on a pre-existing red. GREP MEASURED WITH A CANARY, not trusted: this shell's grep is a ugrep wrapper carrying --ignore-files, and a token written into gitignored node_modules returned a CONFIDENT CLEAN ZERO from `grep -rl <token> .` (rc=1) while `grep -rl <token> node_modules` found it (rc=0); git check-ignore confirms node_modules is ignored. Every population statement rests on an explicit path or on a positive control (grep -rln classifyRunningRom src -> src/main/aether/build-run.ts). FILES: src/main/aether/build-run.ts (declaredDebug read before the overwrite, flavourConflict, the third refusal, romPath = builtRom) and src/main/aether/__tests__/build-run.test.ts (7 rows, one new describe). NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted: emulator/status and the whole reload sequence are client calls and every row drives a served fake, the pattern the existing rows already used.

title: FIXED as ruled: every gesture on a CHUNK document now records ONE step on the SAME zoneart:<zone> stack its atlas-backed pencil already used, so Ctrl+Z takes back the AUTHOR'S OWN gesture and the earlier edit made on another document survives. Both harnesses green and both shown red on revert. A chunk document is no longer a scratch buffer, and what Save and Discard mean on one has changed.
detail: Branch parcel/chunk-undo-routing, base bbff194b. Implements owner ruling d-37 route_onto_zone_stack exactly; option tell_the_author was a separate ask he did not answer and is NOT implemented (and is now moot as written -- there is no silent loss left to announce). THE DEFECT, measured across the two packets this closes: a chunk document was half live-editing and half buffered. A pencil stroke on an ATLAS-BACKED cell was a set-tileset-tiles command on the zone-art stack (P3a); its EMPTY cells, every allowCow gesture and every applyTileCell write recorded NOTHING while focusedDocId() resolved the art facet to zoneart:<zone> regardless, so Ctrl+Z reached that stack and reverted an EARLIER edit made on another document, one per press, with the author's own gesture surviving and the canvas repainting so it looked like it worked. THE FIX is one new module and four call sites. state/chunk-doc-commit.ts folds the open chunk document's contents into ONE step on that same history: a set-chunk against the library chunk (nametable plus BOTH collision planes), preceded where needed by the set-tileset-tiles that materialises the tiles the gesture painted. NO SECOND STACK IS MINTED -- set-chunk is already in editorStore.ZONE_SCOPED_COMMAND_TYPES, so it routes to the SAME document P3a routes to, which is what makes this respect rather than work around the written ruling in the bgOverride comment in focusedDocId ('Without this, one document had two undo stacks interleaved by facet, live-app finding F1'). focusedDocId() itself is UNTOUCHED: it was already right about a chunk document, and the defect was entirely in what got ROUTED onto the stack it names. FORCED, NOT CHOSEN: painting an empty cell materialises the painted tile into the zone tileset at gesture time, because a chunk in the library is a nametable of atlas tiles and pixels have nowhere else to live. It is the same sliceForSave Save has always run with the same flip-aware dedup, moved from Save-time to gesture-time, so the tile count after N gestures is the count Save would have produced; undo removes the appended tiles because they are in the same batch. THE FOUR CALL SITES: commitWrites' chunk branch (the atlas edits and the chunk contents now go in ONE batch, so a stroke crossing an atlas-backed cell and an empty one is one Ctrl+Z instead of one command plus one unrecorded mutation); commitWrites' allowCow doc-local tail; endTileGesture at pointer UP, not per cell, so a twelve-cell drag is one step; and the map clipboard's collision paste. PLUS ONE EFFECT THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: syncChunkDocFromLibrary, on the aeon history clock. Undoing a set-chunk rewrites the LIBRARY CHUNK, a project object the composer read once at open time -- without the re-sync the canvas would keep showing the reverted stroke AND the next gesture would diff against that stale document and fold the reverted stroke straight back in, an undo that silently undoes itself. GREEN: harness:chunk-undo-measure 39 pass / 0 fail / 5 note over 44 rows, exit 0 (was 31/2/5 over 38, exit 1); harness:chunk-undo-redo 46/0/8 over 54, exit 0 (was 44/2/8, exit 1). T2, T5 and S3 -- the three finding rows -- pass with their ASSERTIONS UNCHANGED. Treatment numbers: pencil zone 3069218194 -> 2936393219 -> 3069218194 (its own new tile, then back), collision 3069218194 -> 3069218194, doc witness 0->1->0 in BOTH the control and the treatment -- the one-field control is intact and now pays off the other way, because C and T behave IDENTICALLY where before the same two gestures destroyed two zone-art edits in T and read as inert in C. The redo ladder GAINED A RUNG (the author's own gesture on top of e1/e2/e3) and both sides walk all four in order on both bindings with the chips honest at both ends. RED ON REVERT, and it is a different red on each harness: ComposerCanvas.tsx checked out at base and chunk-doc-commit.ts removed (302 deletions), rebuilt -- measure 26/13/5 exit 1 with T2 and T5 red at the identical baseline numbers (3069218194 -> 218895101, then 218895101 -> 628154474, doc witness 0->1->1), redo 36/10/8 exit 1 with BOTH S3 and X3 red. Restored from committed baseline bc2b3489 and both re-run to exit 0; the green numbers above are the post-restore runs. THE RED PROOF REQUIRED A CHANGE TO EARN ITSELF: R1v's fatal check stopped the file the moment the misfire failed to reproduce, and inverting it naively would have stopped the file the moment it DID -- leaving S3 and X3 unrun, and an unrun row cannot be shown to discriminate. A returning misfire is now reported loudly and the run continues; only 'the press did neither' is fatal. ROWS RE-AIMED, none weakened, each annotated at its call site: C3/T2b/R0b/X0 said the stroke moved no zone art (it materialises a tile, so they now assert the witness lands on NO RUNG of the ladder, and C3 also reads zoneTileCount 919 -> 920 and the cell's new atlasTile 919); C5/C9/T3/T6/S3b said the author's gesture was NOT taken back (it is); C6 said Undo stayed DISABLED (the gesture enables it); C8 gained its second half; R1/R1v/R3/R4/X1/X3 staged or measured a victim that no longer exists; R5/R7/R8/R10 press FOUR times instead of three, asserting every rung the old rows did in the same order; S4 was VACUOUS after the fix (a stamp never moves the tileset, so its assertion held whether or not Redo did anything) and now reads the CELL. Both headers and epilogues rewritten: they said 'exits 1 by design' and now say a non-zero exit is a REGRESSION and name the row. ROW F IS NEW AND CLOSES A GAP NOBODY HAD NOTICED: of the THREE doc-local writers, two were driven and commitWrites' allowCow tail -- the one PASTE, CUT, SELECTION MOVE and all SEVEN TRANSFORMS share -- had no row at all. Row F drives it as a real gesture (one click on the options bar's Flip horizontal button, through the app's pendingAction handler), witnessed on the document's whole FIRST ROW OF CELLS rather than one pixel, because a horizontal flip moves art ACROSS cells and a single pixel can return to its value by coincidence. Measured: zoneArtHash 3069218194 -> 3522785170 (off every rung), Undo enabled, Ctrl+Z restores the row byte-for-byte and the zone art to 3069218194; on the reverted tree F3 and F4 both fail while F1 ('the transform LANDS') passes, which is the anti-vacuous half. TWO THINGS THE SOURCE READING DID NOT PREDICT: (1) THE WRITE-THROUGH DEDUPES, so repeated art does not bloat the tileset -- row X's stroke, the same single pixel at the same offset in a different cell, referenced the tile row R had appended and moved NOT ONE TILESET BYTE (395238756 -> 395238756); a row demanding a move there would have failed on correct, tile-saving behaviour, and X0 now tolerates and reports both outcomes. (2) THE READS HAVE TO BE TAKEN BEFORE THE PRESS -- the first version of C3/C3b sampled artDocCellAt and zoneTileCount after the Ctrl+Z and reported 'zoneTileCount 919 -> 919' with an empty cell, which reads exactly like 'the stroke changed nothing' while actually reading what the UNDO did. WHAT SAVE AND DISCARD NOW MEAN, and this is the cost the owner accepted rather than an oversight: a chunk document is NO LONGER A SCRATCH BUFFER. Edits reach the chunk library as they are made, as recorded undoable steps. Save is now 'publish this chunk into the act' rather than 'commit my strokes' -- its set-chunk is usually a no-op and the part it is still FOR is the act propagation (d-18c) plus the out-of-act report; saveComposerDocument is unchanged. DISCARD NO LONGER DISCARDS: the perimeter still asks (the dirty flag is set exactly as before) but 'Discard & close' throws away only the document, and UNDO is now the way to abandon work on a chunk. The zone tileset grows as you paint (one tile per newly painted cell; dedup means repainting claims no more, and undo gives it back). None of this touches any other document kind: the five pure-doc-local openers keep the per-document stack ART-UNDO-DOC-LOCAL gave them. STILL DERIVED and named rather than implied: the other six transforms, paste, cut and selection move (all reach the tail row F drives, through the identical commitWrites(writes, true) call, but no row drives one); palette-apply (the third mode of applyTileCell -- the other two are driven and the routing decision is in endTileGesture, which is mode-independent, but that is a reading); the map clipboard's collision paste on a chunk document; and NO VITEST WAS ADDED -- the two live harnesses are the specification and the red/green proof, and a node-suite row for commitChunkDocStep would guard the routing in CI where the harnesses do not run. That is the obvious follow-up. npm test: base bbff194b 4 files / 77 failed / 8452 passed (8538), exit 1; tip bc2b3489 7 files / 79 failed / 8431 passed (8538), exit 1. ZERO ASSERTION FAILURES AT EITHER END by the repo's own failure-class reporter, and this parcel adds no test so the totals could not move. The 77 UNCLASSIFIED are the same four files at both ends (aether-badge-identity, classic-map-wheel, map-device-scale, map-viewport-mounted), every row 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useCallback)' -- the node-suite half of the second-React-instance defect in docs/reviews/2026-09-09-save-contract.md section 7, still open. The 3 extra at the tip are TIMEOUTs in art-discard-guard, prose-constant-fold and harness-guard-profile, the same load-sensitive set docs/reviews/2026-09-09-art-undo-fix.md section 4.5 recorded; run together in isolation they are 3 files / 70 tests / 0 failures in 5.19s with the reporter saying 'no failures in this run'. art-discard-guard counts openDocument call sites and is exactly the file someone would suspect of being mine; it never reached an assertion. METHOD: spawnGuarded under xvfb-run, in-tree build of this worktree with AURORA_BUILT_TREE and ELECTRON_BIN both passed and the root announced, VITE_AURORA_DEBUG=1 rebuild after every source change, a hardlinked copy of aeon as the project, opened through the debug door, killTree in a finally, node_modules a real hardlink copy. dpr=1 every run; composer rect x=308 y=135 w=1024 h=1024; every aim an integer client pixel with the cell asserted. Evidence tracked at docs/captures/2026-09-09-chunk-undo-routing/. NO EMULATOR TOUCHED, none attempted.

title: The d-37 chunk-undo repair was guarded ONLY by two CDP harnesses that npm test never invokes, so the fix for a defect that silently destroyed the owner's edits could rot unnoticed. 30 vitest rows over commitChunkDocStep / isChunkDocument / syncChunkDocFromLibrary now run in the suite; five mutations of the repair each go red and three predicted non-discriminating plants stay green.
detail: Follows docs/reviews/2026-09-09-chunk-undo-routing.md, whose own section 5 named this as the obvious follow-up ("No vitest was added"). WHAT THE ROWS HOLD: (1) one gesture is ONE step on zoneart:<zone>, pinned from the state side by walking the stack to empty with undo(), not by a spy; (2) the step is a set-chunk preceded by the set-tileset-tiles that materialises painted tiles ONLY where needed, asserted in both directions (a collision paint and a stamp of an existing tile record a BARE set-chunk; a stroke wholly on atlas-backed cells records a BARE set-tileset-tiles and no set-chunk); (3) no second stack is minted (composerDocId stays null, the only document id the history hub is asked for during a gesture is the zone-art one, recordComposerEdit mints nothing) -- the codebase's own written ruling from the bgOverride branch of focusedDocId; (4) undo takes back the AUTHOR'S OWN gesture and leaves an earlier zone-art edit alone, the two halves of the original defect; (5) syncChunkDocFromLibrary, written as the fold-back property: WITHOUT it the next commit diffs the stale document against the reverted chunk and re-records the undone stroke onto the library chunk, WITH it the same commit records nothing; (6) a refusal to RECORD never becomes a refusal to EDIT (chunk gone from the library, and the tileset ceiling). WHAT THEY DO NOT HOLD, stated in the packet rather than implied: the DELIVERY (node cannot mount ComposerCanvas, so nothing proves a real gesture reaches commitWrites/endTileGesture, that the useEffect([historyVersion, open]) fires, or that a real Ctrl+Z reaches focusedHistory), and the PAINT (the original defect was silent precisely because a wrong undo LOOKED right). Group F is a SOURCE READ of the four call sites and the effect and is labelled as catching deletion and nothing subtler. The harnesses remain the specification. RED-FIRST, mutating the landed repair and restoring from the committed baseline daab0a1b (tree verified clean after, and the mutation script exits 2 on a missing anchor so an unapplied patch cannot read as green): M1 revert the routing to pre-fix 12 failed/18 passed; M2 invert the batch order 1/29, exactly the ordering row; M3 make the sync a no-op 2/28, exactly D1 and D3; M4 let isPureDocLocal mint a stack for a chunk document 18/12 (only three of those are independent -- the rest is one executeCommand throw propagating, reported as such); M5 drop `leading` from the refusal path 3/27. NON-DISCRIMINATING BY PREDICTION AND IN FACT, 30/30 green each: toast wording, the command description string, and sameWords' unequal-length guard (a real declared hole -- no fixture here resizes a chunk under an open document). npm test aggregate BOTH ENDS in this worktree: base 5f63a67f 575 files/8605 tests passed, exit 0; tip 576/8635 passed, exit 0; failure-class 'no failures in this run' at both. The delta is exactly +1 file and +30 tests. This worktree shows NONE of the 77 second-React-instance phantom failures the routing packet recorded in a different worktree.

title: Four of the seat pair's remaining findings: two fixed, one refuted as a UI defect and held as a door observation, one cause determined with its fix parked as a design question.
detail: PARCEL parcel/uxpair-findings, base be742845, dispositioned four of the pair's remaining findings and left the rest. B-F8 art document destroyed by a project switch: REFUTED as a UI defect, HOLDS as a debug-door observation. The seat switched through __dbg.openDir, whose whole body is classicProjectStore.openDirectory called raw; the user's road has awaited confirmProjectOpen() since f0e15731 (2026-08-16), three weeks BEFORE the walk, and that guard's snapshot has carried artDirty since the same commit. Census of every production caller of the two switch primitives: useProject.openPath GUARDED (and every UI entry funnels into it -- both Open Project buttons, the Home switch, the recents rows, the palette's open-project and recent: commands); debug-hooks UNGUARDED, debug builds only; agent-handler guarded BY REFUSAL; ProjectSetupTab re-opens the already-open dir so the session key never changes and resetProjectRuntime never fires. The Untitled Sprite half is not a defect: it had no edits, so endDocumentSession closing it is the documented cross-project-write guard. B-F5 the Explorer filter deletes the panel's only control: FIXED. The panel is the Explorer sidebar, the control is the button labelled 'Open Project...'; the render condition carried a query.trim() === '' term, so three characters removed it. The rule moved to explorerEmptyState in core/shell/explorer.ts (this suite has no jsdom and vitest collects .test.ts only, so a .tsx row would not even be collected) and three rows read Explorer.tsx as text to hold the seam. 'No matches' unchanged in behaviour AND wording -- the seat's second half, that it misdescribes a state with nothing to match, is a wording call and is PARKED. B-F4 the emulator badge produces no visible response: FIXED, with the client STUBBED and no socket opened. The badge renders bus status verbatim when not connected, so a refused connect walks disconnected->connecting->disconnected and ends on the label it started from; the error reached only the button's title. connect() now toasts on a non-connected outcome, relaying the main process's sentence verbatim and saying so when there is none. A-F3 14 pixels rewrote two .nem files for +329 bytes: CAUSE DETERMINED, fix PARKED. Two files because a Sonic 1 act's tile pool is the CONCATENATION of its .nem files (GHZ is the only multi-file zone, all three acts) and writeS1Level re-encodes and emits every pristine file 'patched or not' to preserve the split. THIS IS NOT A DEFECT IN THE FEATURE AND THE CODE IS HONEST ABOUT IT: the docblock says a refused file is 'subtracted a SECOND time', i.e. it is already excluded by never entering loadedPaths. The safety property holds today and the REFUSED row does test it -- via the load side. WHAT IS MISSING IS A GUARD ON THE GUARD. The agent's own M4 established the subtraction is load-bearing only under a FUTURE loader that wrongly admits a refused path to loadedPaths, and had to suspend a fixture invariant to demonstrate it -- so no standing row protects it. This repo has paid for exactly this shape before (O20: a gate resting on a neighbour is discovered the day the neighbour moves; every gate got a row asserting its own refusal reason, verified by deleting each gate in turn). REMEDY: one row that builds an Act whose loadedPaths deliberately contains a refused path -- the future-loader state -- and asserts it is still not removed. That row goes red when the subtraction is deleted and green otherwise, which is what the subtraction currently lacks. Cheap; no running app needed.

title: CONFIRMED and FIXED: a palette edit was discarded because there was nowhere to write it -- no serializer existed and the save plan named no palette file. Lines 1 to 3 now round-trip to the zone's authored palette in place; line 0 is refused by name.
detail: BRANCH palette-write-target, commits a2ca7b97 (implementation) / dd9928b6 (a vacuous assertion of my own) / 9e2eb070 (a second door onto line 0). NOT THE GRID-DIMENSIONS BUG AGAIN: that was a value living in two places and not copied between them; this was a missing DESTINATION. core/formats/palette.ts had parsePaletteLine and buildPalette and no inverse, and buildAeonSavePlan planned no palette file at all, so every colour the author picked lived in the model until the reopen and vanished in silence. WHY NOBODY SAW IT: the live preview pushes CRAM straight into a running game, so the emulator DID show the colour -- aeon's tools/ojz_common.py records the identical trap from the other side of the same file after its own six-month version of this defect ('THE LIVE PATH WORKING IS WHAT HID IT'). Every gate row therefore goes through disk. THE DESTINATION IS zones[].palette IN PLACE, with no editorPalettePath escape hatch and no retarget, which makes it the one art blob that does not follow this repo's editor-destination rule. That is the PRODUCER's ruling, not an omission: aeon declares games/<game>/data/editor/<zone>/<act>/palette.bin the ONLY authored copy, mirrors it into the generated tree on build, and its staleness gate watches data/editor/ specifically so an editor palette save re-bakes ('EXACTLY ONE WRITER, AND IT IS THE EDITOR'). Aurora is that editor and had never written the file. LINE 0 REFUSED, per the recommended refuse_line0 option of the owner's unanswered card PALETTE-LINE0-BLAST-RADIUS: serializeZonePalette starts its loop at ZONE_PALETTE_FIRST_LINE so it cannot emit line 0 whatever it is handed, the plan never names art/palettes/SonicAndTails.bin, and the gesture is refused at the grid with ZONE_LINE0_REFUSAL naming Sonic and Tails. The sprite pane's zone mode used to unlock it -- a control that reached neither disk nor the running game (palBaseOffset throws on line 0) nor the agent tool (validation.ts refused it). NOT OVERWRITING WHAT WAS NOT UNDERSTOOD: Zone.paletteFile carries the LOAD's verdict to the write path (the Section.unreadable / Act.sectionFiles shape, required not optional on the Notice.severity rule). A file shorter than the three lines is not written and the load says so as a 'warning'; a longer one keeps its tail verbatim. MEASURED ON THE REAL FILE: aeon's committed 96-byte palette.bin round-trips through the real buildPalette + serializeZonePalette with 0 differing bytes, so opening and saving an untouched project adds no churn and no spurious re-bake. aeon's live project.json was read the same day and names the authored path, not the generated mirror. GATE src/core/project/aeon/__tests__/palette-write-target.test.ts, 9 rows, all EXECUTED over the real loader, the real set-palette-line command and the real save plan, with expectations derived from the edit word. Ten poisons run red-first from committed baselines, each shown applied by git diff -U0 (P1-P8 in the packet). Suite 595 files / 8865 tests passed, 3 files / 9 rows skipped, 0 failed (baseline 594 / 8851). NOT MEASURED, TAGGED FOR FOREGROUND: nobody has seen the refusal tooltip on a screen or driven Ctrl+S in the real app -- no Electron, no CDP, no ROM build on this box.

title: A SECOND, QUIETER DOOR onto the shared player palette: the copy-to menu and swatch drop gated on `line === 0 && !inSprite`, so line 0 was a legal copy TARGET in the sprite pane while the grid's own policy refused the same write.
detail: FOUND BY A POISON THAT CAME BACK GREEN. After closing the door in a2ca7b97, restoring `&& !inSprite` passed the WHOLE suite -- 595 files, 8863 rows, zero red -- because nothing anywhere asserted the copy bridge's rule. The lock I had added was a defensive guard with no row that reddens on its deletion, which this repo files as a finding (cf. SWEEP-SECOND-SUBTRACTION-UNGUARDED, same week, same class). WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE SLIDER: a copy lands in ONE gesture with no slider to notice, and it was open exactly when the swatch grid was refusing the identical write. FIXED in 9e2eb070 by moving the decision to zoneCopyTargetRefusal(line, standaloneRow) in providers/palette-aeon.ts, whose argument list has no inSprite in it: reopening the door now means reintroducing an argument. TWO ROWS, both red under the re-aimed poison P7b -- an EXECUTED one in providers/__tests__/palette-aeon.test.ts (refusal for a zone row, absence for lines 1 to 3, absence for the standalone sprite row) and a SOURCE SCAN in art-shared/__tests__/palette-grid-wiring.test.ts pinning that the host still asks (no inSprite, no hard-coded line number), because a re-inlined `line === 0` would restore the fork with both files looking reasonable.

title: A gate assertion I had just written was vacuous: it took `body.indexOf('return')` for the refusal's return, but that lands on the `if (!z) return;` two statements below, so deleting the short-circuit stayed GREEN.
detail: SELF-FOUND, in the red-first run of the row itself. Poison P6b kept the zonePaletteLineRefusal(line) call in previewZone and deleted only its `return`, so a refused line 0 was warned about and then WRITTEN ANYWAY. All three index comparisons stayed true because a different statement supplied the keyword. THE RULE THAT CAUGHT IT: when a poison comes back green, suspect the MATCHER before the guard -- the identifier half of the scan was sound, the ordering half was measuring the wrong statement. FIXED in dd9928b6 by anchoring the span instead of comparing free indices: between the refusal call and the first thing that touches the zone (getCurrentZone) there must be a `return;`, and nothing else in the callback can supply it. Re-run: RED under P6b, RED under P6 (the call deleted outright), 27/27 clean.

title: A project.json whose zones[].palette names the GENERATED mirror rather than the authored file would have its palette edits overwritten by the next aeon build -- not by Aurora, but the author sees the same silent loss.
detail: NOT A LIVE DEFECT, recorded so it is not rediscovered. The palette write goes to whatever zones[].palette names, in place, because aeon declares data/editor/<zone>/<act>/palette.bin the only authored copy and MIRRORS it into data/generated/ on every build ('do not add a second writer of the generated file'). If a checkout's pointer still named the generated file, Aurora's save would land there, the round trip would work in the editor, and the next build's mirror step would replace it from the authored file. MEASURED 2026-09-10: aeon's live project.json names games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/palette.bin, the authored path, so the shipping configuration is not this one. The stale shape survives only in this repo's deliberately pre-change fixture, where the new 96-byte plan entry is now commented with this hazard. NO GUARD INVENTED: refusing a path by directory name would be a heuristic over a peer's convention, and the right fix if it ever fires is on the aeon side.

title: SUCCEEDS NUMBERFIELD-FOCUSED-CLICK-INSERT, whose mechanism I filed and which measurement REFUTED. The symptom is real and reproduces; the cause is UNKNOWN and must not be guessed again.
detail: WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: seat A's gesture yields 12872 on the FIXED build; Bot reads '1287' after ONE keystroke, so the caret inserted rather than the selection replacing. Three runs, byte-identical, at loads 7.8/10.5/11.8 on 16 cores. The value changed WRONGLY rather than never changing, which separates a reproduction from a click that missed. WHAT IS REFUTED, AND IT WAS MINE: I filed the cause as 'clicking an ALREADY-FOCUSED box collapses the selection to a caret'. A seven-variant census kills it -- variants B, C, F and G were provably UNFOCUSED at the click and INSERTED anyway; only the two COLD-click variants replaced. Not the already-focused click, not the Tab, not the keystroke gap, not a flush race. HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the shape matters more than the error: I read the source correctly. NumberField DOES select on focus and not on click -- that source fact is true and still true. I then treated a true mechanism I could see as THE mechanism producing the observed symptom, without running the experiment that separates it from the alternatives. A correct reading of code is not a measurement of behaviour, and it is at its most convincing exactly when it explains the symptom neatly. My row said 'NOT YET REPRODUCED, do not close it on the derivation' -- the caveat was right and the content underneath it was wrong, which is the part a caveat cannot save. THE ONLY LEAD THE DATA SUPPORTS, offered as a hypothesis and explicitly NOT a cause: the two variants that REPLACED are the two COLD clicks -- the first interaction with that field. Every variant involving a prior commit or a prior focus on the box INSERTED, including one with a 2s settle and one with no Tab at all. That is consistent with a re-render after focus rewriting the input's value and destroying the selection made in onFocus, but nobody has tested it and I am not filing it as the cause. NEXT STEP IS AN EXPERIMENT, NOT A FIX. The committed harness scratchpad/cdp-sweep-f4-harness.mjs already runs the seven variants and is registered; extend it rather than reasoning further from source.

title: The sweep's refused-file subtraction is defence-in-depth with NO standing test that goes red when it is deleted -- so a future refactor removes it as dead code exactly when it starts mattering.
detail: FIXED by one row in src/core/project/aeon/__tests__/grid-resize-roundtrip.test.ts (5 rows -> 6): 'the refused subtraction is load-bearing: a loader that admitted a refused path to loadedPaths still does not get it deleted'. THE EXACT MUTATION THAT TURNS IT RED: in save.ts's stranded-section sweep, replace the third argument of the removalsFor call, act.sectionFiles.unreadablePaths, with [] (1 insertion, 1 deletion). Under that mutation, on committed baseline 8612cb03, the run over grid-resize-roundtrip.test.ts + section-file-ledger.test.ts is Tests 1 failed | 11 passed (12), and the single failure is this row at THE PROPERTY assertion (plan.removals must not contain the refused path) -- not at an earlier fixture invariant, which is where the original M4 experiment stopped. The other 11 rows stay green under the same mutation, reproducing the finding on this base. HOW IT REACHES THE STATE: resizeSaveReopen gained an optional afterLoad(act) seam between the real loadAeonProject and the real buildAeonSavePlan, and the row pushes the refused path into act.sectionFiles.loadedPaths there -- the future-loader state in one statement, which M4 could only reach by suspending a fixture invariant with a throwaway edit. Everything else is real: the truncated tiles.bin, the loader's refusal, the 2x2 to 3x2 resize, the plan builder. ANTI-VACUITY: the row also asserts the refused path is NOT in plan.files (understood() refuses to write it), so it is not in the keep set either and the FIRST subtraction demonstrably is not what saves it, and asserts section_3 IS removed in the same save so it cannot pass on an empty removable set. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: nothing reachable produces that state today, so this is evidence about the guard and not about a live data-loss bug; and it is ambiguous between the call-site argument and the refused filter inside removalsFor, going red for either, which is correct because they are one rule. NOT WIDENED: the other two removalsFor call sites (the effects libraries) still have no such row. Runner npm test: Test Files 595 passed | 3 skipped (598), Tests 8875 passed | 9 skipped (8884), zero failed.

title: THE CAUSE IS NO LONGER UNKNOWN -- the id is now false and is kept because ids do not change. The symptom is STILL LIVE on the fixed build.
detail: Measured foreground on master 33ccee18, debug build stamped 2026-09-10T08:13:57Z, harness:cdp-sweep-f4 re-run (it last ran at a49cfd92, BEFORE the fix). 15/17 PASS, 1 FAIL, 1 UNMEASURABLE, 62.6s, load 10.92->6.26. The FAIL is P2d, the row built to be able to refute. CAUSE: the fix arms its re-select at mousedown on `e.button === 0 && !editing`. Seat A focuses Bot with a TAB, so `editing` is already true when the pointer goes down, the arm is never set, the click collapses the Tab's select-all to a caret, and 72 appends to 128. The census is decisive in ONE run: variant A (tab-then-click) is the ONLY one with `focus before click: true` and the ONLY one that INSERTED; B,C,D,E,F,G all arrived unfocused and all REPLACED, which is the fix working in the same frame. Anti-vacuous floor held: P2a reset to the seat's numbers, P2c proved a cold click on the same two boxes REPLACES in this run, P2b read activeElement between the Tab and the click. NOT FIXED HERE: the remedy is a trade between two real gestures and is filed as decisions.jsonl NUMBERFIELD-TAB-THEN-CLICK.

title: Superseded by NUMBERFIELD-INSERT-CAUSE-UNKNOWN and re-measured: this row's ORIGINAL mechanism -- a click on an ALREADY-FOCUSED box -- turns out to be right after all, for the one arrival it named wrongly.
detail: Recorded so the refutation is not left standing as the last word on this id. The row was filed as 'clicking an already-focused box inserts', then REFUTED on 2026-09-09 because four of the five reproducing gestures read activeElement !== box before the click. On the FIXED build those four now REPLACE and only the already-focused one inserts, so the refuted mechanism is what remains -- it was masked by a second, broader defect that the fix has since removed. A finding can age back into correctness; ask whether a row still holds IN THE DIRECTION FILED rather than whether it was once refuted. State stays `open` because the symptom is live; the live row is the successor.

title: A rule whose END CONDITION is a fact about ANOTHER repo's file keeps being obeyed after it lapses, because nothing re-reads the condition. TWO instances found in this boot doc in one grep; both had lapsed on 2026-09-06 and were still being cited on 2026-09-10.
detail: Instance 1: CUT THE CEREMONY clause 2, scoped 'until EFFECTS-W1 ships'. contract/projects.json at empyrean origin/main has read EFFECTS-W1 state=done since 2026-09-06; this lane cited the clause as live tonight, in a refusal, four days after it lapsed. Aeon hit the identical clause the same hour independently (aeon 8caa9dd4) having quoted it as live at every boot since 09-03 -- two lanes, no contact, same dead clause. Instance 2, found by grepping this doc for the SHAPE rather than for the clause: `emulator/reset is off-limits on the hosted build until aeon's F-HOSTED-RESET-SRM closes` was wrong three ways -- the finding is ORACLE's not aeon's (aeon origin/master greps zero), it CLOSED 2026-09-06 on branch fix/hosted-reset-srm, and oracle's own closure says the mitigation this row taught never covered the defect ('NOT hosted-only, the window's own F1/palette reset reaches it through the same door'), so a partial cover was reading as a full one. BOTH FIXED at this commit: each now states the one command that tests its condition instead of asserting a state. FOUND AND NOT FIXED, deliberately: the ENGINE/SERVER split section still opens 'Until `initialize` carries a build identity, the split is the mitigation' while the same section records that parcel CLOSED 2026-08-29 -- a stale rationale, not a false prohibition, it ships no wrong output, and this file's own move-(3) rule makes rewriting live rulings interleaved with narrative the owner's parcel rather than a lane's tidy-up. THE GENERAL FORM: a hold, a lift and a scope are all present-tense claims about somebody else's work; write the test, never the verdict.

title: The in-app guide's §1 panel schematic drew RASTER TIMELINE at the TOP of the Colour sub-tab, which it has not been since 8e3727ad -- and §3 step 1 four screens below it said the opposite in the same rendered page.
detail: A LIVE DEFECT IN WHAT THE APP TELLS A PERSON, not a doc tidy-up: guides.ts imports this file with Vite's ?raw and the Guide tab renders it VERBATIM. providers/effects-sub-tabs.ts declares the Colour column as presets, preset.bands, preset.channels, preset.anchors, TIMELINE LAST, and effects-facet.tsx mounts BandPresetPanel before RasterTimelineStrip to match. WHO BROKE IT, AND IT WAS THE FIX: `git show 8e3727ad -- docs/guides/effects-first-run.md` is a three-line diff. uxa F5 moved the preset panel to the top of the tab, moved the provider's declared order with it, and updated exactly ONE sentence -- step 1, the one the seat had quoted. The picture went stale in the same commit, and the guard added for step 1 (colour-tab-arrival.test.ts) was phrased at step 1's TEXT so it could not see it. THE SHAPE WORTH KEEPING: the landing that fixes a route claim is the landing most likely to falsify its siblings, because it is the only landing that moves the thing they all describe. FIXED in the guide, against the source, never the other way round: no component, control label or mount order was touched. CONTROL: npm run check:guide-text passes on the STALE diagram, exit 0 -- that gate's population is backticked labels, and it says nothing about position, order or arrival state.

title: 45 route claims enumerated in the in-app guide; ONE was false, and exactly ONE (half of one) was held by any test. 26 are now pinned by 31 rows derived from the producers.
detail: A ROUTE CLAIM asserts WHERE a control is, in what ORDER things appear, or what state a section ARRIVES in. scripts/check-guide-text.mjs covers the LABEL class -- does this string exist on screen -- and its own header is explicit about that population. Position, order and arrival state were covered by nothing. THE CENSUS IS THE DELIVERABLE: every claim with its producer, its truth value and what would go red, so the next parcel does not guess a subset. WHAT IS PINNED: the three schematic columns against providers/effects-sub-tabs.ts, the three job buttons' count and order, arrival state per section read off its own <CollapsibleSection> tag, the strip above the buttons, PROPERTIES below all three, SECTION ASSIGNMENT last on Parallax, the Section <n> dropdown last in RASTER BAND PRESETS, the §8 sub-tab column, the drift seed via driftFromToggle, the drift direction via LAYER_DRIFT_ROW.title, a new preset's single band via newPreset, an absent Start at via newAnchorSweep. EVERY EXPECTATION DERIVED FROM THE PRODUCER -- copying an order out of the guide would make the test agree with the thing under test. Mutation B proves it: reordering the PROVIDER with the guide untouched turns the column row red. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: no pixel (no jsdom here), not the facet's mount order (that seam is colour-tab-arrival.test.ts's), not the sticky mechanism (a foreground poison), and 19 enumerated claims are left unheld with reasons in the packet's §5, including the one pixel claim on the page (the LAYERS list's 211px) which is TAGGED FOR THE FOREGROUND.

title: My own loud-on-unmeasurable row was vacuous: it asserted `starts.every(s => s >= 0)` when every offset was >= 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, because the header line had only been accepted for containing all three labels.
detail: SELF-FOUND, in the red-first run. Mutation G renamed the schematic's middle heading Colour -> Colours and ALL 30 ROWS STAYED GREEN. Applied-and-still-green is a defect to diagnose, never a pass. TWO CAUSES. (1) `line.includes(l)` matches a SUPERSTRING, so the header was still found at the same offset and the reader carried on working correctly. (2) THE GUARD ASSERTED ITS OWN SEARCH CONDITION -- the shape of a row that reads as care and discriminates nothing, and it would have gone on passing through a rename that DID break the slicing. FIXED (fac93e2b) by requiring what the column slicing actually rests on: three DISTINCT, INCREASING offsets in the order the bar paints them. Mutation G2 (heading deleted outright) then went red on four rows. THEN THE SECOND LESSON: mutation G re-applied was STILL green, and this time correctly -- with rising distinct offsets the slicing still worked and every order row still measured what it claimed. The real fault was that the picture headed a column with a word no button carries and NO ROW ANYWHERE ASKED THAT; check-guide-text cannot either, since its DIAGRAM rows are the entries and this is the fenced header above them. Closed in 396e2905 with a 31st row deriving each heading from EFFECTS_SUB_TABS. THE RULE: when a mutation stays green, the diagnosis can be 'the row I was testing was RIGHT to pass, and the row that should have caught this does not exist' -- which is a different repair from fixing the guard you were aiming at.

title: The SAME unguarded second subtraction exists at the other two removalsFor call sites -- the effects scenes and the raster presets -- and MEASURED, not inferred: both can be deleted with the whole suite green.
detail: FIXED by two rows in src/core/project/aeon/__tests__/save-removals.test.ts (15 rows -> 17), in one new describe 'the refused subtraction is load-bearing at the effects call sites': (1) 'SCENES: a loader that admitted a refused path to loadedPaths still does not get it deleted' and (2) 'RASTER PRESETS: a loader that admitted a refused path to loadedPaths still does not get it deleted'. THE EXACT MUTATION THAT TURNS EACH RED, applied INDEPENDENTLY (one at a time, so each row is shown to guard its own site): for row 1, replace the third argument of the scene removalsFor call, [...unreadableScenePaths], with [] (1 insertion, 1 deletion); for row 2, replace the third argument of the preset call, [...unreadablePresetPaths], with []. On committed baseline 401b47f4 each mutation gives Tests 1 failed | 16 passed (17) over save-removals.test.ts, the single failure being ITS OWN row at THE PROPERTY assertion (plan.removals must not contain the refused path -- line 312 for scenes, line 335 for presets), reached past both anti-vacuity assertions above it. Under the scene mutation the preset row stayed GREEN and vice versa, which is what proves the rows are site-independent; a single row covering both would have passed the pair while leaving one site naked. HOW THEY REACH THE STATE, AND NO SEAM WAS NEEDED: unlike the section-file site (which needed resizeSaveReopen's afterLoad callback), both libraries hang off `project`, which buildAeonSavePlan takes as an argument, and this test file already calls loadAeonProject and buildAeonSavePlan as separate steps -- five existing rows already mutate r.project.effectsScenes in that gap. Each row asserts the loader really refused a TRUNCATED real document and really kept it out of loadedPaths, then pushes it into loadedPaths: the future-loader state in one statement. save.ts is UNCHANGED and byte-identical to master. ANTI-VACUITY, three per row: the injection reached the plan builder (loadedPaths and unreadable both read back off r.project after the build); the refused path is NOT in plan.files, so it is not in the keep set either and the FIRST subtraction demonstrably is not what saves it; and victim.json / victim_p.json ARE removed in the same save, so neither row can pass on an empty removable set. WHAT THEY DO NOT PROVE: nothing reachable produces that state today, so this is evidence about the guard and not about a live data-loss bug; each row is ambiguous between its call-site argument and the refused filter inside removalsFor, going red for either, which is correct because they are one rule (it is NOT ambiguous between call sites, measured); and they judge the PLAN, not an unlink -- the on-disk claim belongs to npm run harness:deleted-scene-returns. ALL THREE removalsFor call sites in save.ts now have a row that reddens on their own second subtraction; there is no fourth. Runner npm test: Test Files 595 passed | 3 skipped (598), Tests 8877 passed | 9 skipped (8886), zero failed, load 25.85 at launch.

title: LEAD, NOT A FINDING: the scene site's write-side throw has a row against buildAeonSavePlan; the preset half may have none. Established by GREP, never by deletion.
detail: Raised by the agent that built the two subtraction guards and carried here rather than left in a transcript, with its own hedge intact. The scene site's write-side throw is covered at aeon-effects-scenes.test.ts:287; for the raster-preset half the agent found only agent-handler-level `rejects.toThrow` rows, nothing against buildAeonSavePlan itself. IT WAS NOT ESTABLISHED BY DELETING THE THROW, which is the only thing that would settle it -- the whole lesson of the row this parcel closed is that a guard resting on a neighbour looks identical to a guarded one until you delete it. So this is a lead: cheap to settle (delete the throw, run the suite, see whether anything reddens), and NOT to be quoted as a gap until someone does. Deliberately out of that parcel's scope, correctly.

title: S2 and S3 were UNMEASURABLE because nothing could dirty a LEVEL document from outside the app. A debug door now can, and it commits through classicSetLayoutCells rather than setting a flag.
detail: The 2026-09-10 CDP sweep parked S2 (does Ctrl+S flash Saved!) and S3 (does a classic save's toast name the files) as UNMEASURABLE after four routes failed, every one a limit of the harness's reach. renderer/debug-level-edit.ts stamps one chunk-id cell into the fg layout through classicSetLayoutCells, EXACTLY the function ClassicLevelViewport's endStroke ends a real stamp gesture in: same argument shape, one undo entry, the real dirty domain (fg, which s1-io.ts:549 routes to paths.fg), the real file on the next save. IT DOES NOT SET A DIRTY FLAG, and the whole value of the parcel is in that refusal: a door that flipped `dirty` would make S2 vacuous, proving the chip reacts to a flag rather than that an EDIT reaches the chip. THE ROW THAT REFUSES THE DEGRADATION is the undo row -- a raw setState records no history, so 'exactly ONE undo step, and undoing restores the byte AND clears the domain' cannot pass unless commitLayout ran. 20 rows in src/renderer/__tests__/debug-level-edit.test.ts, seven mutations applied on disk and each red on exactly the intended rows (M1, the degradation itself, reddens the undo row plus three of the four source guards; the doc-byte and dirty rows stay GREEN under it, which is precisely why they are not the guard). WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: the pointer gesture INTO that call is still unexercised; arming the classic paint tool from outside remains a door no instrument here has.

title: The sweep's S2a predicate read `__dbg.aeon.state().dirty` on a CLASSIC act, and its comment called that 'the editor store's LEVEL flag'. It is the AEON flag; a classic act's dirtiness is a different field, so the predicate could not have gone true even with a working stroke.
detail: FOUND WHILE GROUNDING THE DOOR, not by running anything. useEditorStore.dirty is written by markDirty, which keys on useProjectStore's currentZoneId/currentActId -- the AEON project's act. A classic act's dirtiness lives in useClassicLevelStore.dirty, and shell/dirty-snapshot.ts reads the two as SEPARATE fields, classicDirty and aeonDirty, both of which SaveChip's tabHasDirtyDot consumes. So the sweep's S2a had two independent reasons to stay false on its classic subject: the stroke painted nothing AND the flag it watched belongs to the other engine. This does not change the sweep's UNMEASURABLE verdict, which was and remains correct and correctly worded -- it changes what a reader should conclude about the four-route table, because the fourth route's stated symptom (`tool` stuck at `view`) was not the only thing standing between it and a green. The comment is CORRECTED IN PLACE rather than deleted, the flag is still read and printed so a reader watches it stay false, and the row now predicates on the classic store's own byte and on the app's own chip tooltip.

title: MASTER IS RED AND NEITHER SIDE HAS A DEFECT: aeon made demo's SCANLINE_CAPS a DERIVED binding, our reader only parses literals, and the row reports the producer's ABSENCE when the truth is our own blindness.
detail: DIAGNOSED FOREGROUND 2026-09-10. Timeline, from ../aeon's reflog rather than from commit dates (they differ and only the reflog says when it reached THIS machine): aeon committed the derived form at 07:42Z/07:54Z, and it landed on this clone's origin/master by PUSH at 08:54:40Z and 08:55:13Z. title: CLOSED: scanlineCaps now answers in FOUR outcomes, so an absence and a blindness can never share a message again.
detail: FIXED on parcel/caps-reader-derived, base master 7e8a3553. scanlineCaps() returned `number | null` over one literal regex, so aeon's DERIVED binding read as null and the row printed `games/demo/config/game.emp declares no SCANLINE_CAPS` -- FALSE. It now returns four outcomes: `literal` (a hand-written mask, games/sonic4 `$0FDE`), `proved` (a derived binding provable FROM SOURCE, with the proof NAMED in the value's provenance string), `unreadable` (NOT a value and NOT null; the message names OUR limit and what to do, and is pinned to contain 'limit of THIS READER' and NOT to contain the absence sentence), and `absent` (no binding line at all -- the ONLY one of the four that is a claim about aeon). THE REMEDY IS AEON'S, at 25d88e38: follow a name to `fold_caps(<registry>)` whose registry is DECLARED `[Scene; 0]` and read 0 off the OR-fold's identity, refusing every other shape loudly. ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE: aeon's caps_from_manifest decides absence by failing a literal regex then a name regex, so an unparsed VALUE SHAPE (`= $0FDE // note`, an expression) reports 'no binding' -- the same conflation. Here the BINDING is found first, anchored on its own line, and only then is the RHS classified, so absence is structural. WHICH STATE AEON IS IN, ESTABLISHED BY READING, NOT ASSUMED: demo is state 2 (PROVED) -- `DEMO_SCENES: [Scene; 0]`, `DemoScenes_CapsFolded = fold_caps(DEMO_SCENES)`, `SCANLINE_CAPS = DemoScenes_CapsFolded`; sonic4 is state 1 (LITERAL `$0FDE`). Read at aeon 1e6946fb and RE-READ at 332edb5e after origin/master moved MID-SESSION -- identical. So state 3 is NOT REACHABLE today: it is defensive, the rows stay ASSERTING, and no skip was added (suite skip count unchanged at 9). THE JUDGEMENT CALL: `unreadable` FAILS, it does not skip. This repo skips for an ENVIRONMENT it does not control (no aeon checkout); `unreadable` is not that -- aeon's source is present and the missing evaluator is OURS, actionable here. And `unreadable` is CORRELATED with the change it would hide: the only route to it is DEMO_SCENES gaining a scene, exactly the event that could raise demo's caps and falsify the panel's clause. Skipping there is green-because-blind at the moment the answer most likely moved. THE ROW WAS ALSO SPLIT IN TWO (sonic4 half / demo half): as one `it` the demo failure took sonic4's conjunct down with it and that run never evaluated sonic4 at all. M1 measures the split -- under a mutation blinding the demo half, the sonic4 half stays GREEN and evaluated. TIP STAYS `origin/master`, deliberately: pinning it would make a live drift detector a fossil. It moved 1e6946fb->332edb5e during this session, which is the detector working. RED-FIRST, four mutations each quoted from disk and restored from committed baseline: M1 proof path removed (2 failed/5 passed; sonic4 half PASSED); M2 guess zero for ANY registry length, the degradation aeon refused (1 failed); M3 absence folded back into blindness, this parcel's own thesis re-planted (1 failed); M4 every literal reads as zero, which reddens the SONIC4 half and proves it still asserts what it did (2 failed). All four reddened; none went green-and-applied. npm test GREEN at tip: 596 passed | 3 skipped (599) files, 8910 passed | 9 skipped (8919) tests, NPM_TEST_EXIT=0, 33.58s, 1-min load 5.53->21.55 on 16 cores. NOT PROVEN: this reads aeon's SOURCE, never a ROM; the fold is proven by DECLARED type and the OR-fold identity, not evaluated, so a sigil change from OR would make the proof quietly wrong (which is why the proof is NAMED in the message); state 3 has only ever been exercised on synthetic manifests. title: FOUR rows disappear entirely when CLASSIC_DIR is unset, and the run reports 13/14 PASS - 1 UNMEASURABLE, so a reader concludes every question was asked. Only S3 emits an UNMEASURABLE; S2a1/S2a2/S2a3/S2b emit NOTHING.
detail: Found by the overseer RUNNING it, not by reading it -- the first foreground run of the door parcel. S2a1..S2b sit inside the `else` branch of the `if (!CLASSICDIR || !existsSync(CLASSICDIR))` gate at ~:484, while the gate's own arm emits a single UNMEASURABLE for S3 alone. So with CLASSIC_DIR unset the totals line reads 13/14 PASS - 0 FAIL - 1 UNMEASURABLE and FOUR rows are simply absent from it. Both logs are captured side by side in the capture directory so the difference is readable: 14 rows without CLASSIC_DIR, 20 with. THE SHAPE: an absence dressed as an outcome, which is the same defect as reading a missing result file as a verdict -- and it is WORSE than a silent skip because the totals line is arithmetically honest about the rows it printed and says nothing about the rows it did not. A harness that is loud on unmeasurable for one row and silent for its four siblings, under the SAME gate, teaches a reader that the gate was handled. REMEDY: the gate's refusing arm emits an UNMEASURABLE for every row it suppresses, named, so the totals move from 14 to 18 and the reader sees four questions unasked. Not fixed tonight -- the verdicts it was blocking are now taken (20/20 with CLASSIC_DIR set) so this is instrument work, not a blocker.

title: The failure MODE of the load-dependent suite flake is now MEASURED: `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`, on three rows that shell out to a subprocess. The prior packet could only guess it.
detail: docs/reviews/2026-09-10-effects-subtraction-guards.md recorded a one-row `npm test` flake in test/config/prose-constant-fold.test.ts and said explicitly that it did NOT capture the failure text, so it could not say the mode was a timeout rather than an assertion. This run captured it. At load average 14.80 a full `npx vitest run` came back Test Files 3 failed | 595 passed | 3 skipped (601), Tests 4 failed | 8928 passed | 9 skipped (8941), duration 34.84s. One failure was the deliberate mutation under test. The other THREE were all `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.`: prose-constant-fold.test.ts:181 (5246ms), prose-constant-fold.test.ts:194 (6498ms) and src/renderer/components/art/__tests__/art-discard-guard.test.ts:518 (5273ms). So the mode is a TIMEOUT and the population is wider than one file. vitest.config.ts sets no `testTimeout`, so these rows run on vitest's default while shelling out to a node subprocess that walks the repo, in parallel with the rest of the suite. The same tree at load 5.08 to 5.80 ran green three separate times in this parcel (8930 and 8931 passed, zero failed). CONSEQUENCE, and why this is worth a row rather than a shrug: these are GATES. A gate that goes red on a busy box teaches readers to re-run rather than to read, and every `npm test` green in a review packet is silently a claim about the box's load at that moment. THE ASK: an explicit `testTimeout` for the subprocess rows, sized off a measurement of how long the gate subprocess actually takes on a loaded box, not off the largest figure observed here.

title: FRAMING CORRECTED, FINDING UNCHANGED. I called this 'a load-shaped false red, not a defect' and that sentence was WRONG and was relayed to three lanes before sigil refused it.
detail: THE ERROR WAS MINE AND IT WAS ALREADY IN MY OWN BANK. Load explains WHEN a red fires, never WHETHER the thing it fired on is real. A failure appearing only under load is a NARROW-WINDOW DEFECT, and load OPENS narrow windows rather than faking them; the green re-run is a CHECK, never a verdict. Calling it a false red pre-decided the question the re-run was supposed to ask, and it did so in a sentence handed to peers as a machine fact. Sigil refused to bank it and was right; the hub had already relayed my wording onward. WHAT ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATES, aeon's addition after hitting a high-load red that turned out to be a contaminated control: the FAILURE TEXT, not the machine's business. Here the text is measured, not inferred -- 'Error: Test timed out in 5000ms' at prose-constant-fold.test.ts:181 (5246ms), :194 (6498ms) and art-discard-guard.test.ts:518 (5273ms), all in one load-14.80 run, with the same tree green three times at load 5.08-5.80. So the mode qualifies, and the DEFECT is a missing explicit testTimeout sized off real subprocess work rather than left at vitest's 5000ms default; load merely opened the window on it. ORACLE'S STRONGER FORM, adopted: CHECK THE DIRECTION before accepting a borrowed mode -- their own row failed 1 in 31 runs at the LOW end of a load population whose high end was clean, the opposite sign from this one. A borrowed explanation that does not match the sign of your data is not evidence. STILL NOT MEASURED HERE: which of the two files introduced the exposure, and no controlled-load repro; reproduced once, mode identified, no bisect.

HISTORY: git log -S and -L give one commit, 25efe5c0, subject only; its comment says the effect only fires on an actual act/zone switch and never mentions the mount-time run, so that run was accidental. LOAD-BEARING: marquee, pasting and mapClipboard live in editorStore and outlive the map, so the mount run was the only thing catching an act, zone or project change made while the map was unmounted. PASTE: the facet bar never brings a paste back either way, because switchFacet calls setTool (facet-tools.ts:82) which disarms it; no shipped remount path keeps act, project and tool, so the bare-remount row pins the component property. detail: The overseer's entry asked the right question first: a red that shows only under load can be a narrow window that load OPENS, so is this one? Answered by measurement before any change. WHAT THEY WAIT ON: the gate and its fold contain no await, timer, poll, watcher or promise (grep zero, live control 10 in facet-modules); the art rows are synchronous (zero in lines 460-650, control 24 in the same file's section C); the facet row awaits only module loading (no top-level await under src/, 0 files against a 438-file control; no import-time registration, 0 against 804). THREE MEASUREMENTS SAY WORK: (1) one tight mode per condition, stretching smoothly: idle load 7.9-8.5 exits-row 540-554ms, coverage row 1090-1147, facet 610-653, art 916-1032; 16 busy loops load 26-55 coverage row 5700 and 5355 (both past 5000, reproducing the red), others 1803-4170; full suite load 15-20 facet 3026-3045, coverage 2430-2986. (3) synchronous code cannot wait. detail: Branch parcel/collision-paste-across-tilesets, base 165dde4f; 31cfba9f reproduction rows (red on base), 2f75042e the rule and its rows, c83c76e8 the art-only erase fix, fb542e56 packet. WHAT A COLLISION WORD INDEXES: bits 0-9 a shape number, bits 10-11 flips, 12-13 solidity, 14-15 the loop crossover mark (collision-cell-word.ts:6-10); only the shape number indexes a table. Aurora loads ONE CollisionProfileSet per project open, first candidate dir wins (aeon/load.ts:208-210), written only by openLoaded (projectStore.ts:82). aeon at b3db547e: bake_plane_cell reads "9:0 base-bank shape index" (collision_pipeline.py:279, :328), load_base_bank reads one path games/sonic4/data/collision/base (ojz_strip_gen.py:1630, :1634) into "ONE shared set across all sections" (:1898), and the runtime tables are embedded once, "shared across all zones" (collision_data.emp:1, :18-22, :221, :224), probed with no zone pointer (player_sensors.emp:250-259). VERDICT: MIXED by scope, zone-independent and project-dependent. RULE (map-clipboard.ts): tile words fit only the tile set they were copied from; collision words fit the project they were copied in, read by reference as "the clipboard's tile set is one of the open project's zones'" (a Tileset is built once per zone per load; the same load identity editorStore.ts:979 keys on), so no new field. pasteRefusal picks its sentence by which written words would be wrong: tiles only is the landed OTHER_TILESET_REFUSAL, collision only is the new OTHER_PROJECT_COLLISION_REFUSAL (no word about tiles), both is OTHER_PROJECT_REFUSAL. armRefusal refuses Ctrl+V only where no click could land anything. SITES: map Ctrl+V into another zone of the same project now arms with an info notice (COLLISION_ONLY_HERE); a Shift click or the sticky Collision setting lands the collision and no tile word; a click that would write tiles is refused at the click and paste mode is left; the ghost rasterises no art over a foreign tile set; another project is refused at Ctrl+V and at the click. The composer's Ctrl+V pastes from any zone of the project and refuses another project's collision with the collision sentence, key claimed, nothing written. REPRODUCTION, red on base by ASSERTION: map Shift paste across zones (Ctrl+V refused), the same by the sticky setting, a collision-only click into another project refused with the TILES sentence, and the composer overwriting another project's collision. ROWS: 13 new (4 mounted map incl. a ghost row that counts rasterised canvases on the block's document stub, 4 mounted composer on a NEW mounted ComposerCanvas harness, map-clipboard 7d-1..4, one writer row); 4 landed PASTE-ACROSS-TILESETS rows rewritten because the verdict changes what they pin (one premise had gone vacuous: it matched a fragment the new notice also contains). PLANTS P1..P13 by a scratch script outside the repo, each shown on disk, restored from the committed tip and clean against HEAD; every new or rewritten row is reddened by at least one, all ASSERTION, TIMEOUT 0 (the composer same-zone CONTROL is a control). The writer now returns false for an art-only region and the handler refuses out loud. TRADES, for the overseer: the composer now refuses a cross-project paste even between two checkouts whose banks are identical (options: keep, built; a content check of the bank, which cannot vouch when the profiles are null; path identity, which trusts a bank aeon may have rewritten); a refused click still leaves paste mode (staying armed is one line, not built); the Paste layers panel does not grey out Both and Art in another zone (not built). CLASSIC: not served, ComposerCanvas is imported only by the aeon art facet (art-facet.tsx:26, registered for aeon at register-facets.ts:17-19), and classic's tileClipboard holds 64 palette indices (classicLevelStore.ts:276).
